1.52.s:
sanandana uvāca
atha vyākaraṇaṃ vakṣye saṃkṣepāttava nārada /
siddharūpaprabandhena mukhaṃ vedasya sāṃpratam //
1.52.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
अथ व्याकरणं वक्ष्ये संक्षेपात्तव नारद ।
सिद्धरूपप्रबन्धेन मुखं वेदस्य सांप्रतम् ॥
1.52.m:
Sanandana said:
Now I will speak to you briefly of grammar, O Nārada,
as a presentation of standard forms, the mouth of the Veda today.

1.52.s:
suptiṅaṃtaṃ padaṃ vipra supāṃ sapta vibhaktayaḥ /
svaujasaḥ prathamā proktā sā prātipadikātmikā //
1.52.d:
सुप्तिङंतं पदं विप्र सुपां सप्त विभक्तयः ।
स्वौजसः प्रथमा प्रोक्ता सा प्रातिपदिकात्मिका ॥
1.52.m:
A word ends in sup or tiṅ, O vipra; of the sup affixes there are seven case-endings.
su-au-jas is called the first; its nature is the nominal stem,

1.52.s:
saṃbodhane ca liṅgādāvukte karmaṇi kartari /
arthāvatprātipadikaṃ dhātupratyayavārjitam //
1.52.d:
संबोधने च लिङ्गादावुक्ते कर्मणि कर्तरि ।
अर्थावत्प्रातिपदिकं धातुप्रत्ययवार्जितम् ॥
1.52.m:
and it occurs in the vocative, in [denoting] gender, and so on, when the object or agent is already expressed.
A nominal stem is meaningful, excluding verbal roots and affixes.

1.52.s:
amausaśo dvitīyā syāttatkarma kriyate ca yat /
dvitīyā karmaṇi proktāntarāntareṇa saṃyute //
1.52.d:
अमौसशो द्वितीया स्यात्तत्कर्म क्रियते च यत् ।
द्वितीया कर्मणि प्रोक्तान्तरान्तरेण संयुते ॥
1.52.m:
am-auṭ-śas is the second; that is the object, and what is done.
The second is declared to denote the object, and in connection with antarā and antareṇa.

1.52.s:
ṭābhyāṃbhisastṛtīyā syātkaraṇe kartarīritā /
yena kriyate tatkaraṇaṃ saḥ kartā syātkaroti yaḥ //
1.52.d:
टाभ्यांभिसस्तृतीया स्यात्करणे कर्तरीरिता ।
येन क्रियते तत्करणं सः कर्ता स्यात्करोति यः ॥
1.52.m:
ṭā-bhyām-bhis is the third, said to denote the instrument and the agent;
that by which an act is done is the instrument, and he who does it is the agent.

1.52.s:
ṅebhyāṃbhyasaścaturtho syātsaṃ pradāne ca kārake /
yasmai ditsā dhārayedvai rocate saṃpradānakam //
1.52.d:
ङेभ्यांभ्यसश्चतुर्थो स्यात्सं प्रदाने च कारके ।
यस्मै दित्सा धारयेद्वै रोचते संप्रदानकम् ॥
1.52.m:
ṅe-bhyām-bhyas is the fourth, in the case of the recipient kāraka:
to whom one wishes to give, [to whom one] owes, or who is pleased, is the recipient.

1.52.s:
pañcamī syānṅasibhyāṃbhyo hyapādāne ca kārake /
yato 'paiti samādatte apadatte ca yaṃ yataḥ //
1.52.d:
पञ्चमी स्यान्ङसिभ्यांभ्यो ह्यपादाने च कारके ।
यतो ऽपैति समादत्ते अपदत्ते च यं यतः ॥
1.52.m:
The fifth is ṅasi-bhyām-bhyas, in the case of the point of departure kāraka:
from which [one] departs, or takes, and from what [one protects] whom.

1.52.s:
ṅasosāmaśca ṣaṣṭhī syātsvāmisaṃbandhamukhyake /
ṅyoḥsupaḥ saptamī tu syātsā cādhikaraṇe bhavet //
1.52.d:
ङसोसामश्च षष्ठी स्यात्स्वामिसंबन्धमुख्यके ।
ङ्योःसुपः सप्तमी तु स्यात्सा चाधिकरणे भवेत् ॥
1.52.m:
ṅas-os-ām is the sixth, primarily denoting the master and relation.
ṅi-os-sup is the seventh, and it occurs to denote the locus,

1.52.s:
ādhāre cāpi viprendra rakṣārthānāṃ prayogataḥ /
īpsitaṃ cānīpsitaṃ yattadapādānakaṃ smṛtam //
1.52.d:
आधारे चापि विप्रेन्द्र रक्षार्थानां प्रयोगतः ।
ईप्सितं चानीप्सितं यत्तदपादानकं स्मृतम् ॥
1.52.m:
as well as the substratum, O best of vipras; by the use of [verbs] meaning protection,
that which is desired or undesired is known as the point of departure.

1.52.s:
pañcamī paryaṇaṅyoge itararte 'nyadiṅmukhe /
etairyoge dvitīyā syātkarmapravacanīyakaiḥ //
1.52.d:
पञ्चमी पर्यणङ्योगे इतरर्ते ऽन्यदिङ्मुखे ।
एतैर्योगे द्वितीया स्यात्कर्मप्रवचनीयकैः ॥
1.52.m:
The fifth occurs in connection with pari, apa, and āṅ, and with itara, ṛte, and anya in the sense of direction.
In connection with these karmapravacanīyas the second occurs:

1.52.s:
lakṣaṇetthaṃbhūto 'bhirabhāge cānupariprati /
antareṣu sahārthe ca hīne hyupaśca kathyate //
1.52.d:
लक्षणेत्थंभूतो ऽभिरभागे चानुपरिप्रति ।
अन्तरेषु सहार्थे च हीने ह्युपश्च कथ्यते ॥
1.52.m:
abhi in the sense of a sign or state, and anu, pari, and prati when not denoting a share;
upa is declared in the sense of between, together with, and inferior.

1.52.s:
dvitīyā ca caturthī syāñceṣṭāyāṃ gatikarmaṇi /
aprāṇiṣu vibhaktī dve manyakarmaṇyanādare //
1.52.d:
द्वितीया च चतुर्थी स्याञ्चेष्टायां गतिकर्मणि ।
अप्राणिषु विभक्ती द्वे मन्यकर्मण्यनादरे ॥
1.52.m:
The second and the fourth occur to denote the object of motion involving bodily action,
and the two case-endings [occur] with inanimate objects as the object of manya in contempt.

1.52.s:
namaḥsvastisvadhāsvāhālaṃvaṣaḍyoga īritā /
caturthī caiva tādarthye tumarthādbhāvavācinaḥ //
1.52.d:
नमःस्वस्तिस्वधास्वाहालंवषड्योग ईरिता ।
चतुर्थी चैव तादर्थ्ये तुमर्थाद्भाववाचिनः ॥
1.52.m:
The fourth is declared in connection with namaḥ, svasti, svadhā, svāhā, alam, and vaṣaṭ,
and also in the sense of purpose, from a verbal noun in the sense of the infinitive.

1.52.s:
tṛtīyā sahayoge syātkutsiteṃ'ge viśeṣaṇe /
kāle bhāve saptamī syādetairyoge ca ṣaṣṭhyapi //
1.52.d:
तृतीया सहयोगे स्यात्कुत्सितेंऽगे विशेषणे ।
काले भावे सप्तमी स्यादेतैर्योगे च षष्ठ्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
The third occurs in connection with saha, with a deformed limb, and with a characteristic mark.
The seventh occurs in time and condition, and the sixth also in connection with these,

1.52.s:
svāmīśvarodhipatibhiḥ sākṣidāyādasūtakaiḥ /
nirdhāraṇe dve vibhaktī ṣaṣṭī hetuprayogake //
1.52.d:
स्वामीश्वरोधिपतिभिः साक्षिदायादसूतकैः ।
निर्धारणे द्वे विभक्ती षष्टी हेतुप्रयोगके ॥
1.52.m:
with the words svāmin, īśvara, adhipati, sākṣin, dāyāda, and prasūta.
In selection there are two case-endings; the sixth is used with hetu,

1.52.s:
smṛtyarthakarmaṇi tathā karoteḥ pratiyatnake /
hiṃsārthānāṃ prayoge ca kṛtikarmaṇi kartari //
1.52.d:
स्मृत्यर्थकर्मणि तथा करोतेः प्रतियत्नके ।
हिंसार्थानां प्रयोगे च कृतिकर्मणि कर्तरि ॥
1.52.m:
likewise with the object of [verbs] meaning remembrance, with the effort of kṛ,
in the use of [verbs] meaning violence, and in the agent and object of a kṛt-affix.

1.52.s:
/
na kartṛkarmaṇoḥ ṣaṣṭī niṣṭādipratipādikā /
etā vai dvividhā jñeyāḥ subādiṣu vibhaktiṣu /
bhūvādiṣu tiṅateṣu lakārā daśa vai smṛtāḥ //
1.52.d:
।
न कर्तृकर्मणोः षष्टी निष्टादिप्रतिपादिका ।
एता वै द्विविधा ज्ञेयाः सुबादिषु विभक्तिषु ।
भूवादिषु तिङतेषु लकारा दश वै स्मृताः ॥
1.52.m:
The sixth does not express the agent or object with niṣṭhā and other [affixes].
These are to be known as twofold among the sup and other case-endings.
Ten lakāras are recorded for tiṅ-endings after roots beginning with bhū:

1.52.s:
tipta saṃtīti prathamo madhyamaḥ sipthasthottamaḥ /
mivvasmasaḥ parasmai tu pādānāṃ cā mapanedam //
1.52.d:
तिप्त संतीति प्रथमो मध्यमः सिप्थस्थोत्तमः ।
मिव्वस्मसः परस्मै तु पादानां चा मपनेदम् ॥
1.52.m:
tip, tas, jhi is the third person; sip, thas, tha is the second person; the first person
is mip, vas, mas, of the parasmaipada [endings]; and now of the ātmanepada:

1.52.s:
ta āteṃ'te prathamo madhvaḥ se āthe dhve tathottamaḥ /
e vahe maha ādeśā jñeyā hyanye liṅādiṣu //
1.52.d:
त आतेंऽते प्रथमो मध्वः से आथे ध्वे तथोत्तमः ।
ए वहे मह आदेशा ज्ञेया ह्यन्ये लिङादिषु ॥
1.52.m:
ta, ātām, jha is the third person; the middle is thās, āthām, dhvam; likewise the first
is iṭ, vahi, mahiṅ; and other substitutes should be known in the liṅ, etc.

1.52.s:
nāmni prayujyamāne tu prathamaḥ puruṣo bhavet /
madhyamo yuṣmadi prokta uttamaḥ puruṣo 'smadi //
1.52.d:
नाम्नि प्रयुज्यमाने तु प्रथमः पुरुषो भवेत् ।
मध्यमो युष्मदि प्रोक्त उत्तमः पुरुषो ऽस्मदि ॥
1.52.m:
When a noun is used, the third person occurs;
the second person is stated when yuṣmad [is used], and the first person when asmad [is used].

1.52.s:
bhūvādyā dhātavaḥ proktāḥ sanādyantāstathā tataḥ /
laḍīrito vartamāne bhūte 'nadyatane tathā //
1.52.d:
भूवाद्या धातवः प्रोक्ताः सनाद्यन्तास्तथा ततः ।
लडीरितो वर्तमाने भूते ऽनद्यतने तथा ॥
1.52.m:
Roots are stated as beginning with bhū and ending with san, etc. Then,
laṭ is declared in the present; and likewise in the non-recent past,

1.52.s:
māsmayoge ca laṅ vācyo loḍāśiṣi ca dhātutaḥ /
vidhyādau syādāśiṣi ca liṅito dvividho mune //
1.52.d:
मास्मयोगे च लङ् वाच्यो लोडाशिषि च धातुतः ।
विध्यादौ स्यादाशिषि च लिङितो द्विविधो मुने ॥
1.52.m:
in connection with mā and sma, laṅ is to be stated, and loṭ after a root in benediction;
liṅ is of two kinds, O sage, in injunction, etc., and in benediction.

1.52.s:
liḍatīte parokṣe syāt śvastane luṅ bhaviṣyati /
syādanadyatane ḷṭū ca bhaviṣyati tu dhātutaḥ //
1.52.d:
लिडतीते परोक्षे स्यात् श्वस्तने लुङ् भविष्यति ।
स्यादनद्यतने ऌटू च भविष्यति तु धातुतः ॥
1.52.m:
liṭ occurs in the past beyond perception; in the tomorrow-future, luṭ occurs;
and in the non-recent future, lṛṭ occurs after a root.

1.52.s:
bhūte luṅ tipasyapau ca kriyāyāṃ ḷṅ prakīrtitaḥ /
siddhodāharaṇaṃ viddhi saṃhitādipuraḥ saram //
1.52.d:
भूते लुङ् तिपस्यपौ च क्रियायां ऌङ् प्रकीर्तितः ।
सिद्धोदाहरणं विद्धि संहितादिपुरः सरम् ॥
1.52.m:
luṅ is in the past, and tip and syap, and lṛṅ is proclaimed in [conditional] action.
Know the illustrative examples, beginning with euphony, etc.:

1.52.s:
/
daṇḍāgraṃ ca dadhīdaṃ ca madhūdakaṃ pitrarṣabhaḥ /
hotṝkārastathā seyaṃ lāṅgalīṣā manīṣayā //
1.52.d:
।
दण्डाग्रं च दधीदं च मधूदकं पित्रर्षभः ।
होतॄकारस्तथा सेयं लाङ्गलीषा मनीषया ॥
1.52.m:
daṇḍāgram, dadhīdam, madhūdakam, pitrarṣabhaḥ,
hotṝkāraḥ, and likewise seyam, lāṅgalīṣā, manīṣayā,

1.52.s:
gaṅgodakaṃ tavalkāra ṛṇārṇaṃ ca munīśvara //ṭha
śītārtaśca muniśreṣṭha seṃdraḥ saukāra ityapi //
1.52.d:
गङ्गोदकं तवल्कार ऋणार्णं च मुनीश्वर ॥ठ
शीतार्तश्च मुनिश्रेष्ठ सेंद्रः सौकार इत्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
gaṅgodakam, tavalkāraḥ, and ṛṇārṇam, O lord of sages,
and śītārtaḥ, O best of sages, sendraḥ, and saukāraḥ,

1.52.s:
vadhvāsanaṃ pitrartho nāyako lavaṇastathā /
ta ādyā viṣṇave hyatra tasmā argho gurā adhaḥ //
1.52.d:
वध्वासनं पित्रर्थो नायको लवणस्तथा ।
त आद्या विष्णवे ह्यत्र तस्मा अर्घो गुरा अधः ॥
1.52.m:
vadhvāsanam, pitrarthaḥ, nāyakaḥ, likewise lavaṇaḥ;
ta ādyāḥ, viṣṇave here, tasmā arghaḥ, gurā adhaḥ,

1.52.s:
hare 'va viṣṇo 'vetyeṣādasomādapyamī adhāḥ /
śaurī etau viṣṇu imau durge amū no arjunaḥ //
1.52.d:
हरे ऽव विष्णो ऽवेत्येषादसोमादप्यमी अधाः ।
शौरी एतौ विष्णु इमौ दुर्गे अमू नो अर्जुनः ॥
1.52.m:
hare 'va, viṣṇo 'va; after these, asomāt, and also amī adhāḥ,
śaurī etau, viṣṇū imau, durge amū, no arjunaḥ.

1.52.s:
ā evaṃ ca prakṛtyaite tiṣṭanti munisattama /
ṣaḍatra ṣaṇmātaraśca vākchuro vāgdhasrithā //
1.52.d:
आ एवं च प्रकृत्यैते तिष्टन्ति मुनिसत्तम ।
षडत्र षण्मातरश्च वाक्छुरो वाग्धस्रिथा ॥
1.52.m:
These remain unchanged in original form, O best of sages:
ṣaḍ atra, ṣaṇ mātaraḥ, vākśūraḥ, vāg dhasrithā,

1.52.s:
hariḥśete vibhuścintyastaccheṣo yañcarastanthā /
praśnastvatha hariḥṣaṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇaṣṭīkata ityapi //
1.52.d:
हरिःशेते विभुश्चिन्त्यस्तच्छेषो यञ्चरस्तन्था ।
प्रश्नस्त्वथ हरिःषष्ठः कृष्णष्टीकत इत्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
hariḥ śete, vibhuś cintyaḥ, taccheṣaḥ, yañ caraḥ, and likewise
praśnaḥ, then hariḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ, kṛṣṇaṣ ṭīkate, and also

1.52.s:
bhavānṣaṣṭhaśca ṣaṭ santaḥ ṣaṭte tallepa eva ca /
cakriṃśchindhi bhavāñchaurirbhavāñśaurirityapi //
1.52.d:
भवान्षष्ठश्च षट् सन्तः षट्ते तल्लेप एव च ।
चक्रिंश्छिन्धि भवाञ्छौरिर्भवाञ्शौरिरित्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
bhavāñ ṣaṣṭhaḥ, ṣaṭ santaḥ, ṣaṭ te, and tal-lepaḥ,
cakriñś chindhi, bhavāñ śauriḥ, bhavāñś śauriḥ,

1.52.s:
samyaṅṅanantoṅgacchāyā kṛṣṇaṃ vande munīśvara /
tejāṃsi maṃsyate gaṅgā hariśchettā maraḥśivaḥ //
1.52.d:
सम्यङ्ङनन्तोङ्गच्छाया कृष्णं वन्दे मुनीश्वर ।
तेजांसि मंस्यते गङ्गा हरिश्छेत्ता मरःशिवः ॥
1.52.m:
samyaṅṅ anantaḥ, aṅgacchāyā, kṛṣṇaṃ vande, O lord of sages;
tejāṃsi, maṃsyate, gaṅgā, hariś chettā, maraḥ śivaḥ,

1.52.s:
rāma kāmyaḥ kṛpa pūjyo hariḥ pūjyor'cya eva hi /
romo dṛṣṭo 'balā atra suptā iṣṭā imā yataḥ //
1.52.d:
राम काम्यः कृप पूज्यो हरिः पूज्योर्ऽच्य एव हि ।
रोमो दृष्टो ऽबला अत्र सुप्ता इष्टा इमा यतः ॥
1.52.m:
rāma kāmyaḥ, kṛpa pūjyaḥ, hariḥ pūjyaḥ, arcya eva hi,
romo dṛṣṭaḥ, abalā atra suptāḥ, iṣṭā imāḥ, yataḥ,

1.52.s:
viṣṇurnabhyo ravirayaṃ gī )( phalaṃ prātaracyutaḥ /
bhaktairvadyo 'pyantarātmā bho bho eṣa haristathā /
eṣa śārṅgī saiṣa rāmaḥ saṃhitaivaṃ prakīrtitā //
1.52.d:
विष्णुर्नभ्यो रविरयं गी )( फलं प्रातरच्युतः ।
भक्तैर्वद्यो ऽप्यन्तरात्मा भो भो एष हरिस्तथा ।
एष शार्ङ्गी सैष रामः संहितैवं प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.52.m:
viṣṇur nabhyaḥ, ravir ayam, gīḥ phalam, prātar acyutaḥ,
bhaktair vadyaḥ, antarātmā, bho bho eṣa hariḥ, and likewise
eṣa śārṅgī, saiṣa rāmaḥ—thus has euphony been proclaimed.

1.52.s:
rāmeṇābhihitaṃ karomi satataṃ rāmaṃ bhaje sāḍharam /
rāmeṇāpahṛtaṃ samastaduritaṃ rāmāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ /
rāmānmuktimabhīpsitā mama sadā rāmasya dāso 'smyaham /
rāme rañjat me manaḥ suviśadaṃ he rāma tubhyaṃ namaḥ //
1.52.d:
रामेणाभिहितं करोमि सततं रामं भजे साढरम् ।
रामेणापहृतं समस्तदुरितं रामाय तुभ्यं नमः ।
रामान्मुक्तिमभीप्सिता मम सदा रामस्य दासो ऽस्म्यहम् ।
रामे रञ्जत् मे मनः सुविशदं हे राम तुभ्यं नमः ॥

1.52.s: sarva ityādikā gopāḥ sakhā caiva patirhariḥ //
1.52.d: सर्व इत्यादिका गोपाः सखा चैव पतिर्हरिः ॥
1.52.m: The [nominal stems] are: sarva and so on, gopāḥ, sakhā, and patiḥ, hariḥ,

1.52.s:
suśrīrbhānuḥ svayaṃbhūśca kartā rau gaustu nauriti /
anaṅghāngodhugliṭ ca dve trayaścatvāra eva ca //
1.52.d:
सुश्रीर्भानुः स्वयंभूश्च कर्ता रौ गौस्तु नौरिति ।
अनङ्घान्गोधुग्लिट् च द्वे त्रयश्चत्वार एव च ॥
1.52.m:
suśrīḥ, bhānuḥ, svayambhūḥ, kartā, raiḥ, gauḥ, nauḥ;
anadvān, godhuk, liṭ, and dve, trayaḥ, catvāraḥ.

1.52.s:
rājā panthāstathā daṇḍī brahmahā pañca cāṣṭa ca /
aṣṭau ayaṃ mune samrāṭ savibhradvapuṅmanaḥ //
1.52.d:
राजा पन्थास्तथा दण्डी ब्रह्महा पञ्च चाष्ट च ।
अष्टौ अयं मुने सम्राट् सविभ्रद्वपुङ्मनः ॥
1.52.m:
rājā, panthās, as well as daṇḍī, brahmahā, [and the numerals] pañca and aṣṭa;
aṣṭau, ayam, O sage, samrāṭ, savibhṛt, vapuḥ, manaḥ;

1.52.s:
pratyaṅ pumānmahān dhīmān vidvānṣaṭ pipaṭhīśca doḥ /
uśanāsāviṃme puṃsi syāraktalavirāmakāḥ //
1.52.d:
प्रत्यङ् पुमान्महान् धीमान् विद्वान्षट् पिपठीश्च दोः ।
उशनासाविंमे पुंसि स्यारक्तलविरामकाः ॥
1.52.m:
pratyaṅ, pumān, mahān, dhīmān, vidvān, ṣaṭ, pipaṭhīḥ, and doḥ;
uśanā, asau—these masculine [words] end in consonants: s, r, k, t, l, and the rests [stops];

1.52.s:
rādhā sarvā gatirgopī srī śrīrdhenurvadhūḥ svasā /
gaurnauṃrupān dūdyaurgoḥ kṣut kakupsaṃvittu vā kvacit //
1.52.d:
राधा सर्वा गतिर्गोपी स्री श्रीर्धेनुर्वधूः स्वसा ।
गौर्नौंरुपान् दूद्यौर्गोः क्षुत् ककुप्संवित्तु वा क्वचित् ॥
1.52.m:
rādhā, sarvā, gatiḥ, gopī, strī, śrīḥ, dhenuḥ, vadhūḥ, svasā,
gauḥ, nauḥ, upānat, dyauḥ, gauḥ, kṣut, kakup, saṃvit, and sometimes [vā];

1.52.s:
rugviḍudbhāḥ sriyāstapaḥ kulaṃ somapamakṣi ca /
grāmaṇyaṃburavalapvevaṃ kartṛ cātiri vātinu //
1.52.d:
रुग्विडुद्भाः स्रियास्तपः कुलं सोमपमक्षि च ।
ग्रामण्यंबुरवलप्वेवं कर्तृ चातिरि वातिनु ॥
1.52.m:
ruk, viṭ, udbhāḥ, strī; [in neuter:] tapaḥ, kulam, somapam, and akṣi,
grāmaṇi, ambu, avalapu, thus kartṛ, and atiri or atinu;

1.52.s:
svanahucca vimaladyu vāśvatvārīdameva ca /
etadbrahmāhaśca daṇḍī asṛkkiñcittyadādi ca //
1.52.d:
स्वनहुच्च विमलद्यु वाश्वत्वारीदमेव च ।
एतद्ब्रह्माहश्च दण्डी असृक्किञ्चित्त्यदादि च ॥
1.52.m:
svanahuḥ, vimaladyu, vāśva, trī, and idam itself,
etat, brahma, ahaḥ, and daṇḍi, asṛk, kiñcit, and tyad etc.;

1.52.s:
etadve bhidgavākgavāṅ goak goṅgok goṅ /
tiryagyakṛcchakṛccaiva dadadbhavatpacattudat //
1.52.d:
एतद्वे भिद्गवाक्गवाङ् गोअक् गोङ्गोक् गोङ् ।
तिर्यग्यकृच्छकृच्चैव ददद्भवत्पचत्तुदत् ॥
1.52.m:
etat, vid, bhid, gavāk, gavāṅ, goak, goṅ, gok, goṅ,
tiryak, yakṛt, and śakṛt, dadat, bhavat, pacat, tudat;

1.52.s:
dīvyaddhanuśca pipaṭhīḥ payo 'daḥsumumāṃsi ca /
guṇadravya kriyāyogāṃsriliṅgāṃśca kati bruve //
1.52.d:
दीव्यद्धनुश्च पिपठीः पयो ऽदःसुमुमांसि च ।
गुणद्रव्य क्रियायोगांस्रिलिङ्गांश्च कति ब्रुवे ॥
1.52.m:
dīvyat, dhanuḥ, and pipaṭhi, payaḥ, adaḥ, and sumumān;
and those used in the three genders by connection to quality, substance, or action—how many shall I state?

1.52.s:
śuktaḥ kīlālapāścaiva śuciśca grāmaṇīḥ sudhīḥ /
paṭuḥ svayaṃbhūḥ kartā ca mātā caiva va pitā ca nā //
1.52.d:
शुक्तः कीलालपाश्चैव शुचिश्च ग्रामणीः सुधीः ।
पटुः स्वयंभूः कर्ता च माता चैव व पिता च ना ॥
1.52.m:
śuklaḥ, kīlālapāḥ, and śuciḥ, grāmaṇīḥ, sudhīḥ,
paṭuḥ, svayaṃbhūḥ, kartā, and mātā, or pitā, and nā;

1.52.s:
satyānāgyāstathā puṃso matabhramaradīrghapāt /
dhanākṛsomau cāgarhastavirgrathāsvarṇanbahū //
1.52.d:
सत्यानाग्यास्तथा पुंसो मतभ्रमरदीर्घपात् ।
धनाकृसोमौ चागर्हस्तविर्ग्रथास्वर्णन्बहू ॥
1.52.m:
satya, anāgyā, as well as of the masculine mata, bhramara, dīrghapāt,
dhanākṛ, somau, agarha, staviḥ, grathāḥ, suvarṇān, bahu;

1.52.s: rimapavviṣādvajātānaho tathā sarvaṃ viśvobhaye cobhau anyāntaretarāṇi ca //
1.52.d: रिमपव्विषाद्वजातानहो तथा सर्वं विश्वोभये चोभौ अन्यान्तरेतराणि च ॥
1.52.m: … so also sarva, viśva, ubhaya, both ubhau, anya, antara, itara, and the rest;

1.52.s:
uttaraścottamo nemastvasamo 'tha samā iṣaḥ /
pūrvottarottarāścaiva dakṣiṇaścottarādharau //
1.52.d:
उत्तरश्चोत्तमो नेमस्त्वसमो ऽथ समा इषः ।
पूर्वोत्तरोत्तराश्चैव दक्षिणश्चोत्तराधरौ ॥
1.52.m:
uttara, uttama, nema, asama, then samāḥ, iṣaḥ,
pūrvottarottarāḥ, dakṣiṇa, uttara, and adhara;

1.52.s:
aparaścaturo 'pyetadyāvattatkimasau dvayam /
yuṣmadasmañca prathamaścaramolpastathārdhakaḥ //
1.52.d:
अपरश्चतुरो ऽप्येतद्यावत्तत्किमसौ द्वयम् ।
युष्मदस्मञ्च प्रथमश्चरमोल्पस्तथार्धकः ॥
1.52.m:
apara, catur, this yāvat, tat, kim, asau, dvayam,
yuṣmad, asmad, prathama, carama, alpa, as well as ardhaka;

1.52.s:
noraḥ katipayo dve ca trayo śuddhādayastathā /
svekābhuvirodhapari viparyayaścāvyayāstathā //
1.52.d:
नोरः कतिपयो द्वे च त्रयो शुद्धादयस्तथा ।
स्वेकाभुविरोधपरि विपर्ययश्चाव्ययास्तथा ॥
1.52.m:
[the affix] na, uḥ, katipaya, dve, trayaḥ, śuddha, and so forth,
sva, eka, in the sense of opposition, pari, contrariety, and likewise the indeclinables;

1.52.s:
taddhitāścāpyapatyārthe pāṇḍavāḥ śraidharastathā /
gārgyo nāḍāyanātreyau gāṅgeyaḥ paitṛṣvasrīyaḥ //
1.52.d:
तद्धिताश्चाप्यपत्यार्थे पाण्डवाः श्रैधरस्तथा ।
गार्ग्यो नाडायनात्रेयौ गाङ्गेयः पैतृष्वस्रीयः ॥
1.52.m:
and the secondary derivative suffixes (taddhita) in the patronymic sense: pāṇḍavāḥ, śraidhara,
gārgya, nāḍāyana, ātreya, gāṅgeya, paitṛṣvasrīya;

1.52.s:
devatārthe cedamarthe hyaidraṃ brāhmo havirbalī /
kriyāyujoḥ karmakartrordhairiyaḥ kauṅkumaṃ tathā //
1.52.d:
देवतार्थे चेदमर्थे ह्यैद्रं ब्राह्मो हविर्बली ।
क्रियायुजोः कर्मकर्त्रोर्धैरियः कौङ्कुमं तथा ॥
1.52.m:
in the sense of a deity or 'pertaining to this': aindra, brāhma, havis, balī;
of two joining in an action as agent and object: dhairya, and kauṅkuma;

1.52.s:
bhavādyarthe tu kānīnaḥ kṣatriyo vaidikaḥ svakaḥ /
svārthe caurastu tulyārthe candravanmukhamīkṣate //
1.52.d:
भवाद्यर्थे तु कानीनः क्षत्रियो वैदिकः स्वकः ।
स्वार्थे चौरस्तु तुल्यार्थे चन्द्रवन्मुखमीक्षते ॥
1.52.m:
in the sense of 'born there' and so forth: kānīna, kṣatriya, vaidika, svaka;
in its own base meaning: caura; in the sense of comparison: 'he looks at the face like the moon' (candravat);

1.52.s:
brāhmaṇatvaṃ brāhmaṇatā bhāve brāhmaṇyameva ca /
gomāndhanī ca dhanavānastyarthe pramitau kiyān //
1.52.d:
ब्राह्मणत्वं ब्राह्मणता भावे ब्राह्मण्यमेव च ।
गोमान्धनी च धनवानस्त्यर्थे प्रमितौ कियान् ॥
1.52.m:
brāhmaṇatva, brāhmaṇatā, and brāhmaṇya in the abstract state;
gomān, dhanī, and dhanavān in the sense of possession; in measure: kiyān;

1.52.s:
jātārthe tundilaḥ śraddhāluraunnattye tu danturaḥ /
sragvī tapasvī medhāvī māyāvyastyartha eva ca //
1.52.d:
जातार्थे तुन्दिलः श्रद्धालुरौन्नत्त्ये तु दन्तुरः ।
स्रग्वी तपस्वी मेधावी मायाव्यस्त्यर्थ एव च ॥
1.52.m:
tundila in the sense of born with, śraddhālu; in the sense of prominence: dantura;
sragvī, tapasvī, medhāvī, māyāvī, also in the sense of possession;

1.52.s:
vācālaścaiva vācāṭo bahukutsitabhāṣiṇi /
īṣadaparisamāptau kalpavdeśīya eva ca //
1.52.d:
वाचालश्चैव वाचाटो बहुकुत्सितभाषिणि ।
ईषदपरिसमाप्तौ कल्पव्देशीय एव च ॥
1.52.m:
vācāla and vācāṭa in the sense of talking much or contemptibly;
in the sense of slightly incomplete: the suffixes -kalpa and -deśīya;

1.52.s:
kavikalpaḥ kavideśyaḥ prakāravacane tathā /
paṭujātīyaḥ kutsāyāṃ vaidyapāśaḥ praśaṃsane //
1.52.d:
कविकल्पः कविदेश्यः प्रकारवचने तथा ।
पटुजातीयः कुत्सायां वैद्यपाशः प्रशंसने ॥
1.52.m:
kavikalpa, kavideśya; so too in expressing type:
paṭujātīya; in contempt: vaidyapāśa; in praise: [vaidyarūpa];

1.52.s:
vaidyarūpo bhūtapūrve mato dṛṣṭacaro mune /
prācuryādiṣvannamayo mṛṇmayaḥ srīmayastathā //
1.52.d:
वैद्यरूपो भूतपूर्वे मतो दृष्टचरो मुने ।
प्राचुर्यादिष्वन्नमयो मृण्मयः स्रीमयस्तथा ॥
1.52.m:
vaidyarūpa; in the sense of 'having been previously': dṛṣṭacara, O sage;
in the sense of abundance: annamaya, mṛṇmaya, and strīmaya;

1.52.s:
jātārthe lajjito 'tyarthe śreyāñchreṣṭaśca nārada /
kṛṣṇataraḥ śuklatamaḥ kima ākhyānato 'vyayān //
1.52.d:
जातार्थे लज्जितो ऽत्यर्थे श्रेयाञ्छ्रेष्टश्च नारद ।
कृष्णतरः शुक्लतमः किम आख्यानतो ऽव्ययान् ॥
1.52.m:
lajjita in the sense of arisen; in the superlative degree: śreyān and śreṣṭha, O Nārada;
kṛṣṇatara, śuklatama; after 'kim', verbs, or indeclinables:

1.52.s:
kintarāṃ caivātitarāmabhihyuccaistarāmapi /
parimāṇe jānudaghnaṃ jānudvayasamityapi //
1.52.d:
किन्तरां चैवातितरामभिह्युच्चैस्तरामपि ।
परिमाणे जानुदघ्नं जानुद्वयसमित्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
kintarām, and atitarām, abhihyuccaistarām;
in measure: jānudaghna, as well as jānudvayasam;

1.52.s:
jānumātraṃ ca nirddhāre bahūnāṃ ca dvayoḥ kramāt /
katamaḥ kataraḥ saṃkhyeyaviśeṣāvadhāraṇe //
1.52.d:
जानुमात्रं च निर्द्धारे बहूनां च द्वयोः क्रमात् ।
कतमः कतरः संख्येयविशेषावधारणे ॥
1.52.m:
and jānumātra; in single selection among many or of two, respectively:
katama and katara; in specifying ordinal numbers:

1.52.s:
dvitīyaśca tṛtīyaśca caturthaḥ ṣaṣṭapañcamau /
etādaśaḥ katipayaḥ katithaḥ kati nārada //
1.52.d:
द्वितीयश्च तृतीयश्च चतुर्थः षष्टपञ्चमौ ।
एतादशः कतिपयः कतिथः कति नारद ॥
1.52.m:
dvitīya, tṛtīya, caturtha, ṣaṣṭha, pañcama,
etādṛśa, katipaya, katitha, and kati, O Nārada;

1.52.s:
viṃśaśca viṃśatitamastathā śatatamādayaḥ /
dvedhā dvaidhā dvidhā saṃkhyā prakāre 'tha munīśvara //
1.52.d:
विंशश्च विंशतितमस्तथा शततमादयः ।
द्वेधा द्वैधा द्विधा संख्या प्रकारे ऽथ मुनीश्वर ॥
1.52.m:
viṃśa and viṃśatitama, and likewise śatatamā and so forth;
dvedhā, dvaidhā, dvidhā in expressing the manner of numbers, O lord of sages;

1.52.s:
kriyāvṛttau pañcakṛtvo dvisrirbahuśa ityapi /
dvitayaṃ tritapaṃ cāpi saṃkhyāyāṃ hi dvayaṃ trayam //
1.52.d:
क्रियावृत्तौ पञ्चकृत्वो द्विस्रिर्बहुश इत्यपि ।
द्वितयं त्रितपं चापि संख्यायां हि द्वयं त्रयम् ॥
1.52.m:
in repetition of an action: pañcakṛtvaḥ, dviḥ, triḥ, and bahuśaḥ;
dvitayam and tritayam, and of numerals, dvayam and trayam;

1.52.s:
kuṭīraśca śamīraśca śuṇḍāro 'lpārthake mataḥ /
traiṇaḥ pauṣṇastuṇḍibhaśca vṛndārakakṛṣīvalau //
1.52.d:
कुटीरश्च शमीरश्च शुण्डारो ऽल्पार्थके मतः ।
त्रैणः पौष्णस्तुण्डिभश्च वृन्दारककृषीवलौ ॥
1.52.m:
kuṭīra, śamīra, and śuṇḍāra are regarded in the diminutive sense;
traiṇa, pauṣṇa, tuṇḍibha, vṛndāraka, and kṛṣīvala;

1.52.s:
malino vikaṭo gomī bhaurikīvidhamutkaṭam /
avaṭīṭovanāṭe nibiḍaṃ cekṣuśākinam //
1.52.d:
मलिनो विकटो गोमी भौरिकीविधमुत्कटम् ।
अवटीटोवनाटे निबिडं चेक्षुशाकिनम् ॥
1.52.m:
malina, vikaṭa, gomī, bhaurikividha, utkaṭa,
avaṭīṭa, vanāṭa, nibiḍa, and ikṣuśākina;

1.52.s:
nibirīsameṣukārī vittovidyāñcaṇastathā /
vidyāthuñcurbahutithaṃ parvataḥ śṛṅgiṇastathā //
1.52.d:
निबिरीसमेषुकारी वित्तोविद्याञ्चणस्तथा ।
विद्याथुञ्चुर्बहुतिथं पर्वतः शृङ्गिणस्तथा ॥
1.52.m:
nibirīsa, meṣukārī, vitta, vidyācaṇa,
vidyāthuñcu, bahutitha, parvata, and śṛṅgī;

1.52.s:
svāmī viṣamarūpyaṃ copatyakādhityakā tathā /
cillaśca cipiṭaṃ cikvaṃ vātūlaḥ kutapastathā //
1.52.d:
स्वामी विषमरूप्यं चोपत्यकाधित्यका तथा ।
चिल्लश्च चिपिटं चिक्वं वातूलः कुतपस्तथा ॥
1.52.m:
svāmī, viṣamarūpya, upatyakā, adhityakā,
cilla, cipiṭa, cikva, vātūla, kutapa;

1.52.s:
vallaśva himeluśca kahoḍaścopaḍastataḥ /
ūrṇāyuśca marūtaścaikākī carmaṇvatī tathā //
1.52.d:
वल्लश्व हिमेलुश्च कहोडश्चोपडस्ततः ।
ऊर्णायुश्च मरूतश्चैकाकी चर्मण्वती तथा ॥
1.52.m:
valla, himelu, kahoḍa, upaḍa,
ūrṇāyu, maruta, ekākī, carmaṇvatī;

1.52.s:
jyotsnā tamisrāṣṭīvacca kakṣīvardṣamaṇvatī /
āsaṃdī vañca cakrīvattūṣṇīkāṃ jalpatakyapi //
1.52.d:
ज्योत्स्ना तमिस्राष्टीवच्च कक्षीवर्द्षमण्वती ।
आसंदी वञ्च चक्रीवत्तूष्णीकां जल्पतक्यपि ॥
1.52.m:
jyotsnā, tamisrā, aṣṭīvat, kakṣīvat, carmaṇvatī,
āsandīvat, cakrīvat, tūṣṇīkā, jalpatakī;

1.52.s:
kaṃbhaśca kaṃyuḥ kaṃvaśca nāradaketiḥ kantuḥ kantakaṃpau śaṃvastathaiva ca /
śantaḥ śantiḥ śaṃyaśantau śaṃyohaṃyuḥ śubhaṃyuvat //
1.52.d:
कंभश्च कंयुः कंवश्च नारदकेतिः कन्तुः कन्तकंपौ शंवस्तथैव च ।
शन्तः शन्तिः शंयशन्तौ शंयोहंयुः शुभंयुवत् ॥
1.52.m:
kaṃbha, kaṃyu, kaṃva, O Nārada, keti, kantu, kantaka, kaṃpa, śaṃva,
śanta, śanti, śaṃya, śantu, śaṃyu, haṃyu, like śubhaṃyu;

1.52.s: bhavati bagabhūva bhavitā bhaviṣyati bhavatvabhavadbhaghaveccāpi //
1.52.d: भवति बगभूव भविता भविष्यति भवत्वभवद्भघवेच्चापि ॥
1.52.m: [The root bhū:] bhavati, babhūva, bhavitā, bhaviṣyati, bhavatu, abhavat, bhavet,

1.52.s:
bhūyādabhūdabhaviṣaayallādāvetāni rūpāṇi /
atti jaghāsāttātsyatyattvādadadyāddviraghasadātsyat //
1.52.d:
भूयादभूदभविषअयल्लादावेतानि रूपाणि ।
अत्ति जघासात्तात्स्यत्यत्त्वाददद्याद्द्विरघसदात्स्यत् ॥
1.52.m:
bhūyāt, abhūt, abhaviṣyat—these are the forms in the l-tenses [laṭ, etc.];
[The root ad:] atti, jaghāsa, attā, atsyati, attu, ādat, adyāt, aghasat, ātsyat;

1.52.s:
juhito juhāva juhavāñcakāra hotā hoṣyati juhotu /
ajuhojjuhuyāddhūyādahauṣīdahoṣyaddīvyati /
dideva devitā deviṣyati ca adīvyaddīvyeddīvyādvai //
1.52.d:
जुहितो जुहाव जुहवाञ्चकार होता होष्यति जुहोतु ।
अजुहोज्जुहुयाद्धूयादहौषीदहोष्यद्दीव्यति ।
दिदेव देविता देविष्यति च अदीव्यद्दीव्येद्दीव्याद्वै ॥
1.52.m:
[The root hu:] juhoti, juhāva, juhavāñcakāra, hotā, hoṣyati, juhotu,
ajuhot, juhuyāt, hūyāt, ahauṣīt, ahoṣyat; [The root div:] dīvyati,
dideva, devitā, deviṣyati, adīvyat, dīvyet, dīvyāt,

1.52.s:
adevīdadevīṣyatsunoti suṣāva sotā soṣyati vai /
sunotvasunotsunuyātsūyādaśāvīdasoṣyuttudati ca //
1.52.d:
अदेवीददेवीष्यत्सुनोति सुषाव सोता सोष्यति वै ।
सुनोत्वसुनोत्सुनुयात्सूयादशावीदसोष्युत्तुदति च ॥
1.52.m:
adevīt, adevīṣyat; [The root su:] sunoti, suṣāva, sotā, soṣyati,
sunotu, asunot, sunuyāt, sūyāt, asāvīt, asoṣyat; and [the root tud:] tudati,

1.52.s:
tutoda tottā totsyati tudatvatudattudettudyāddhi /
atautsīdatotsyaditi ca ruṇaddhi rūrodha roddhā rotsyati vai //
1.52.d:
तुतोद तोत्ता तोत्स्यति तुदत्वतुदत्तुदेत्तुद्याद्धि ।
अतौत्सीदतोत्स्यदिति च रुणद्धि रूरोध रोद्धा रोत्स्यति वै ॥
1.52.m:
tutoda, tottā, totsyati, tudatu, atudat, tudet, tudyāt,
atautsīt, atotsyat; and [the root rudh:] ruṇaddhi, rurodha, roddhā, rotsyati,

1.52.s:
ruṇaddhu aruṇadrudhyādarautsīdārotsyañca /
tanoti tatāna tanitā taniṣyati tanotvatanottanuyāddhi //
1.52.d:
रुणद्धु अरुणद्रुध्यादरौत्सीदारोत्स्यञ्च ।
तनोति ततान तनिता तनिष्यति तनोत्वतनोत्तनुयाद्धि ॥
1.52.m:
ruṇaddhu, aruṇat, rundhyāt, arautsīt, arotsyat;
and [the root tan:] tanoti, tatāna, tanitā, taniṣyati, tanotu, atanot, tanuyāt,

1.52.s:
atanīñcātānīdataniṣyatkrīṇāti cikrāya kretā kreṣyati krīṇātviti ca /
akrīṇātkrīṇātkrīṇīyātkrīyādakraiṣīdakreṣyañcorayati corayāmāsa corayitā corayiṣyati corayatu //
1.52.d:
अतनीञ्चातानीदतनिष्यत्क्रीणाति चिक्राय क्रेता क्रेष्यति क्रीणात्विति च ।
अक्रीणात्क्रीणात्क्रीणीयात्क्रीयादक्रैषीदक्रेष्यञ्चोरयति चोरयामास चोरयिता चोरयिष्यति चोरयतु ॥
1.52.m:
atanīt, atānīt, ataniṣyat; [The root krī:] krīṇāti, cikrāya, kretā, kreṣyati, krīṇātu,
akrīṇāt, krīṇīyāt, krīyāt, akraiṣīt, akreṣyat; [The root cur:] corayati, corayāmāsa, corayitā, corayiṣyati, corayatu,

1.52.s:
acorayañcorayeccoryāt acūcuradacoriṣyadityevaṃ daśa vai gaṇāḥ /
prayojake bhāvayati sanīcchāyāṃ bubhūṣati /
kriyāsamabhihāre tu paṇḍito bobhūyate mune //
1.52.d:
अचोरयञ्चोरयेच्चोर्यात् अचूचुरदचोरिष्यदित्येवं दश वै गणाः ।
प्रयोजके भावयति सनीच्छायां बुभूषति ।
क्रियासमभिहारे तु पण्डितो बोभूयते मुने ॥

1.52.s:
tathā yaṅluki bobhavīti ca paṭhyate /
putrīyatītyātmanīcchāyāṃ tathācāre 'pi nārada /
anudāttañito dhātoḥ kriyāvinimaye tathā //
1.52.d:
तथा यङ्लुकि बोभवीति च पठ्यते ।
पुत्रीयतीत्यात्मनीच्छायां तथाचारे ऽपि नारद ।
अनुदात्तञितो धातोः क्रियाविनिमये तथा ॥

1.52.s:
niviśādestathā vipra vijānīhyātmanepadam /
parasmaipadamākhyātaṃ śeṣātkartāri śābdikaiḥ //
1.52.d:
निविशादेस्तथा विप्र विजानीह्यात्मनेपदम् ।
परस्मैपदमाख्यातं शेषात्कर्तारि शाब्दिकैः ॥
1.52.m:
and after ni, vi, etc., O brāhmaṇa, know that the Ātmanepada is used;
the Parasmaipada is stated by grammarians to occur in the active voice for the remaining roots;

1.52.s:
ñitsvaritetaśca ubhe yakca syādbhāvakarmaṇoḥ /
saukaryātiśayaṃ caiva yadādyotayituṃ mune //
1.52.d:
ञित्स्वरितेतश्च उभे यक्च स्याद्भावकर्मणोः ।
सौकर्यातिशयं चैव यदाद्योतयितुं मुने ॥
1.52.m:
and from roots with an anudātta, ñ, or svarita indicator, both [padas occur]; and the yak-affix occurs in the passive and impersonal senses,
and when denoting exceptional ease [of accomplishment], O sage.

1.52.s:
vivakṣyate na vyāpāro lakṣye kartustadāpare /
labhante kartṛte paśya pacyate hyodanaḥ svayam //
1.52.d:
विवक्ष्यते न व्यापारो लक्ष्ये कर्तुस्तदापरे ।
लभन्ते कर्तृते पश्य पच्यते ह्योदनः स्वयम् ॥
1.52.m: When the action of the agent is not intended to be expressed in the object, then other [factors] / obtain the nature of the agent; behold: “Indeed the rice cooks by itself.”

1.52.s:
sādhu vāsiśchinattyevaṃ sthālī pacati vai mune /
dhātoḥ sakarmakādbhāve karmaṇyapi lapratyayāḥ //
1.52.d:
साधु वासिश्छिनत्त्येवं स्थाली पचति वै मुने ।
धातोः सकर्मकाद्भावे कर्मण्यपि लप्रत्ययाः ॥
1.52.m: “The axe cuts well”; likewise, O sage: “The pot cooks.” / From a transitive verbal root, the L-affixes are taught in the senses of verbal state and object;

1.52.s:
tasmai vākarmakādvipra bhāve kartari kīrtitaḥ /
phalavyāparayorekaniṣṭatāyāmakarmakaḥ //
1.52.d:
तस्मै वाकर्मकाद्विप्र भावे कर्तरि कीर्तितः ।
फलव्यापरयोरेकनिष्टतायामकर्मकः ॥
1.52.m: Or from an intransitive [root], O twice-born one, [an L-affix] is proclaimed in the senses of verbal state and agent. / When the fruit and the action reside in the same substrate, [the root] is intransitive;

1.52.s:
dhātustayorddharmibhede sakarmaka udāhṛtaḥ /
gauṇe karmaṇi druhyādeḥ pradhāne nīhṛkṛṣvahām //
1.52.d:
धातुस्तयोर्द्धर्मिभेदे सकर्मक उदाहृतः ।
गौणे कर्मणि द्रुह्यादेः प्रधाने नीहृकृष्वहाम् ॥
1.52.m: When there is a distinction between the loci of those two, the root is called transitive. / In the secondary object of roots like druh- (to bear malice), and in the primary [object] of nī-, hṛ-, kṛṣ-, and vah-;

1.52.s:
buddhibhakṣārthayoḥ śabdakarmakāṇāṃ nijecchayā /
prayojya karmaṇyanyeṣāṃ ṇyantānāṃ lādayo matāḥ //
1.52.d:
बुद्धिभक्षार्थयोः शब्दकर्मकाणां निजेच्छया ।
प्रयोज्य कर्मण्यन्येषां ण्यन्तानां लादयो मताः ॥
1.52.m: For verbs meaning to know or to eat, and for those having sound as their object, according to one's desire, / in the case of other [verbs] ending in ṇi (causatives), the L[-affixes] and others are held to occur with the prompted agent as object.

1.52.s:
phalavyāpārayorddhāturāśraye tu tiṅaḥ smṛtāḥ /
phale pradhānaṃ vyāpārastirṅthastu viśeṣaṇam //
1.52.d:
फलव्यापारयोर्द्धातुराश्रये तु तिङः स्मृताः ।
फले प्रधानं व्यापारस्तिर्ङ्थस्तु विशेषणम् ॥
1.52.m: The verbal root denotes the fruit and the action; the tiṅ-affixes, however, denote their substrate. / With respect to the fruit, the action is primary, while the meaning of the tiṅ-affix is a qualifier.

1.52.s:
edhitavyamedhanīyamiti kṛtye nidarśanam /
bhāve karmaṇi kṛtyāḥ syuḥ kṛtaḥ kartari kīrtitāḥ //
1.52.d:
एधितव्यमेधनीयमिति कृत्ये निदर्शनम् ।
भावे कर्मणि कृत्याः स्युः कृतः कर्तरि कीर्तिताः ॥
1.52.m: “Edhitavyam” (to be increased), “edhanīyam” (to be increased) are illustrations in the case of a kṛtya-affix; / kṛtya-affixes occur in the senses of verbal state and object, while kṛt-affixes are declared in the sense of the agent.

1.52.s:
kartā kāraka ityādyā bhūte bhūtādi kīrtitam /
gamyādigamye nirdiṣṭaṃ śeṣamadyatane matam //
1.52.d:
कर्ता कारक इत्याद्या भूते भूतादि कीर्तितम् ।
गम्यादिगम्ये निर्दिष्टं शेषमद्यतने मतम् ॥
1.52.m: “Kartā” (agent), “kāraka” (maker), and so forth [are examples]. In the past tense, bhūta- and others are taught; / gamya- and others are prescribed for the future (gamya), and the rest is taught for the proximate past (adyatana).

1.52.s:
adhisrītyavyayībhāve yathāśakti ca kīrtitam /
rāmāśritastatpuruṣe dhānyārtho yūpadāru ca //
1.52.d:
अधिस्रीत्यव्ययीभावे यथाशक्ति च कीर्तितम् ।
रामाश्रितस्तत्पुरुषे धान्यार्थो यूपदारु च ॥
1.52.m: “Adhistri” (concerning women) and “yathāśakti” (according to ability) are cited in an avyayībhāva compound; / “rāmāśritaḥ” (resorting to Rāma), “dhānyārthaḥ” (wealth acquired by grain), and “yūpadāru” (wood for the sacrificial post) are in a tatpuruṣa;

1.52.s:
vyāghrabhī rājapuruṣo 'kṣaśaiṇḍo dvigurucyate /
pañcagavaṃ daśagrāmī triphaleti tu rūḍhitaḥ //
1.52.d:
व्याघ्रभी राजपुरुषो ऽक्षशैण्डो द्विगुरुच्यते ।
पञ्चगवं दशग्रामी त्रिफलेति तु रूढितः ॥
1.52.m: “Vyāghrabhīḥ” (fear of a tiger), “rājapuruṣaḥ” (the king's man), “akṣaśauṇḍaḥ” (skilled at dice) [are also tatpuruṣas]. A dvigu is declared / conventionally in “pañcagavam” (a collection of five cows), “daśagrāmī” (a collection of ten villages), and “triphalā” (three fruits);

1.52.s:
nīlotpalaṃ mahāṣaṣṭī tulyārthe karmadhārayaḥ /
abrāhmaṇo na ñi proktaḥ kuṃbhakārādikaḥ kṛtā //
1.52.d:
नीलोत्पलं महाषष्टी तुल्यार्थे कर्मधारयः ।
अब्राह्मणो न ञि प्रोक्तः कुंभकारादिकः कृता ॥
1.52.m: “Nīlotpalam” (blue lotus) and “mahāṣaṣṭī” (great sixth day) are karmadhārayas in the sense of apposition; / “abrāhmaṇaḥ” (non-Brahmin) is stated with the negative particle nañ; “kumbhakāraḥ” (pot-maker) and the like are formed by a kṛt-affix.

1.52.s:
anyārthe tu bahuvrīhau grāmaḥ prāptodako dvija /
pañcagū rūpavadbhāryo madhyāhnaḥ sasutādikaḥ //
1.52.d:
अन्यार्थे तु बहुव्रीहौ ग्रामः प्राप्तोदको द्विज ।
पञ्चगू रूपवद्भार्यो मध्याह्नः ससुतादिकः ॥
1.52.m: In a bahuvrīhi denoting another sense, O twice-born one: “prāptodako grāmaḥ” (a village to which water has come), / “pañcaguḥ” (one who has five cows), “rūpavadbhāryaḥ” (one whose wife is beautiful), “madhyāhnaḥ” (midday), “sasutaḥ” (accompanied by a son), and so forth.

1.52.s:
samuccaye guruṃ ceśaṃ bhajasvānvācaye tvaṭa // ca dvayoḥ kramāt /
bhikṣāmānaya gāṃ cāpi vākyamevānayorbhavet //
1.52.d:
समुच्चये गुरुं चेशं भजस्वान्वाचये त्वट ॥ च द्वयोः क्रमात् ।
भिक्षामानय गां चापि वाक्यमेवानयोर्भवेत् ॥
1.52.m: In conjunction: “Worship the guru and God”; in secondary connection: “Worship, and wander!” [using “ca”] in the two respectively; / “Bring alms, and the cow as well”—this very sentence illustrates both of them.

1.52.s:
itaretarayoge tu rāmakṛṣṇau samāhṛtau /
rāmakṛṣṇaṃ dvija dvai dvai brahma caikamupāsyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde vyākaraṇanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvipañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.52.d:
इतरेतरयोगे तु रामकृष्णौ समाहृतौ ।
रामकृष्णं द्विज द्वै द्वै ब्रह्म चैकमुपास्यते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे व्याकरणनिरूपणं नाम द्विपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.52.m:
In mutual association: “Rāmakṛṣṇau” (Rāma and Kṛṣṇa); in collective aggregation: / “Rāmakṛṣṇam”, O twice-born one. The two are distinct, yet one Brahman is worshipped.

Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, titled “Exposition of Grammar”, in the second quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna, in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.53.s:
sanandana uvāca
niruktaṃ te pravakṣyāmi vedaṃ śrotrāṅgamuttamam /
tatpañcavidhamākhyātaṃ vaidikaṃ dhāturūpakam //
1.53.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
निरुक्तं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि वेदं श्रोत्राङ्गमुत्तमम् ।
तत्पञ्चविधमाख्यातं वैदिकं धातुरूपकम् ॥
1.53.m: Sanandana said: / I shall declare to you the Nirukta, the excellent ear-limb of the Veda; / that Vedic [science], consisting of verbal forms, is declared to be of five kinds.

1.53.s:
kvacidūrṇāgamastatra kvacidvarṇaviparyayaḥ /
vikāraḥ kvāpi varṇānāṃ varṇanāśaḥ kvacinmataḥ //
1.53.d:
क्वचिदूर्णागमस्तत्र क्वचिद्वर्णविपर्ययः ।
विकारः क्वापि वर्णानां वर्णनाशः क्वचिन्मतः ॥
1.53.m: In some cases there is the addition of a letter; in some, the transposition of letters; / in some, the modification of letters; and in some, the elision of a letter is accepted;

1.53.s:
tathā vikāranāśābhyāṃ varṇānāṃ yatra nārada /
dhātoryogātiśayī ca saṃyogaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.53.d:
तथा विकारनाशाभ्यां वर्णानां यत्र नारद ।
धातोर्योगातिशयी च संयोगः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.53.m: Likewise where, through modification and loss of letters, O Nārada, / there is an intensive connection of the root, that is proclaimed as the fifth combination.

1.53.s:
siddhedvarṇāgamāddhaṃsaḥ siṃho varṇaviparyayāt /
gūḍhotmā varṇavikṛtervarṇanāṃśātpṛṣodaraḥ //
1.53.d:
सिद्धेद्वर्णागमाद्धंसः सिंहो वर्णविपर्ययात् ।
गूढोत्मा वर्णविकृतेर्वर्णनांशात्पृषोदरः ॥
1.53.m: From the addition of a letter “haṃsaḥ” (swan) is derived; “siṃhaḥ” (lion) from the transposition of letters; / “gūḍhotmā” from the modification of letters; “pṛṣodaraḥ” from the loss of a letter.

1.53.s:
bhramarāduṣu śabdeṣu jñeyo yogo hi pañcamaḥ /
bahulaṃ chandasītyuktamatra vācyaṃ punarvasū //
1.53.d:
भ्रमरादुषु शब्देषु ज्ञेयो योगो हि पञ्चमः ।
बहुलं छन्दसीत्युक्तमत्र वाच्यं पुनर्वसू ॥
1.53.m: In words such as “bhramara” (bee) the fifth combination is to be known. / It is stated that “diversely [it occurs] in the Veda”; here must be stated the dual form “Punarvasū”;

1.53.s:
nabhasvadvṛṣaṇaścaivāparasmaipadi cāpi hi /
paraṃ vyavahitāścāpi gatisaṃjñāstathā hi ā //
1.53.d:
नभस्वद्वृषणश्चैवापरस्मैपदि चापि हि ।
परं व्यवहिताश्चापि गतिसंज्ञास्तथा हि आ ॥
1.53.m: “Nabhasvat” (wind) and “vṛṣaṇaḥ”, and even where an Ātmanepada is used instead of a Parasmaipada; / separated by intervening elements, and having the designation gati, as in “ā”;

1.53.s:
vibhaktīnāṃ viparyāso yathā dadhanā juhoti hi /
abhyutsādayāmaketurdhvanayītpramukhāstathā /
niṣṭarkyāndyāstathoktāśca gṛbhāyetyādikāstathā //
1.53.d:
विभक्तीनां विपर्यासो यथा दधना जुहोति हि ।
अभ्युत्सादयामकेतुर्ध्वनयीत्प्रमुखास्तथा ।
निष्टर्क्यान्द्यास्तथोक्ताश्च गृभायेत्यादिकास्तथा ॥
1.53.m: The transposition of case-terminations, as in “dadhanā juhoti”; / forms beginning with “abhyutsādayāmaketuḥ”, “dhvanayīt”, / “niṣṭarkya”, and the like, as well as “gṛbhāya” and so forth;

1.53.s:
suptiṅupagrahaliṅganarāṇāṃ kālahalūcūsvarakartṛyaḍāṃ ca /
vyatyayamicchati śāsrakṛdeṣāṃ so 'pi ca siddhyati bāhulakena //
1.53.d:
सुप्तिङुपग्रहलिङ्गनराणां कालहलूचूस्वरकर्तृयडां च ।
व्यत्ययमिच्छति शास्रकृदेषां सो ऽपि च सिद्ध्यति बाहुलकेन ॥
1.53.m: Of sup-affixes, tiṅ-affixes, voice, gender, person, tense, consonants, vowels, accents, agents, and y-augment / the author of the treatise accepts interchange; and that too is established by diversity (bāhulaka).

1.53.s: rātrī vimbī ca kadrūścāviṣṭvau vājasaneyinaḥ //
1.53.d: रात्री विम्बी च कद्रूश्चाविष्ट्वौ वाजसनेयिनः ॥
1.53.m: “Rātrī”, “bimbī”, “kadrūḥ”, and “aviṣṭvau” among the Vājasaneyins;

1.53.s:
karṇebhiśca yaśobhāgya ityādyāścaturakṣaram /
devāso 'tho sarvadevatātitvāvata ityapi //
1.53.d:
कर्णेभिश्च यशोभाग्य इत्याद्याश्चतुरक्षरम् ।
देवासो ऽथो सर्वदेवतातित्वावत इत्यपि ॥
1.53.m: “Karṇebhiḥ”, “yaśobhāgya”, and four-syllabled forms of that kind; / “devāsaḥ”, and then “sarvadevatāt”, “itvāvataḥ” as well;

1.53.s:
ubhayāvina mādyāśca pralayādyāśca stṛcaṃ tathā /
apaspṛdhethāṃ no avyādāyo asmānmukhāstathā //
1.53.d:
उभयाविन माद्याश्च प्रलयाद्याश्च स्तृचं तथा ।
अपस्पृधेथां नो अव्यादायो अस्मान्मुखास्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Forms such as “ubhayāvin”, “pralaya”, and “stṛcam”; / “apaspṛdhethām”, “no avyāt”, and those beginning with “āyo asmān”;

1.53.s:
sagarbhyosthāpadī ṛtvyorajiṣṭaṃ tripañcakam /
hiraṇyayena naraṃ ca parame vyomanityapi //
1.53.d:
सगर्भ्योस्थापदी ऋत्व्योरजिष्टं त्रिपञ्चकम् ।
हिरण्ययेन नरं च परमे व्योमनित्यपि ॥
1.53.m: “Sagarbhyaḥ”, “sthāpadī”, “ṛtvyā”, “ajiṣṭam”, the group of fifteen; / “hiraṇyayena”, “naram”, and “parame vyoman” as well;

1.53.s:
urviyā svaprayā vāravadhvādaduhavaivadhī /
yajadhvainamemasi ca snātvī gatvā pacāsthabhauḥ //
1.53.d:
उर्विया स्वप्रया वारवध्वाददुहवैवधी ।
यजध्वैनमेमसि च स्नात्वी गत्वा पचास्थभौः ॥
1.53.m: “Urviyā”, “svaprayā”, “vāravadhvā”, “aduhava”, “evadhī”, / “yajadhvainam”, “emasi”, “snātvī”, “gatvā”, “pacāsthabhauḥ”;

1.53.s:
gonāñcāparihravṛttāścāturirgrasitādikā /
paśyedadhadbrabhūthāpi pramiṇāntityavīvṛdhat //
1.53.d:
गोनाञ्चापरिह्रवृत्ताश्चातुरिर्ग्रसितादिका ।
पश्येदधद्ब्रभूथापि प्रमिणान्तित्यवीवृधत् ॥
1.53.m: “Gonām”, “aparihvṛtāḥ”, “cāturiḥ”, forms beginning with “grasita”, / “paśyet”, “adhadbrap”, “bhūtha”, “pramiṇanti”, and “yavīvṛdhat”;

1.53.s:
mitrayuśca durasvā vā hātvā sudhitamityapi /
dadhartyādyā svavadbhiśca sasūveti ca dhiṣva ca //
1.53.d:
मित्रयुश्च दुरस्वा वा हात्वा सुधितमित्यपि ।
दधर्त्याद्या स्ववद्भिश्च ससूवेति च धिष्व च ॥
1.53.m: “Mitrayuḥ”, “durasvā”, “hātvā”, and “sudhitam”; / roots beginning with “dadharti”, “svavadbhiḥ”, “sasūva”, and “dhiṣva”;

1.53.s:
praprāyaṃ ca harivatekṣaṇvataḥ suparthitaraḥ /
rathītarī nasatādyā amnarbhuvaratho iti //
1.53.d:
प्रप्रायं च हरिवतेक्षण्वतः सुपर्थितरः ।
रथीतरी नसताद्या अम्नर्भुवरथो इति ॥
1.53.m: “Praprāyam”, “harivate”, “akṣaṇvataḥ”, “suparthitaraḥ”, / “rathītarī”, forms beginning with “nasat”, “amnar”, “bhuvar”, and “atho”;

1.53.s:
brūhyādyādeḥ parasyāpyau śrāvayetyādike plutaḥ /
dāśvāṃśva svatavānyāpautribhiṣṭvaṃ ca nṛbhiṣṭutaḥ //
1.53.d:
ब्रूह्याद्यादेः परस्याप्यौ श्रावयेत्यादिके प्लुतः ।
दाश्वांश्व स्वतवान्यापौत्रिभिष्ट्वं च नृभिष्टुतः ॥
1.53.m: A prolated vowel after verbal forms beginning with “brūhi”, or in “śrāvaya” and the like; / “dāśvāṃsaḥ”, “svatavān”, “yāpau”, “tribhiṣṭvam”, and “nṛbhiṣṭutaḥ”;

1.53.s:
abhīṣuṇa ṛtāvāhaṃ nyaṣīdannṛmaṇā api /
caturvidhādbāhulakātpravṛtterapravṛttitaḥ //
1.53.d:
अभीषुण ऋतावाहं न्यषीदन्नृमणा अपि ।
चतुर्विधाद्बाहुलकात्प्रवृत्तेरप्रवृत्तितः ॥
1.53.m: “Abhīṣuṇaḥ”, “ṛtāvāham”, “nyaṣīdan”, and “nṛmaṇāḥ”. / From the fourfold diversity—application, non-application,

1.53.s:
vibhāṣayānyathābhāvātsarvaṃ siddhyeñca vaidikam /
bhūvādyā dhātavo jñeyāḥ parasmaipadinaḥsmṛtāḥ //
1.53.d:
विभाषयान्यथाभावात्सर्वं सिद्ध्येञ्च वैदिकम् ।
भूवाद्या धातवो ज्ञेयाः परस्मैपदिनःस्मृताः ॥
1.53.m: optional application, and variation—everything Vedic is established. / The roots beginning with bhū are to be known as taking Parasmaipada terminations;

1.53.s:
edhādyā ātmanebhāṣā udāttāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśasaṃkhyakāḥ /
atādayo 'ṣṭatriṃśañca parasmaipadino mune //
1.53.d:
एधाद्या आत्मनेभाषा उदात्ताः षट्त्रिंशसंख्यकाः ।
अतादयो ऽष्टत्रिंशञ्च परस्मैपदिनो मुने ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with edh- take Ātmanepada, have an acute accent, and number thirty-six; / those beginning with at- number thirty-eight and take Parasmaipada, O sage;

1.53.s:
lokṛpūrvā dvicatvāriṃśaduktā ca hyātmane pade /
udāttetaratu pañcāśatphakkādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
1.53.d:
लोकृपूर्वा द्विचत्वारिंशदुक्ता च ह्यात्मने पदे ।
उदात्तेतरतु पञ्चाशत्फक्काद्याः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with lokṛ- are stated to be forty-two in Ātmanepada; / those having an accent other than the acute, beginning with phakk-, are declared to be fifty;

1.53.s:
varcādyā anudātteta ekaviṃśatirīrītāḥ /
gupādayo dvicatvāriṃśadudāttetāḥ samīritāḥ //
1.53.d:
वर्चाद्या अनुदात्तेत एकविंशतिरीरीताः ।
गुपादयो द्विचत्वारिंशदुदात्तेताः समीरिताः ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with varc- have a grave accent and are stated to be twenty-one; / those beginning with gup- are stated to be forty-two with an acute accent;

1.53.s:
dhiṇyādayo 'nudātteto daśa proktā hi śābdikaiḥ /
aṇādayopyudāttetaḥ saptaviṃśatidhātavaḥ //
1.53.d:
धिण्यादयो ऽनुदात्तेतो दश प्रोक्ता हि शाब्दिकैः ।
अणादयोप्युदात्तेतः सप्तविंशतिधातवः ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with dhiṇy- have a grave accent and are said by grammarians to be ten; / those roots beginning with aṇ- have an acute accent and are twenty-seven;

1.53.s:
amādayaḥ samuddiṣṭāścatursriṃśaddhiśābdikaiḥ /
dvisaptatimitā mavyamukhāścodāttabandhanā //
1.53.d:
अमादयः समुद्दिष्टाश्चतुर्स्रिंशद्धिशाब्दिकैः ।
द्विसप्ततिमिता मव्यमुखाश्चोदात्तबन्धना ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with am- are taught by grammarians to be thirty-four; / those beginning with mavy- are seventy-two in number and bound to the acute accent;

1.53.s:
svāriteddhāvudhātustu eka eva prakīrtitaḥ /
kṣudhādayo 'nudātteto dviṣapañcāśadudāhṛtāḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वारितेद्धावुधातुस्तु एक एव प्रकीर्तितः ।
क्षुधादयो ऽनुदात्तेतो द्विषपञ्चाशदुदाहृताः ॥
1.53.m: The root [dhāv-] having a circumflex accent is proclaimed to be only one; / those beginning with kṣudh- having a grave accent are mentioned as fifty-six;

1.53.s:
ghuṣirādyā udāttato 'ṣṭāśītirdhātavo matāḥ /
dyutādyā anudātteto dvāviṃśatirato matāḥ //
1.53.d:
घुषिराद्या उदात्ततो ऽष्टाशीतिर्धातवो मताः ।
द्युताद्या अनुदात्तेतो द्वाविंशतिरतो मताः ॥
1.53.m: The roots beginning with ghuṣir- having an acute accent are held to be eighty-eight; / those beginning with dyut- having a grave accent are held thereafter to be twenty-two.

1.53.s:
ṣitasrayodaśa ghaṭādiṣvenudatteta īritaḥ /
tato jvaladudātteto dvipañcāśanmitāstathā //
1.53.d:
षितस्रयोदश घटादिष्वेनुदत्तेत ईरितः ।
ततो ज्वलदुदात्तेतो द्विपञ्चाशन्मितास्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Thirteen [roots] with an indicated ṣ are declared among those beginning with ghaṭ with an indicated anudātta; / then those beginning with jval with an indicated udātta are likewise measured at fifty-two.

1.53.s:
svaritedrājṛsaṃprokta stanahebhrājṛtasrayaḥ /
anudātteta akhyātā bhādyutāttā itaḥ syamāt //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेद्राजृसंप्रोक्त स्तनहेभ्राजृतस्रयः ।
अनुदात्तेत अख्याता भाद्युतात्ता इतः स्यमात् ॥
1.53.m: Rājṛ is said to have an indicated svarita; three [roots], beginning with staneh and bhrājṛ, / are declared to have an indicated anudātta, from bhādyut down to syam.

1.53.s:
saho 'nudāttedekastu ramaiko 'pyātmanaipadī /
sadasraya udāttetaḥ kucādvedā udātta it //
1.53.d:
सहो ऽनुदात्तेदेकस्तु रमैको ऽप्यात्मनैपदी ।
सदस्रय उदात्तेतः कुचाद्वेदा उदात्त इत् ॥
1.53.m: Sah is the one with an indicated anudātta, and ram is the one taking the Ātmanepada endings; / three [roots] beginning with sad have an indicated udātta; four from kuc have an indicated udātta.

1.53.s:
svaritetaḥ pañcatriṃśaddhikkādyāśca tataḥ param /
svaritecchiñbhṛñādyāścatvāra svaritettataḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेतः पञ्चत्रिंशद्धिक्काद्याश्च ततः परम् ।
स्वरितेच्छिञ्भृञाद्याश्चत्वार स्वरितेत्ततः ॥
1.53.m: There are thirty-five with an indicated svarita; and after that those beginning with dhikk; / chiñ, bhṛñ and others with an indicated svarita are four; then with an indicated svarita:

1.53.s:
dheṭaḥ parasmaipadinaḥ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadudīritāḥ /
aṣṭādaśasmiṅādyāstu āmanepadino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
धेटः परस्मैपदिनः षट्चत्वारिंशदुदीरिताः ।
अष्टादशस्मिङाद्यास्तु आमनेपदिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Forty-six taking the Parasmaipada endings are stated from dheṭ; / eighteen beginning with smiṅ are considered to take the Ātmanepada endings.

1.53.s:
tatasrayo 'nudāttetaḥ pūṅādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
hṛparasmaipadī cātmanebhāṣāstu gupātrayaḥ //
1.53.d:
ततस्रयो ऽनुदात्तेतः पूङाद्याः परिकीर्तिताः ।
हृपरस्मैपदी चात्मनेभाषास्तु गुपात्रयः ॥
1.53.m: Then three beginning with pūṅ are proclaimed to have an indicated anudātta; / hṛ takes the Parasmaipada endings, whereas the three roots from gup are Ātmanepada.

1.53.s:
rabhadyabdayanudātteto ñikṣvidotātta inmataḥ /
parasmaipadinaḥ pañca daśa skaṃmbhvādayastathā //
1.53.d:
रभद्यब्दयनुदात्तेतो ञिक्ष्विदोतात्त इन्मतः ।
परस्मैपदिनः पञ्च दश स्कंम्भ्वादयस्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Rabh and labh have an indicated anudātta, and ñikṣvid is considered to have an indicated udātta; / fifteen beginning with skambh take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
kitadhāturudātteñca dānaśānobhayātmakau /
svaritetaḥ pacādyaṅkāḥ parasmaipadino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
कितधातुरुदात्तेञ्च दानशानोभयात्मकौ ।
स्वरितेतः पचाद्यङ्काः परस्मैपदिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: The root kit has an indicated udātta, and dān and śān take both sets of endings; / nine roots beginning with pac have an indicated svarita, regarded as Parasmaipada.

1.53.s:
svaritetastrayaścaitau vadavacī paribhāṣiṇau /
bhvādyā ete ṣaḍadhikaṃ sahasraṃ dhātavo matāḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेतस्त्रयश्चैतौ वदवची परिभाषिणौ ।
भ्वाद्या एते षडधिकं सहस्रं धातवो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Three roots have an indicated svarita, and these two, vad and vac, speak [Parasmaipada]; / these roots of the first class beginning with bhū are reckoned as one thousand and six.

1.53.s:
parasmaipadinaḥ proktā vadāścāpi haneti ca /
svariteto dviṣādyāstu catvāro dhātavo matāḥ //
1.53.d:
परस्मैपदिनः प्रोक्ता वदाश्चापि हनेति च ।
स्वरितेतो द्विषाद्यास्तु चत्वारो धातवो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Vad and also han are declared to take the Parasmaipada endings; / four roots beginning with dviṣ are considered to have an indicated svarita.

1.53.s:
cakṣiṅekaḥ samākhyāto dhāturatrātmanepadī /
irādayo 'nudātteto dhātavastu trayodaśa //
1.53.d:
चक्षिङेकः समाख्यातो धातुरत्रात्मनेपदी ।
इरादयो ऽनुदात्तेतो धातवस्तु त्रयोदश ॥
1.53.m: Cakṣiṅ is declared to be the single root here taking the Ātmanepada endings; / thirteen roots beginning with i have an indicated anudātta.

1.53.s:
ātmanepadinau proktau ṣūṅśīṅdvau śābdikairmune /
parasmaipadinaḥ proktā ṣumukhāḥ sapta dhātavaḥ //
1.53.d:
आत्मनेपदिनौ प्रोक्तौ षूङ्शीङ्द्वौ शाब्दिकैर्मुने ।
परस्मैपदिनः प्रोक्ता षुमुखाः सप्त धातवः ॥
1.53.m: The two roots ṣūṅ and śīṅ are proclaimed by grammarians to take the Ātmanepada endings, O sage; / seven roots beginning with ṣu are declared to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
svaritedurṇuñākhyāto dhātureko munīśvara /
ghumukhāstraya uddiṣṭāḥ parasmaipadinastathā //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेदुर्णुञाख्यातो धातुरेको मुनीश्वर ।
घुमुखास्त्रय उद्दिष्टाः परस्मैपदिनस्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Urṇuñ is declared to be a single root with an indicated svarita, O lord of sages; / three roots beginning with ghu are likewise indicated as Parasmaipada.

1.53.s: ṣṭuñekastu samā khyātaḥ smṛte nārada śābdikaiḥ //
1.53.d: ष्टुञेकस्तु समा ख्यातः स्मृते नारद शाब्दिकैः ॥
1.53.m: And ṣṭuñ is traditionally declared to be single, O Nārada, by grammarians.

1.53.s:
aṣṭādaśa rāprabhṛtayaḥ parasmaipadinaḥ smṛtāḥ /
iṅṅātmanepadī prokto dhāturnārada kevalaḥ //
1.53.d:
अष्टादश राप्रभृतयः परस्मैपदिनः स्मृताः ।
इङ्ङात्मनेपदी प्रोक्तो धातुर्नारद केवलः ॥
1.53.m: Eighteen roots beginning with rā are remembered as taking the Parasmaipada endings; / the root iṅ alone, O Nārada, is declared to take the Ātmanepada endings.

1.53.s:
vidāda yastu catvāraḥ parasmaipadino matāḥ /
ñiṣvapśaye samuddiṣṭaḥ parasmaipadikastathā //
1.53.d:
विदाद यस्तु चत्वारः परस्मैपदिनो मताः ।
ञिष्वप्शये समुद्दिष्टः परस्मैपदिकस्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Four roots beginning with vid are considered to take the Parasmaipada endings; / ñiṣvap is indicated in lying down, and likewise as taking the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
parasmaipadinaścaiva te mayoktāḥ syamādayaḥ /
dīdhīṅveṅsmṛtau dhātū ātmanepadinau mune //
1.53.d:
परस्मैपदिनश्चैव ते मयोक्ताः स्यमादयः ।
दीधीङ्वेङ्स्मृतौ धातू आत्मनेपदिनौ मुने ॥
1.53.m: And those beginning with syam have been spoken of by me as taking the Parasmaipada endings; / dīdhīṅ and veṅ are remembered, O sage, as two roots taking the Ātmanepada endings.

1.53.s:
prathādayasrayaścāpi udāttetaḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
carkarītaṃ ca hnuṅ prokto 'nudāttenmunisattama //
1.53.d:
प्रथादयस्रयश्चापि उदात्तेतः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
चर्करीतं च ह्नुङ् प्रोक्तो ऽनुदात्तेन्मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.53.m: And three roots beginning with prath are proclaimed to have an indicated udātta; / and intensive [forms] and hnuṅ are declared to have an indicated anudātta, O best of sages.

1.53.s:
trisaptati samākhyātā dhātavo 'dādike gaṇe /
dādayo dhātavo vedāḥ parasmaipadino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
त्रिसप्तति समाख्याता धातवो ऽदादिके गणे ।
दादयो धातवो वेदाः परस्मैपदिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Seventy-three roots are enumerated in the class beginning with ad; / four roots beginning with dā are considered to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
svaritedvai bhṛñākhyāta udātteddhāk prakīrtitaḥ /
māṅhāṅdvāvanudāttetau svariteddānadhātuṣu //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेद्वै भृञाख्यात उदात्तेद्धाक् प्रकीर्तितः ।
माङ्हाङ्द्वावनुदात्तेतौ स्वरितेद्दानधातुषु ॥
1.53.m: Bhṛñ indeed is declared to have an indicated svarita, and hāk is proclaimed to have an indicated udātta; / māṅ and hāṅ are two roots with an indicated anudātta, and among roots of giving, [dā] has an indicated svarita.

1.53.s:
vāṇitirādyāsrayaśvāpi svariteta udāhṛtāḥ /
ghṛmukhā dvādaśa tathā parasmaipatino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
वाणितिराद्यास्रयश्वापि स्वरितेत उदाहृताः ।
घृमुखा द्वादश तथा परस्मैपतिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: And three roots beginning with vāṇiti are cited as having an indicated svarita; / likewise twelve roots beginning with ghṛ are considered to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
dvāviṃśatirihoddiṣṭā dhātavo hvādike gaṇe /
parasmaipadinaḥ proktā divādyāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ //
1.53.d:
द्वाविंशतिरिहोद्दिष्टा धातवो ह्वादिके गणे ।
परस्मैपदिनः प्रोक्ता दिवाद्याः पञ्चविंशतिः ॥
1.53.m: Twenty-two roots are indicated here in the class beginning with hu; / twenty-five beginning with div are declared to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
ātmanepadinau dhātū ṣūṅdūṅdvāvapi nārada /
oditaḥ pūṅmukhāḥ sapta ātmanedapino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
आत्मनेपदिनौ धातू षूङ्दूङ्द्वावपि नारद ।
ओदितः पूङ्मुखाः सप्त आत्मनेदपिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Both roots, ṣūṅ and dūṅ, take the Ātmanepada endings, O Nārada; / seven beginning with pūṅ, having an indicated o, are considered to take the Ātmanepada endings.

1.53.s:
ātmanepadino vipra dīṅmukhāstviha kīrtitāḥ /
syatiprabhṛtayo vedāḥ parasmaipadino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
आत्मनेपदिनो विप्र दीङ्मुखास्त्विह कीर्तिताः ।
स्यतिप्रभृतयो वेदाः परस्मैपदिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Those beginning with dīṅ are proclaimed here as taking the Ātmanepada endings, O brāhmaṇa; / four roots beginning with syati are considered to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
janyādayaḥ pañcadaśa ātmanepadino mune /
mṛṣādyāḥ svaritetastu dhātavaḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ //
1.53.d:
जन्यादयः पञ्चदश आत्मनेपदिनो मुने ।
मृषाद्याः स्वरितेतस्तु धातवः पञ्च कीर्तिताः ॥
1.53.m: Fifteen roots beginning with jan take the Ātmanepada endings, O sage; / five roots beginning with mṛṣ are proclaimed to have an indicated svarita.

1.53.s:
ekādaśa padādyāstu hyātmanepadino matāḥ /
rādhoḥ karmaka evātra vṛddhau svādicurādike //
1.53.d:
एकादश पदाद्यास्तु ह्यात्मनेपदिनो मताः ।
राधोः कर्मक एवात्र वृद्धौ स्वादिचुरादिके ॥
1.53.m: Eleven roots beginning with pad are considered to take the Ātmanepada endings; / here rādh is exclusively intransitive in the sense of growth in the class beginning with svā and cur.

1.53.s:
udāttetastudādyāstu trayodaśa samīritāḥ /
parasmaipadino 'ṣṭātra radhādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
1.53.d:
उदात्तेतस्तुदाद्यास्तु त्रयोदश समीरिताः ।
परस्मैपदिनो ऽष्टात्र रधाद्याः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.53.m: Thirteen roots beginning with tud are declared to have an indicated udātta; / eight roots beginning with radh are proclaimed here to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
samādyāścāpyudāttetaḥ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadudīritāḥ /
catvāriśacchataṃ cāpi divādau dhātavo matāḥ //
1.53.d:
समाद्याश्चाप्युदात्तेतः षट्चत्वारिंशदुदीरिताः ।
चत्वारिशच्छतं चापि दिवादौ धातवो मताः ॥
1.53.m: And forty-six roots beginning with śam are declared to have an indicated udātta; / and one hundred and forty roots are considered to be in the class beginning with div.

1.53.s:
svādayaḥ svaritettoṅkā dhātavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
saptākhyāto dunotistu parasmaipadino mune //
1.53.d:
स्वादयः स्वरितेत्तोङ्का धातवः परिकीर्तिताः ।
सप्ताख्यातो दुनोतिस्तु परस्मैपदिनो मुने ॥
1.53.m: Roots beginning with su are proclaimed to have an indicated svarita, marked by an indicated o; / the root duno is declared to be of seven [verbs] taking the Parasmaipada endings, O sage.

1.53.s:
aṣṭighāvanudāttetau dhātū dvau parikīrtitau /
parasmaipadinastvatra tikādyāstu caturdaśa //
1.53.d:
अष्टिघावनुदात्तेतौ धातू द्वौ परिकीर्तितौ ।
परस्मैपदिनस्त्वत्र तिकाद्यास्तु चतुर्दश ॥
1.53.m: Aṣ and tiṅ are proclaimed as two roots with an indicated anudātta; / but here fourteen roots beginning with tik take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
dvātriṃśaddhātavaḥ proktā viprendra svādike gaṇe /
svaritetaḥ ṣaṅākhyātāstudādyā munisattama //
1.53.d:
द्वात्रिंशद्धातवः प्रोक्ता विप्रेन्द्र स्वादिके गणे ।
स्वरितेतः षङाख्यातास्तुदाद्या मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.53.m: Thirty-two roots are declared in the class beginning with su, O lord of brāhmaṇas; / those beginning with tud are declared to have an indicated svarita, having an indicated ṣa, O best of sages.

1.53.s:
ṛṣyudāttejjuṣīpūrvā atmanepadinorṇavāḥ /
vraścādaya udāttetaḥ proktāḥ pañcādhikaṃ śatam //
1.53.d:
ऋष्युदात्तेज्जुषीपूर्वा अत्मनेपदिनोर्णवाः ।
व्रश्चादय उदात्तेतः प्रोक्ताः पञ्चाधिकं शतम् ॥
1.53.m: Ṛṣ has an indicated udātta; four beginning with juṣ take the Ātmanepada endings; / those beginning with vraśc have an indicated udātta and are declared to be one hundred and five.

1.53.s:
gūryudāttedihoddiṣṭo dhātureko munīśvara /
ṇūmukhāścaiva catvāraḥ parasmaipadino matāḥ //
1.53.d:
गूर्युदात्तेदिहोद्दिष्टो धातुरेको मुनीश्वर ।
णूमुखाश्चैव चत्वारः परस्मैपदिनो मताः ॥
1.53.m: Gūr is indicated here as a single root with an indicated udātta, O lord of sages; / and four roots beginning with ṇū are considered to take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
kuṅākhyātonudātteñca kuṭādyāḥ pūrtimāgatāḥ /
pṛṅ mṛṅ cātmanebhāṣau ṣaṭ parasmaipade ripeḥ //
1.53.d:
कुङाख्यातोनुदात्तेञ्च कुटाद्याः पूर्तिमागताः ।
पृङ् मृङ् चात्मनेभाषौ षट् परस्मैपदे रिपेः ॥
1.53.m: The root named kuṅ has an indicated anudātta, and those beginning with kuṭ have reached completion; / pṛṅ and mṛṅ take the Ātmanepada endings, and six from rip take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
ātmanepadino dhātū dṛṅdhṛṅdvau cāpyudāhṛtau /
pracchādiṣoḍaśākhyātāḥ parasmaipadino mune //
1.53.d:
आत्मनेपदिनो धातू दृङ्धृङ्द्वौ चाप्युदाहृतौ ।
प्रच्छादिषोडशाख्याताः परस्मैपदिनो मुने ॥
1.53.m: And the two roots dṛṅ and dhṛṅ are cited as taking the Ātmanepada endings; / sixteen roots beginning with pracch are declared to take the Parasmaipada endings, O sage.

1.53.s:
svaritetaḥ ṣaṭ tataśca proktā milamukhā mune /
kṛtīprabhṛtaya ścāpi parasmaipadinasrayaḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेतः षट् ततश्च प्रोक्ता मिलमुखा मुने ।
कृतीप्रभृतय श्चापि परस्मैपदिनस्रयः ॥
1.53.m: Then six roots beginning with mil are declared to have an indicated svarita, O sage; / and three roots beginning with kṛt take the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
sapta pañcāśadadhikāstudādau dhātavaḥ śatam /
svariteto rudhonandā parasmaibhāṣitaḥ kṛtī //
1.53.d:
सप्त पञ्चाशदधिकास्तुदादौ धातवः शतम् ।
स्वरितेतो रुधोनन्दा परस्मैभाषितः कृती ॥
1.53.m: There are one hundred and fifty-seven roots in the class beginning with tud; / nine roots from rudh have an indicated svarita, and kṛt takes the Parasmaipada endings.

1.53.s:
ñiindhīto 'nudātetasrayo dhātava īritāḥ /
udāttetaḥ śiṣapiṣarudhādyāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ //
1.53.d:
ञिइन्धीतो ऽनुदातेतस्रयो धातव ईरिताः ।
उदात्तेतः शिषपिषरुधाद्याः पञ्चविंशतिः ॥
1.53.m: Three roots beginning with ñiindhī are declared to have an indicated anudātta; / twenty-five roots, śiṣ, piṣ, and those beginning with rudh, have an indicated udātta.

1.53.s:
svaritetastanoḥ sapta dhātavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
manuvanvātmanebhāṣau svaritettkṛñudāhṛtaḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वरितेतस्तनोः सप्त धातवः परिकीर्तिताः ।
मनुवन्वात्मनेभाषौ स्वरितेत्त्कृञुदाहृतः ॥
1.53.m: Seven roots of the class beginning with tan are proclaimed to have an indicated svarita; / man and van take the Ātmanepada endings, and kṛñ is cited as having an indicated svarita.

1.53.s:
tato dvau kīrtitau vipra dhātavo daśa śābdikaiḥ /
kyādyāḥ saptobhayebhāṣāḥ sautrāḥ staṃbhvādikāstathā //
1.53.d:
ततो द्वौ कीर्तितौ विप्र धातवो दश शाब्दिकैः ।
क्याद्याः सप्तोभयेभाषाः सौत्राः स्तंभ्वादिकास्तथा ॥
1.53.m: Then, O brāhmaṇa, ten roots are proclaimed [in this group] by grammarians; / seven beginning with krī take both sets of endings; similarly the Vedic roots beginning with stambh,

1.53.s:
parasmaipadinaḥ proktāścatvāro 'pi munīśvara /
dvāviṃśatirudāttetaḥ kudhādyā dhātavo matāḥ //
1.53.d:
परस्मैपदिनः प्रोक्ताश्चत्वारो ऽपि मुनीश्वर ।
द्वाविंशतिरुदात्तेतः कुधाद्या धातवो मताः ॥
1.53.m: and four roots are declared to take the Parasmaipada endings, O lord of sages; / twenty-two roots beginning with kudh are considered to have an indicated udātta.

1.53.s:
vṛṅṅātmanepadī dhātuḥ śraṃthādyāścaikaviṃśatiḥ /
parasmaipadinaścātha svaritedgraha eva ca //
1.53.d:
वृङ्ङात्मनेपदी धातुः श्रंथाद्याश्चैकविंशतिः ।
परस्मैपदिनश्चाथ स्वरितेद्ग्रह एव च ॥
1.53.m: The root vṛṅ takes the Ātmanepada endings, and twenty-one roots beginning with śrath / take the Parasmaipada endings; and grah has an indicated svarita.

1.53.s:
rkyādikeṣu dvipañcāśaddhātavaḥ kīrtitā budhaiḥ /
curādyā dhātavo ñyantā ṣaṭrtriṃśadadhikaḥ śatam //
1.53.d:
र्क्यादिकेषु द्विपञ्चाशद्धातवः कीर्तिता बुधैः ।
चुराद्या धातवो ञ्यन्ता षट्र्त्रिंशदधिकः शतम् ॥
1.53.m: Fifty-two roots among those beginning with krī are proclaimed by the wise; / the roots beginning with cur end in the affix ṇi and are one hundred and thirty-six.

1.53.s:
cityādyaṣṭādaśākhyātā ātmanepadino mune /
carcādyā ādhṛṣīyāstu pyantā vā parikīrtitāḥ //
1.53.d:
चित्याद्यष्टादशाख्याता आत्मनेपदिनो मुने ।
चर्चाद्या आधृषीयास्तु प्यन्ता वा परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.53.m: Eighteen roots beginning with cit are declared to take the Ātmanepada endings, O sage; / those beginning with carc up to ādhṛṣ are proclaimed as optionally ending in pi.

1.53.s:
adantā dhātavaścaiva catvāriṃśattathāṣṭaṃ ca /
padādyāstu daśa proktā dhātavo hyātmanepade //
1.53.d:
अदन्ता धातवश्चैव चत्वारिंशत्तथाष्टं च ।
पदाद्यास्तु दश प्रोक्ता धातवो ह्यात्मनेपदे ॥
1.53.m: And roots ending in short a are forty-eight; / ten roots beginning with pad are declared to be in the Ātmanepada.

1.53.s:
sūtrādyā aṣṭa cāpyatra ñyantā proktā manīṣibhiḥ /
dhātvarthe prātipadikādvahulaṃ ceṣṭavanmatam //
1.53.d:
सूत्राद्या अष्ट चाप्यत्र ञ्यन्ता प्रोक्ता मनीषिभिः ।
धात्वर्थे प्रातिपदिकाद्वहुलं चेष्टवन्मतम् ॥
1.53.m: And eight roots beginning with sūtra here are declared by the wise to end in the affix ṇi; / [an affix is applied] diversely to a nominal stem in the sense of a verb, like an action.

1.53.s:
tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe hetumatyapi ṇirmataḥ /
dhātvarthe kartṛkaraṇāñcitrādyāścāpi dhātavaḥ //
1.53.d:
तत्करोति तदाचष्टे हेतुमत्यपि णिर्मतः ।
धात्वर्थे कर्तृकरणाञ्चित्राद्याश्चापि धातवः ॥
1.53.m: The affix ṇi is prescribed in the sense of 'he does that', 'he tells that', and in a causal sense; / roots beginning with citra are also formed from the agent and instrument in the sense of a verb.

1.53.s:
aṣṭa saṃgrāma ākhyāto 'nudāttecchabdikairbudhaiḥ /
stomādyāḥ ṣoḍaśa tathā andatasyaṃ nidarśanam //
1.53.d:
अष्ट संग्राम आख्यातो ऽनुदात्तेच्छब्दिकैर्बुधैः ।
स्तोमाद्याः षोडश तथा अन्दतस्यं निदर्शनम् ॥
1.53.m: The root saṃgrām is declared by learned grammarians to have an indicated anudātta, having eight [meanings]; / likewise sixteen beginning with stoma are an illustration of that ending in short a.

1.53.s:
tathā bāhulakādanye sautralaukikavaidikāḥ /
sarve sarvagaṇīyāśca tathānekārthavācinaḥ //
1.53.d:
तथा बाहुलकादन्ये सौत्रलौकिकवैदिकाः ।
सर्वे सर्वगणीयाश्च तथानेकार्थवाचिनः ॥
1.53.m: Likewise, other roots through diversity are from sūtras, worldly, or Vedic; / they all belong to all classes and likewise convey multiple meanings.

1.53.s:
sanādyantā dhātavaśca tathā vai nāmadhātavaḥ /
evamānantyamudbhāvyaṃ dhātūnāmiha nārada /
saṃkṣepo 'yaṃ samuddiṣṭo vistarastatra tatra ca //
1.53.d:
सनाद्यन्ता धातवश्च तथा वै नामधातवः ।
एवमानन्त्यमुद्भाव्यं धातूनामिह नारद ।
संक्षेपो ऽयं समुद्दिष्टो विस्तरस्तत्र तत्र च ॥
1.53.m: And [there are] verbal roots ending in san and the like, as well as nominal roots; / in this way, O Nārada, the infinity of roots is to be understood here. / This summary has been stated, and the elaboration [is found] here and there.

1.53.s:
ūdṛdantairyaunti rukṣṇuśūṅsnunukṣuściḍīṅśribhiḥ /
vṛṅvṛñbhyāṃ ca vinaikāco 'janteṣu nihatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.53.d:
ऊदृदन्तैर्यौन्ति रुक्ष्णुशूङ्स्नुनुक्षुश्चिडीङ्श्रिभिः ।
वृङ्वृञ्भ्यां च विनैकाचो ऽजन्तेषु निहताः स्मृताः ॥
1.53.m: Except for roots ending in ū and ṛ, [and except for] yā, yu, ru, kṣnu, śūṅ, snu, nu, kṣu, śvī, ḍīṅ, and śri, / and without vṛṅ and vṛñ, the monosyllabic roots among vowel-ending ones are taught as unaccented [aniṭ].

1.53.s:
śaklapacmucārcvacvicsicpracchityajnijir bhajaḥ /
bhañjbhujbhrasjmatjiyajyujrujrañjavijirsvañjisañjsṛjaḥ //
1.53.d:
शक्लपच्मुचार्च्वच्विच्सिच्प्रच्छित्यज्निजिर् भजः ।
भञ्ज्भुज्भ्रस्ज्मत्जियज्युज्रुज्रञ्जविजिर्स्वञ्जिसञ्ज्सृजः ॥
1.53.m: Śakl, pac, muc, ric, vac, vic, sic, pracch, tyaj, nij, bhaj, / bhañj, bhuj, bhrajj, majj, yaj, yuj, ruj, rañj, vij, svañj, sañj, and sṛj;

1.53.s:
adkṣudkhidchidtudinudaḥ padyabhidvidyatirvinad /
śadsadī svidyatiḥskandirhadī krudhkṣudhibudhyatī //
1.53.d:
अद्क्षुद्खिद्छिद्तुदिनुदः पद्यभिद्विद्यतिर्विनद् ।
शद्सदी स्विद्यतिःस्कन्दिर्हदी क्रुध्क्षुधिबुध्यती ॥
1.53.m: ad, kṣud, khid, chid, tud, nud, pad, bhid, vid, vyadh, vinad, / śad, sad, svid, skand, had, krudh, kṣudh, and budh;

1.53.s:
bandhiryudhirudhīrādhivyadhśudhaḥ sādhisidhyatī /
manyahannāpkṣipchupitaptipastṛpyatidṛpyatī //
1.53.d:
बन्धिर्युधिरुधीराधिव्यध्शुधः साधिसिध्यती ।
मन्यहन्नाप्क्षिप्छुपितप्तिपस्तृप्यतिदृप्यती ॥
1.53.m: bandh, yudh, rudh, rādh, vyadh, śudh, sādh, sidh, / man, han, āp, kṣip, chup, tap, tip, tṛp, dṛp;

1.53.s:
libluvvapūśapsvapūsṛpiyabharabhagamnamyamo rabhiḥ /
kruśirdaṃśidiśī dṛśmṛśriruśliśviśspṛśaḥ kṛṣiḥ //
1.53.d:
लिब्लुव्वपूशप्स्वपूसृपियभरभगम्नम्यमो रभिः ।
क्रुशिर्दंशिदिशी दृश्मृश्रिरुश्लिश्विश्स्पृशः कृषिः ॥
1.53.m: lip, lup, vap, śap, svap, sṛp, yabh, rabh, gam, nam, yam, rabh, / kruś, daṃś, diś, dṛś, mṛś, ruś, liś, viś, spṛś, kṛṣ;

1.53.s:
tviṣṭuṣduṣpuṣyapiṣviṣśiṣśuṣśliṣyatayo ghasiḥ /
vasatirdahadihiduho nahmihruhlihvahistathā //
1.53.d:
त्विष्टुष्दुष्पुष्यपिष्विष्शिष्शुष्श्लिष्यतयो घसिः ।
वसतिर्दहदिहिदुहो नह्मिह्रुह्लिह्वहिस्तथा ॥
1.53.m: tviṣ, tuṣ, duṣ, puṣ, piṣ, viṣ, śiṣ, śuṣ, śliṣ, ghas, / vas, dah, dih, duh, nah, mih, ruh, lih, and vah—

1.53.s:
anudāttā halanteṣu dhātavo dvyadhikaṃ śatam /
cādyā nipātā gavayaḥ prādyā digdeśakālajāḥ //
1.53.d:
अनुदात्ता हलन्तेषु धातवो द्व्यधिकं शतम् ।
चाद्या निपाता गवयः प्राद्या दिग्देशकालजाः ॥
1.53.m: these consonant-ending roots are anudātta [aniṭ], one hundred and two [in number]. / The particles beginning with ca, gavaya, and those beginning with pra; words born of direction, region, and time,

1.53.s:
śabdāḥ proktā hyanekārthāḥ sarvaliṅgā api dvija /
gaṇapāṭhaḥ sūtrapāṭho dhātupāṭhastathaiva ca //
1.53.d:
शब्दाः प्रोक्ता ह्यनेकार्थाः सर्वलिङ्गा अपि द्विज ।
गणपाठः सूत्रपाठो धातुपाठस्तथैव च ॥
1.53.m: are indeed proclaimed as polysemous, and occurring in all genders, O twice-born one. / The recitation of the word-lists, the recitation of sūtras, and likewise the recitation of roots,

1.53.s:
pāṭhonunāsikānāṃ ca parāyaṇamihocyate /
śabdāḥ siddhā vaidikāstu laukikāścāpi nārada //
1.53.d:
पाठोनुनासिकानां च परायणमिहोच्यते ।
शब्दाः सिद्धा वैदिकास्तु लौकिकाश्चापि नारद ॥
1.53.m: and the recitation of nasalised vowels is called the comprehensive study [śabdapārāyaṇa] here. / The words established [by them] are both Vedic and worldly, O Nārada.

1.53.s:
śabdapārāyaṇaṃ tasmātkāraṇaṃ śabdasaṃgrahe /
laghumārgeṇa śabdānāṃ sādhūnāṃ saṃnirūpaṇam //
1.53.d:
शब्दपारायणं तस्मात्कारणं शब्दसंग्रहे ।
लघुमार्गेण शब्दानां साधूनां संनिरूपणम् ॥
1.53.m: Therefore, the comprehensive study of words is the cause in gathering words. / The determination of correct words by a concise method,

1.53.s: prakṛtipratyayādeśalopāgamamukhaiḥ kṛtam //
1.53.d: प्रकृतिप्रत्ययादेशलोपागममुखैः कृतम् ॥
1.53.m: is accomplished by means of base, suffix, substitution, elision, and augment.

1.53.s:
itthametatsamākhyātaṃ niruktaṃ kiñcidevate /
kātsnyerna vaktumānantyātko 'piśakto na nārada //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇa pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde niruktalakṣaṇanirūpaṇaṃ nāma tripañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.53.d:
इत्थमेतत्समाख्यातं निरुक्तं किञ्चिदेवते ।
कात्स्न्येर्न वक्तुमानन्त्यात्को ऽपिशक्तो न नारद ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराण पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे निरुक्तलक्षणनिरूपणं नाम त्रिपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.53.m:
Thus has this Nirukta been expounded to you in brief; / due to its endlessness, no one at all is capable of declaring it completely, O Nārada.

Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Characteristics of Nirukta,' in the second quarter of the Bṛhad-upākhyāna in the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.54.s:
sanandana uvāca
jyotiṣāṅgaṃ pravakṣyāmi yaduktaṃ brahmaṇā purā /
yasya vijñāna mātreṇa dharmasiddhirbhavennṛṇām //
1.54.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
ज्योतिषाङ्गं प्रवक्ष्यामि यदुक्तं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ।
यस्य विज्ञान मात्रेण धर्मसिद्धिर्भवेन्नृणाम् ॥
1.54.m: Sanandana said: / I shall declare the limb [of the Veda] that is Jyotiṣa, which was spoken by Brahmā of old, / merely by the knowledge of which the attainment of dharma occurs for men.

1.54.s:
triskandhaṃ jyautiṣāṃ śāstraṃ caturlakṣamudāhṛtam /
gaṇitaṃ jātakaṃ vipra saṃhitāskandhasaṃjñitāḥ //
1.54.d:
त्रिस्कन्धं ज्यौतिषां शास्त्रं चतुर्लक्षमुदाहृतम् ।
गणितं जातकं विप्र संहितास्कन्धसंज्ञिताः ॥
1.54.m: The treatise on astronomy-astrology having three branches is said to consist of four hundred thousand [verses]. / Mathematics [Gaṇita], Horoscopy [Jātaka], and Saṃhitā are designated as the branches, O brahmin.

1.54.s:
gaṇite parikarmādi khagamadhyasphuṭakriṃye /
anuyogaścandrasūryagrahaṇaṃ tacodasyākam //
1.54.d:
गणिते परिकर्मादि खगमध्यस्फुटक्रिंये ।
अनुयोगश्चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहणं तचोदस्याकम् ॥
1.54.m: In mathematics, the operations and so forth, the computation of the mean and true planets, / the question-and-answer, the solar and lunar eclipses, the rising and setting of planets,

1.54.s:
chāyā śṛṅgonnatiyutī pātasādhānamīritam /
jātake rāśibhedāśca grahayoniśca yonijam //
1.54.d:
छाया शृङ्गोन्नतियुती पातसाधानमीरितम् ।
जातके राशिभेदाश्च ग्रहयोनिश्च योनिजम् ॥
1.54.m: the shadow, the elevation of the moon's cusps, conjunction, and determination of planetary nodes are spoken of. / In horoscopy, the divisions of zodiacal signs, the origin of planets, origin [of beings],

1.54.s:
niṣekajanmāriṣṭāni hyāyurdāyo daśākramaḥ /
karmājīvaṃ cāṣṭavargo rājayogāśca nābhasāḥ //
1.54.d:
निषेकजन्मारिष्टानि ह्यायुर्दायो दशाक्रमः ।
कर्माजीवं चाष्टवर्गो राजयोगाश्च नाभसाः ॥
1.54.m: conception, birth, afflictions [ariṣṭa], the lifespan, the order of planetary periods [daśā], / professional livelihood, the aṣṭakavarga, and the royal and celestial yogas,

1.54.s:
candrayogāḥ pravrajyākhyā rāśiśīlaṃ ca dṛkphalam /
grahabhāvaphalaṃ caivāśrayayogaprakīrṇake //
1.54.d:
चन्द्रयोगाः प्रव्रज्याख्या राशिशीलं च दृक्फलम् ।
ग्रहभावफलं चैवाश्रययोगप्रकीर्णके ॥
1.54.m: the lunar yogas, asceticism [renunciation], the disposition of signs, the result of aspects, / the results of planetary houses, the planetary shelter yogas, and miscellaneous matters,

1.54.s:
aniṣṭayogāḥ srījanmapalaṃ niryāṇameva ca /
naṣṭajanmavidhānaṃ ca tathā dreṣkāṇalakṣaṇam //
1.54.d:
अनिष्टयोगाः स्रीजन्मपलं निर्याणमेव च ।
नष्टजन्मविधानं च तथा द्रेष्काणलक्षणम् ॥
1.54.m: inauspicious yogas, the results of female horoscopy, death itself, / the method for lost horoscopes, and the characteristics of decanates [dreṣkāṇa] [are treated].

1.54.s:
saṃhitāśāstrarūpaṃ ca grahacāro 'bdalakṣaṇam /
tithivāsaranakṣatrayogatithyarddhasaṃjñakāḥ //
1.54.d:
संहिताशास्त्ररूपं च ग्रहचारो ऽब्दलक्षणम् ।
तिथिवासरनक्षत्रयोगतिथ्यर्द्धसंज्ञकाः ॥
1.54.m: The nature of the Saṃhitā treatise comprises the motion of planets, the characteristics of years, / the tithis, weekdays, asterisms, yogas, and half-tithis [karaṇas],

1.54.s:
muhūrtopagrahāḥ sūyasaṃkrāntirgocaraḥ kramāt /
candratā rābalaṃ caiva sarvalagrārtavāhvayaḥ //
1.54.d:
मुहूर्तोपग्रहाः सूयसंक्रान्तिर्गोचरः क्रमात् ।
चन्द्रता राबलं चैव सर्वलग्रार्तवाह्वयः ॥
1.54.m: the muhūrtas, secondary planets, solar ingress, transits in due order, / the strength of the moon and stars, the ascendant of all matters, seasonal periods,

1.54.s:
ādhānapuṃsasīmantajātanāmānnabhuktayaḥ /
caulaṅkarṇyayaṇaṃ maiñjī kṣurikābandhanaṃ tathā //
1.54.d:
आधानपुंससीमन्तजातनामान्नभुक्तयः ।
चौलङ्कर्ण्ययणं मैञ्जी क्षुरिकाबन्धनं तथा ॥
1.54.m: impregnation, pumsavana, parting the hair, birth-rites, naming, first feeding, / tonsure, piercing the ears, the sacred girdle, and the investiture of the dagger,

1.54.s:
samāvartinavaivāhapratiṣṭāsadmalakṣaṇam /
yātrāpraveśanaṃ sadyovṛṣṭiḥ karmavilakṣaṇam //
1.54.d:
समावर्तिनवैवाहप्रतिष्टासद्मलक्षणम् ।
यात्राप्रवेशनं सद्योवृष्टिः कर्मविलक्षणम् ॥
1.54.m: graduation from studentship, marriage, consecration, the characteristics of houses, / journeys, house-entering, immediate rainfall, different rites,

1.54.s:
utpattilakṣaṇaṃ caiva sarvaṃ saṃkṣepato bruve /
ekaṃ daśa śataṃ caiva sahasrāyutalakṣakam //
1.54.d:
उत्पत्तिलक्षणं चैव सर्वं संक्षेपतो ब्रुवे ।
एकं दश शतं चैव सहस्रायुतलक्षकम् ॥
1.54.m: and the characteristics of portents: all this I declare in brief. / One, ten, one hundred, one thousand, ten thousand, one hundred thousand,

1.54.s:
prayutaṃ koṭisaṃjñāṃ cārbudamabjaṃ ca rarvavakam /
niravarva ca mahāpadmaṃ śaṅkurjaladhireva ca //
1.54.d:
प्रयुतं कोटिसंज्ञां चार्बुदमब्जं च रर्ववकम् ।
निरवर्व च महापद्मं शङ्कुर्जलधिरेव च ॥
1.54.m: one million, that named ten million [koṭi], one hundred million, one billion, ten billion, / one hundred billion, one trillion, ten trillion, one hundred trillion,

1.54.s:
atyaṃ madhyaṃ parārddhaṃ ca saṃjñā daśaguṇottarāḥ /
kramādutkramato vāpi yogaḥ kāryottaraṃ tathā //
1.54.d:
अत्यं मध्यं परार्द्धं च संज्ञा दशगुणोत्तराः ।
क्रमादुत्क्रमतो वापि योगः कार्योत्तरं तथा ॥
1.54.m: one quadrillion, ten quadrillion, and one hundred quadrillion: these denominations increase tenfold successively. / In order or in reverse order, addition and subtraction are to be performed.

1.54.s:
hanyādguṇena guṇyaṃ syāttainaivopāntimādikān /
śuddheddharoyadguṇaścabhājyāntyāttatphalaṃ mune //
1.54.d:
हन्याद्गुणेन गुण्यं स्यात्तैनैवोपान्तिमादिकान् ।
शुद्धेद्धरोयद्गुणश्चभाज्यान्त्यात्तत्फलं मुने ॥
1.54.m: One should multiply the multiplicand by the multiplier, and by that very [multiplier] the penultimate and subsequent places. / Whatever multiplier times the divisor clears [the dividend], that is the quotient from the end of the dividend, O sage.

1.54.s:
samāṅkato 'tho vargasyāttamevāhuḥ kṛtiṃ budhāḥ /
antyāttu viṣamāttyaktvā kṛtiṃ mūlaṃnyasetpṛthak //
1.54.d:
समाङ्कतो ऽथो वर्गस्यात्तमेवाहुः कृतिं बुधाः ।
अन्त्यात्तु विषमात्त्यक्त्वा कृतिं मूलंन्यसेत्पृथक् ॥
1.54.m: From the square of equal numbers comes the square [varga]; the wise indeed call that the square. / Having subtracted the square from the last odd place, one should set down the root separately.

1.54.s:
dviguṇenāmunā bhakte phalaṃ mūle nyasetkramāt /
tatkṛtiṃ ca tyajedvipra mūlena vibhajetpunaḥ //
1.54.d:
द्विगुणेनामुना भक्ते फलं मूले न्यसेत्क्रमात् ।
तत्कृतिं च त्यजेद्विप्र मूलेन विभजेत्पुनः ॥
1.54.m: When divided by double that [root], one should place the quotient in the root in order; / and one should subtract its square, O brahmin, and divide again by the root.

1.54.s:
evaṃ muhurvargamūlaṃ jāyate ca munīśvara /
samatryaṅkahatiḥ prokto ghanastatravidhiḥ pade //
1.54.d:
एवं मुहुर्वर्गमूलं जायते च मुनीश्वर ।
समत्र्यङ्कहतिः प्रोक्तो घनस्तत्रविधिः पदे ॥
1.54.m: In this way, the square root is produced repeatedly, O lord of sages. / The product of three equal numbers is declared to be the cube; the rule regarding the places therein [is as follows]:

1.54.s:
procyate viṣamaṃ tvādyaṃ same dve ca tataḥ param /
viśodhyaṃ viṣamādantyāddhanaṃ tanmūlamucyate //
1.54.d:
प्रोच्यते विषमं त्वाद्यं समे द्वे च ततः परम् ।
विशोध्यं विषमादन्त्याद्धनं तन्मूलमुच्यते ॥
1.54.m: The first place is called odd, and the next two places are even; / the cube is to be subtracted from the last odd place; its root is spoken of [separately].

1.54.s:
trighnādbhajanmūlakṛtyā samaṃ mūle nyasetphalam /
tatkṛtitvena nihatānnighnīṃ cāpi viśodhayet //
1.54.d:
त्रिघ्नाद्भजन्मूलकृत्या समं मूले न्यसेत्फलम् ।
तत्कृतित्वेन निहतान्निघ्नीं चापि विशोधयेत् ॥
1.54.m: From dividing by three times the square of the root, one should place the quotient in the root for the even place; / and one should subtract the product of its square and [thrice the root],

1.54.s:
ghanaṃ ca viṣamādevaṃ ghanamūlaṃ murhubhavet /
anyonyahāranihatau harāṃśau tu samucchidā //
1.54.d:
घनं च विषमादेवं घनमूलं मुर्हुभवेत् ।
अन्योन्यहारनिहतौ हरांशौ तु समुच्छिदा ॥
1.54.m: and the cube from the odd place; thus repeatedly the cube root arises. / When the numerator and denominator are multiplied reciprocally by the denominator, they have a common divisor.

1.54.s:
lavā lavaghnāśca harā haraghnā hi savarṇanam /
bhāgaprabhāge vijñeyaṃ mune śāsrārthacintakaiḥ //
1.54.d:
लवा लवघ्नाश्च हरा हरघ्ना हि सवर्णनम् ।
भागप्रभागे विज्ञेयं मुने शास्रार्थचिन्तकैः ॥
1.54.m: Numerators multiplied by numerators and denominators multiplied by denominators constitute reduction to a common fraction; / this should be known in fractions and subfractions, O sage, by thinkers on the meaning of the treatises.

1.54.s:
anubandhe 'pavāhe caikasya cedadhikonakaḥ /
bhāgāstalasthahāreṇa haraṃ svāṃśādhikena tān //
1.54.d:
अनुबन्धे ऽपवाहे चैकस्य चेदधिकोनकः ।
भागास्तलस्थहारेण हरं स्वांशाधिकेन तान् ॥
1.54.m: In addition and subtraction of fractions, if one fraction is greater or smaller than another, / [multiply] the fractions by the denominator beneath, and multiply the denominator by that [denominator] increased by its own numerator,

1.54.s:
ūnena cāpi guṇayeddhanarṇaṃ cintayettathā /
kāryastulyaharāṃ śānāṃ yogaścāpyantato mune //
1.54.d:
ऊनेन चापि गुणयेद्धनर्णं चिन्तयेत्तथा ।
कार्यस्तुल्यहरां शानां योगश्चाप्यन्ततो मुने ॥
1.54.m: or by that decreased [by its numerator], and one should consider positive and negative likewise; / and addition of fractions with equal denominators is to be performed at the end, O sage.

1.54.s:
ahārarāśau rūpyaṃ tu kalpayeddharamapyathā /
aṃśāhatiśchedaghātahṛdbhinnaguṇane phalam //
1.54.d:
अहारराशौ रूप्यं तु कल्पयेद्धरमप्यथा ।
अंशाहतिश्छेदघातहृद्भिन्नगुणने फलम् ॥
1.54.m: In an un-fractional quantity, one should suppose the denominator to be unity. / The product of numerators divided by the product of denominators is the result in multiplication of fractions.

1.54.s:
chedaṃ cāpi lavaṃ vidvanparivartya harasya ca /
śeṣaḥ kāryo bhāgahāre kartavyo guṇanāvidhiḥ //
1.54.d:
छेदं चापि लवं विद्वन्परिवर्त्य हरस्य च ।
शेषः कार्यो भागहारे कर्तव्यो गुणनाविधिः ॥
1.54.m: Having inverted the denominator and numerator of the divisor, O wise one, / the rest of the operation is to be done in division: the procedure of multiplication is to be executed.

1.54.s:
hārāṃśayoḥ kṛtī varge ghanau ghanavidhau mune /
padasiddhyai pade kuryādathoravaṃ sarvataśca ravam //
1.54.d:
हारांशयोः कृती वर्गे घनौ घनविधौ मुने ।
पदसिद्ध्यै पदे कुर्यादथोरवं सर्वतश्च रवम् ॥
1.54.m: The squares of the denominator and numerator [are taken] in squaring, and their cubes in the operation of cubing, O sage; / for the purpose of finding the root, one should extract the root; so too in every operation.

1.54.s:
chedaṃ guṇaṃ guṇaṃ chedaṃ vargaṃ mūlaṃ padaṃ kṛtim /
ṛṇaṃ svaṃ svamṛṇaṃ kuryādṛśye rāśiprasiddhaye //
1.54.d:
छेदं गुणं गुणं छेदं वर्गं मूलं पदं कृतिम् ।
ऋणं स्वं स्वमृणं कुर्यादृश्ये राशिप्रसिद्धये ॥
1.54.m: Make the divisor a multiplier, the multiplier a divisor, the square a square root, the root a square, / negative positive, and positive negative, in the visible quantity, in order to determine the [unknown] quantity.

1.54.s:
atha svāṃśādhikone tu lavāḍhyo no haro haraḥ /
aṃśastvavikṛtastatra vilome śeṣamuktavat //
1.54.d:
अथ स्वांशाधिकोने तु लवाढ्यो नो हरो हरः ।
अंशस्त्वविकृतस्तत्र विलोमे शेषमुक्तवत् ॥
1.54.m: Now, when increased or decreased by its own fraction, the denominator increased or decreased by the numerator becomes the denominator, / while the numerator remains unchanged; in the inverse method, the rest is as previously stated.

1.54.s:
uddiṣṭārāśiḥ saṃkṣiptau hṛtoṃ'śai rahito yutaḥ /
iṣṭaghnadṛṣṭenaitena bhaktarāśiranīśitaḥ //
1.54.d:
उद्दिष्टाराशिः संक्षिप्तौ हृतोंऽशै रहितो युतः ।
इष्टघ्नदृष्टेनैतेन भक्तराशिरनीशितः ॥
1.54.m: A designated quantity, reduced, divided, diminished, or increased by its fractions: / that quantity divided by this given value multiplied by the assumed value is determined.

1.54.s:
yogontareṇonayutodvitorāśītasaṃkrame /
rāśyantarahṛtaṃ vargottaraṃ yosutaśca tau //
1.54.d:
योगोन्तरेणोनयुतोद्वितोराशीतसंक्रमे ।
राश्यन्तरहृतं वर्गोत्तरं योसुतश्च तौ ॥
1.54.m: In the transit of two quantities, the sum is decreased or increased by the difference; / the difference of squares divided by the difference of the two quantities gives their sum.

1.54.s:
gajagrīṣṭakṛtirvyaikā dalitā ceṣṭabhājitā /
eko 'sya vargo dalitaḥ saiko rāśiḥ paro mataḥ //
1.54.d:
गजग्रीष्टकृतिर्व्यैका दलिता चेष्टभाजिता ।
एको ऽस्य वर्गो दलितः सैको राशिः परो मतः ॥
1.54.m: The square of an assumed number minus one, halved and divided by the assumed number, [gives one quantity]; / one square of this halved, increased by one, is regarded as the other quantity.

1.54.s:
dviguṇeṣṭahṛtaṃ rūpaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prāgrūpakaṃ param /
vargayogāntare vyeke rāśyorvargosta etayoḥ //
1.54.d:
द्विगुणेष्टहृतं रूपं श्रेष्ठं प्राग्रूपकं परम् ।
वर्गयोगान्तरे व्येके राश्योर्वर्गोस्त एतयोः ॥
