1.54.m: Unity divided by twice the assumed number is the first best value; the other is the former unit; / when the sum and difference of the squares are decreased by one, the square of these two quantities [is obtained].

1.54.s:
iṣṭavagekṛtiśceṣṭaghanoṣṭagrau ca saukakau /
eṣīsyānāmubhe vyakte gaṇite vyaktameva ca //
1.54.d:
इष्टवगेकृतिश्चेष्टघनोष्टग्रौ च सौककौ ।
एषीस्यानामुभे व्यक्ते गणिते व्यक्तमेव च ॥
1.54.m: The desired square, square root, desired cube, and cube roots are thus calculated; / both these manifest quantities are indeed clearly understood in arithmetic.

1.54.s:
guṇaghnamūlonayutaḥ saguṇārddhe kṛtaṃ padam /
dṛṣṭasya ca guṇārddho na yutaṃ vargīkṛtaṃ guṇaḥ //
1.54.d:
गुणघ्नमूलोनयुतः सगुणार्द्धे कृतं पदम् ।
दृष्टस्य च गुणार्द्धो न युतं वर्गीकृतं गुणः ॥
1.54.m: Diminished or increased by the square root multiplied by a factor, the square root of that which is combined with half the coefficient squared / of the known quantity, diminished or increased by half the coefficient and squared, yields the coefficient.

1.54.s:
yadā lavonapumrāśirdṛśyaṃ bhāgonayugbhuvā /
bhaktaṃ tathā mūlaguṇaṃ tābhyāṃ sādhyotha vyaktavat //
1.54.d:
यदा लवोनपुम्राशिर्दृश्यं भागोनयुग्भुवा ।
भक्तं तथा मूलगुणं ताभ्यां साध्योथ व्यक्तवत् ॥
1.54.m: When a quantity is decreased by a fraction, the visible amount divided by the earth [unity] diminished or increased by the fraction, / multiplied likewise by the square root, is solved by these two just like a known quantity.

1.54.s:
pramāṇecche sajātīye ādyante madhaayagaṃ phalam /
icchaghnamādyahṛtseṣṭaṃ phalaṃ vyaste viparyayāt //
1.54.d:
प्रमाणेच्छे सजातीये आद्यन्ते मधअयगं फलम् ।
इच्छघ्नमाद्यहृत्सेष्टं फलं व्यस्ते विपर्ययात् ॥
1.54.m: The standard [measure] and the requisition are of the same kind, placed at the beginning and the end, with the fruit in the middle. / The fruit multiplied by the requisition and divided by the initial [measure] is the desired fruit; in the inverse rule, it is reversed.

1.54.s:
pañcarāsyādike 'nyonyapakṣaṃ kṛtvā phalacchidām /
bahurāśivadhaṃ bhakte phalaṃ svalpavadhena ca //
1.54.d:
पञ्चरास्यादिके ऽन्योन्यपक्षं कृत्वा फलच्छिदाम् ।
बहुराशिवधं भक्ते फलं स्वल्पवधेन च ॥
1.54.m: In the rule of five and the rest, having interchanged the sides of the denominators of the fruits, / when the product of the many quantities is divided by the product of the few, the fruit [is obtained].

1.54.s:
iṣṭakarmavadhemūlaṃ cyutaṃ miśrātkalāntare /
mānaghnakālaścātītakālāghnaphalasaṃhṛtāḥ //
1.54.d:
इष्टकर्मवधेमूलं च्युतं मिश्रात्कलान्तरे ।
मानघ्नकालश्चातीतकालाघ्नफलसंहृताः ॥
1.54.m: In the operation of interest, the square root of the product, subtracted from the mixed capital-interest at the interval of interest, / the time multiplied by the principal, and divided by the fruit multiplied by the elapsed time:

1.54.s:
svayogabhaktānighnāḥ syuḥ saṃprayuktadalāni ca /
bahurāśipalātsvalparāśimāsaphalaṃ bahu //
1.54.d:
स्वयोगभक्तानिघ्नाः स्युः संप्रयुक्तदलानि च ।
बहुराशिपलात्स्वल्पराशिमासफलं बहु ॥
1.54.m: divided by their sum and multiplied [by the total], they are the portions of the capital lent. / If the monthly yield of a small amount from a large amount is large,

1.54.s:
cedrāśivivaraṃ māsaphalāntarahṛtaṃ ca yaḥ /
kṣepā miśrahatāḥ kṣepoyogabhaktāḥ phalāni ca //
1.54.d:
चेद्राशिविवरं मासफलान्तरहृतं च यः ।
क्षेपा मिश्रहताः क्षेपोयोगभक्ताः फलानि च ॥
1.54.m: then the difference between the two amounts is divided by the difference between the monthly yields; / and the investments multiplied by the mixed sum, divided by the sum of the investments, are the fruits [shares].

1.54.s:
bhajecchidāeṃśaistairmiśrai rūpaṃ kālaśca pūrtikṛt /
pūrṇogacchetsamedhyavyesamevargorddhitetyataḥ //
1.54.d:
भजेच्छिदाएंशैस्तैर्मिश्रै रूपं कालश्च पूर्तिकृत् ।
पूर्णोगच्छेत्समेध्यव्येसमेवर्गोर्द्धितेत्यतः ॥
1.54.m: One should divide unity by those mixed fractions, and that becomes the completing time. / When the total period is even, [one halves it]; when odd, [one subtracts one], and thus from squaring and halving:

1.54.s:
vyastaṃ gacchataṃ phalaṃ yadguṇavargaṃ bhacahi tat /
vyekaṃ vyekaguṇāptaṃ ca prādhnaṃ mānaṃ guṇottare //
1.54.d:
व्यस्तं गच्छतं फलं यद्गुणवर्गं भचहि तत् ।
व्येकं व्येकगुणाप्तं च प्राध्नं मानं गुणोत्तरे ॥
1.54.m: The inverse power of the period, which is the square of the common ratio, / diminished by one and divided by the common ratio less one, and multiplied by the first term, is the measure in a geometric progression.

1.54.s:
bhujakoṭikṛtiyogamūlaṃ karṇaśca dorbhavet /
śrutikṛtyantarapada koṭirdoḥ karṇavargayoḥ //
1.54.d:
भुजकोटिकृतियोगमूलं कर्णश्च दोर्भवेत् ।
श्रुतिकृत्यन्तरपद कोटिर्दोः कर्णवर्गयोः ॥
1.54.m: The square root of the sum of the squares of the base and the upright is the hypotenuse, and [similarly] the base is found. / The upright is the square root of the difference between the squares of the hypotenuse and the base.

1.54.s:
viṃvarāttatkarṇapadaṃ kṣetre tricaturasrake /
rāśyorantaravargeṇa dvighne ghāte yute tayoḥ //
1.54.d:
विंवरात्तत्कर्णपदं क्षेत्रे त्रिचतुरस्रके ।
राश्योरन्तरवर्गेण द्विघ्ने घाते युते तयोः ॥
1.54.m: From the difference of the squares of the two, the square root is the hypotenuse in a triangular or quadrilateral figure. / When twice their product is added to the square of the difference between two quantities,

1.54.s:
vargayogotha yogāntahṝntirvargāntaraṃ bhavet /
vyāsa ākṛtisaṃkṣaṇṇovyāsāsyātparidhirmune //
1.54.d:
वर्गयोगोथ योगान्तहॄन्तिर्वर्गान्तरं भवेत् ।
व्यास आकृतिसंक्षण्णोव्यासास्यात्परिधिर्मुने ॥
1.54.m: that is the sum of their squares; and the product of the sum and difference is the difference of their squares. / The diameter multiplied by the square root of ten is the circumference, O sage.

1.54.s:
jyāvyāsayogavivarāhatamūlonito 'rddhitaḥ /
vyāsaḥ śaraḥ śaronāñca vyāsāccharaguṇātpadam //
1.54.d:
ज्याव्यासयोगविवराहतमूलोनितो ऽर्द्धितः ।
व्यासः शरः शरोनाञ्च व्यासाच्छरगुणात्पदम् ॥
1.54.m: The diameter diminished by the square root of the product of the sum and difference of the chord and the diameter, and halved, / is the arrow; and the square root of the diameter diminished by the arrow, multiplied by the arrow,

1.54.s:
dvighnaṃ jīvātha jīvārddhavarge śarahṛte yute /
vyāsoṣṭatebhavedevaṃ proktaṃ gaṇitakovidaiḥ //
1.54.d:
द्विघ्नं जीवाथ जीवार्द्धवर्गे शरहृते युते ।
व्यासोष्टतेभवेदेवं प्रोक्तं गणितकोविदैः ॥
1.54.m: doubled, is the chord; then, when the square of half the chord is divided by the arrow and added [to the arrow], / it becomes the diameter. Thus has it been declared by those learned in calculation.

1.54.s:
cāponanighnaḥ paridhiḥ pragaṅlaḥ paridheḥ kṛte /
turyāṃśena śaradhnenāgheninādhaṃ caturgaṇam //
1.54.d:
चापोननिघ्नः परिधिः प्रगङ्लः परिधेः कृते ।
तुर्यांशेन शरध्नेनाघेनिनाधं चतुर्गणम् ॥
1.54.m: The circumference diminished by the arc, multiplied by [the arc], is the first factor. / Four times [the product of the diameter and arc] divided by one-fourth of the square of the circumference diminished by that product,

1.54.s:
vyāsadhnaṃ prabhajedvipra jyā kāśaṃ jāyate sphuṭā /
jyāṅghrīṣudhnovṛttavargobagdhighnavyāsāḍhyamaurvihṛt //
1.54.d:
व्यासध्नं प्रभजेद्विप्र ज्या काशं जायते स्फुटा ।
ज्याङ्घ्रीषुध्नोवृत्तवर्गोबग्धिघ्नव्यासाढ्यमौर्विहृत् ॥
1.54.m: and multiplied by the diameter, should be divided, O brahmin; the accurate chord is produced. / The square of the circumference multiplied by one-fourth of the chord, divided by the chord increased by four times the diameter,

1.54.s:
labdhonavṛttavargādripaderdhātpatite dhanuḥ /
sthūlamadhyāpṛvannavedho vṛttāṅkāśeṣabhāgikaḥ //
1.54.d:
लब्धोनवृत्तवर्गाद्रिपदेर्धात्पतिते धनुः ।
स्थूलमध्यापृवन्नवेधो वृत्ताङ्काशेषभागिकः ॥
1.54.m: subtracted from the square of the circumference, its fourth part subtracted from half, gives the arc. / The depth is taken as rough, intermediate, and broad, divided into nine equal parts.

1.54.s:
vṛttāṅgāṃśakṛtirvedhaniprīyanakarāmitau /
vārivyāsahataṃ dairdhyaṃvedhāṅgulahataṃ punaḥ //
1.54.d:
वृत्ताङ्गांशकृतिर्वेधनिप्रीयनकरामितौ ।
वारिव्यासहतं दैर्ध्यंवेधाङ्गुलहतं पुनः ॥
1.54.m: The square of a fraction of the circumference measured by cubits according to depth: / the length multiplied by the diameter of the water, and further multiplied by the digits of the depth,

1.54.s:
kharavendurāmavihataṃ mānaṃ droṇādivāriṇaḥ /
vistārāyāmavedhānāṃmaṅgulyonyanāḍighnāḥ //
1.54.d:
खरवेन्दुरामविहतं मानं द्रोणादिवारिणः ।
विस्तारायामवेधानांमङ्गुल्योन्यनाडिघ्नाः ॥
1.54.m: divided by three thousand one hundred and twenty, is the measure of the water in droṇas and the like. / The digits of the breadth, length, and depth multiplied together,

1.54.s:
rasāṃkābhrābdhibhirbhaktā dhānye droṇādikāmitiḥ /
utsedhavyāsadairdhyāṇāmaṅgulyānyasya no dvija //
1.54.d:
रसांकाभ्राब्धिभिर्भक्ता धान्ये द्रोणादिकामितिः ।
उत्सेधव्यासदैर्ध्याणामङ्गुल्यान्यस्य नो द्विज ॥
1.54.m: and divided by four thousand and ninety-six, is the measure of grain in droṇas and the like. / The digits of height, diameter, and length of another [vessel], O twice-born,

1.54.s:
mithoghnāti bhajetsvākṣeśairdreṇādimitirbhavet /
vistārādyaṃ gulānyevaṃ mithoghnānyapasāṃbhavet //
1.54.d:
मिथोघ्नाति भजेत्स्वाक्षेशैर्द्रेणादिमितिर्भवेत् ।
विस्ताराद्यं गुलान्येवं मिथोघ्नान्यपसांभवेत् ॥
1.54.m: multiplied together and divided by five hundred and twenty, yields the measure in droṇas and the like. / Likewise, the digits of breadth and the like multiplied together for liquids,

1.54.s:
vāṇebhamārgaṇairlabdhaṃ droṇādyaṃ mānamādiśet /
dīpaśaṅkutalacchidraghnaḥ śaṅkurbhaivaṃbhavenmune //
1.54.d:
वाणेभमार्गणैर्लब्धं द्रोणाद्यं मानमादिशेत् ।
दीपशङ्कुतलच्छिद्रघ्नः शङ्कुर्भैवंभवेन्मुने ॥
1.54.m: divided by five hundred and eighty-five, gives the measure in droṇas and the rest. / The gnomon multiplied by the distance between the lamp and the base of the gnomon is the shadow, O sage;

1.54.s:
narona dīpakaśikhaucyabhakto hyatha bhodvane /
śaṅkaunṛdīpādhaśchidraghnairdīpauccyaṃ narānvite //
1.54.d:
नरोन दीपकशिखौच्यभक्तो ह्यथ भोद्वने ।
शङ्कौनृदीपाधश्छिद्रघ्नैर्दीपौच्च्यं नरान्विते ॥
1.54.m: divided by the height of the tip of the lamp diminished by the human measure [of the gnomon], the shadow is produced. / The height of the lamp multiplied by the base distance between the gnomon and the lamp, when added to the human measure,

1.54.s:
viṃśakudīpauccaguṇācchāyā śaṅkūddhṛtā bhavet /
dīpaśaṅkvantaraṃ cātha cchāyāgravivaraghnabhā //
1.54.d:
विंशकुदीपौच्चगुणाच्छाया शङ्कूद्धृता भवेत् ।
दीपशङ्क्वन्तरं चाथ च्छायाग्रविवरघ्नभा ॥
1.54.m: the shadow multiplied by the height of the lamp and divided by the gnomon becomes the distance between the lamp and the gnomon. / And the shadow multiplied by the distance between the tips of the shadows,

1.54.s:
mānāntaradrudbhūmiḥ syādathobhūnarāhatiḥ /
prabhāptā jāyate dīpaśikhauccyaṃ syāttrirāśikāt //
1.54.d:
मानान्तरद्रुद्भूमिः स्यादथोभूनराहतिः ।
प्रभाप्ता जायते दीपशिखौच्च्यं स्यात्त्रिराशिकात् ॥
1.54.m: divided by the difference of the measures, is the base distance. Then, the product of the base and the gnomon / divided by the shadow produces the height of the lamp's flame by the rule of three.

1.54.s:
etatsaṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ gaṇite parikarmakam /
grahamadhyādikaṃ vakṣye gaṇite nātivistarān //
1.54.d:
एतत्संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं गणिते परिकर्मकम् ।
ग्रहमध्यादिकं वक्ष्ये गणिते नातिविस्तरान् ॥
1.54.m: Thus the preliminary arithmetic operations have been declared in brief. / I shall now declare the mean positions of the planets and the rest in astronomy, without excessive expansion.

1.54.s:
yugamānaṃ smṛtaṃ vipra khacatuṣkaradārṇavāḥ /
taddaśāṃśāstu catvāraḥ kṛtākhyaṃ pādamucyate //
1.54.d:
युगमानं स्मृतं विप्र खचतुष्करदार्णवाः ।
तद्दशांशास्तु चत्वारः कृताख्यं पादमुच्यते ॥
1.54.m: The measure of a yuga is traditionally taught, O brahmin, as four million three hundred and twenty thousand [years]. / Four-tenths of that is declared to be the quarter known as Kṛtayuga;

1.54.s:
trayasretā dvāparaḥ dvau kalirekaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
manukṛtābdasahitā yugānāmekasaptatiḥ //
1.54.d:
त्रयस्रेता द्वापरः द्वौ कलिरेकः प्रकीर्तितः ।
मनुकृताब्दसहिता युगानामेकसप्ततिः ॥
1.54.m: three [tenths] are Tretā, two Dvāpara, and one is proclaimed to be Kali. / Seventy-one yugas together with the Kṛtayuga years of a Manu [sandhi]

1.54.s:
vidherddine syurviprendra manavastu caturdaśa /
tāvatyeva niśā tasya viprendra parikīrtitā //
1.54.d:
विधेर्द्दिने स्युर्विप्रेन्द्र मनवस्तु चतुर्दश ।
तावत्येव निशा तस्य विप्रेन्द्र परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.54.m: constitute a day of the Creator, O best of brahmins; there are fourteen Manus, / and just as long is declared to be his night, O foremost of brahmins.

1.54.s:
svayaṃbhuvā śaragatānabdānsaṃpiṇḍya nārada /
khacarānayanaṃ kāryamathaveṣṭayugāditaḥ //
1.54.d:
स्वयंभुवा शरगतानब्दान्संपिण्ड्य नारद ।
खचरानयनं कार्यमथवेष्टयुगादितः ॥
1.54.m: Having totaled the elapsed years from the birth of the Self-born Brahmā, O Nārada, / the calculation of the heavenly bodies is to be made, or else from the beginning of the desired yuga.

1.54.s:
yuge sūryajñaśukrāṇāṃ khacatuṣkaradārṇavāḥ /
pūjārkiguruśukrāṇāṃ bhagaṇāpūrvapāpinām //
1.54.d:
युगे सूर्यज्ञशुक्राणां खचतुष्करदार्णवाः ।
पूजार्किगुरुशुक्राणां भगणापूर्वपापिनाम् ॥
1.54.m: In a yuga, the revolutions of the Sun, Mercury, and Venus are four million three hundred and twenty thousand; / the revolutions of Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, and the previously mentioned evil planets [are as follows]:

1.54.s:
indorasāgnitriṣu sapta bhūdharamārgaṇāḥ /
dasratryāṣṭarasāṃkāśvilocanāni kujasya tu //
1.54.d:
इन्दोरसाग्नित्रिषु सप्त भूधरमार्गणाः ।
दस्रत्र्याष्टरसांकाश्विलोचनानि कुजस्य तु ॥
1.54.m: Of the Moon, fifty-seven million seven hundred and fifty-three thousand three hundred and thirty-six; / and of Mars, two million two hundred and ninety-six thousand eight hundred and thirty-two.

1.54.s:
budhaśīghrasya śūnyartukhādritryaṅkanagendavaḥ /
bṛhaspateḥ khadasrākṣivedasraṅhūyastathā //
1.54.d:
बुधशीघ्रस्य शून्यर्तुखाद्रित्र्यङ्कनगेन्दवः ।
बृहस्पतेः खदस्राक्षिवेदस्रङ्हूयस्तथा ॥
1.54.m: Of the quick [conjunction] of Mercury, seventeen million nine hundred and thirty-seven thousand and sixty; / of Jupiter, three hundred and sixty-four thousand two hundred and twenty;

1.54.s:
śitaśīghrasya yaṣṇasatriyamāśvisvabhūdharāḥ /
śanerbhujagaṣaṭpacarasavedaniśākarāḥ //
1.54.d:
शितशीघ्रस्य यष्णसत्रियमाश्विस्वभूधराः ।
शनेर्भुजगषट्पचरसवेदनिशाकराः ॥
1.54.m: of the quick [conjunction] of Venus, seven million twenty-two thousand three hundred and seventy-six; / of Saturn, one hundred and forty-six thousand five hundred and sixty-eight.

1.54.s:
candroñcasyāgniśūnyākṣivasusarpārṇavā yuge /
vāmaṃ pātasya ca svagniyamāśviśikhidasrakāḥ //
1.54.d:
चन्द्रोञ्चस्याग्निशून्याक्षिवसुसर्पार्णवा युगे ।
वामं पातस्य च स्वग्नियमाश्विशिखिदस्रकाः ॥
1.54.m: Of the lunar apogee, four hundred and eighty-eight thousand two hundred and three in a yuga; / and retrogradely of its ascending node, two hundred and thirty-two thousand two hundred and twenty-six.

1.54.s:
udayādudayaṃ bhānorbhūmaiḥ sācena vāsarāḥ /
vasuvdyaṣṭādrirūpāṅkasaptādritithayo yuge //
1.54.d:
उदयादुदयं भानोर्भूमैः साचेन वासराः ।
वसुव्द्यष्टाद्रिरूपाङ्कसप्ताद्रितिथयो युगे ॥
1.54.m: From sunrise to sunrise, the terrestrial civil days of the Sun / are one billion five hundred and seventy-seven million nine hundred and seventeen thousand eight hundred and twenty-eight in a yuga.

1.54.s:
ṣaḍ vahitrihutāśāṅkatithayaścādhimāsakāḥ /
tithikṣayāyamārthākṣidvyaṣṭavyomaśarāśvinaḥ //
1.54.d:
षड् वहित्रिहुताशाङ्कतिथयश्चाधिमासकाः ।
तिथिक्षयायमार्थाक्षिद्व्यष्टव्योमशराश्विनः ॥
1.54.m: The intercalary months are one million five hundred and ninety-three thousand three hundred and thirty-six; / and the omitted lunar days are twenty-five million eighty-two thousand two hundred and fifty-two.

1.54.s:
ravacatuṣkā samudrāṣṭakurpacaravimāsakāḥ /
ṣaṭtryagnivedagnipañcaśubhrāṃśumāsakāḥ //
1.54.d:
रवचतुष्का समुद्राष्टकुर्पचरविमासकाः ।
षट्त्र्यग्निवेदग्निपञ्चशुभ्रांशुमासकाः ॥
1.54.m: The solar months are fifty-one million eight hundred and forty thousand; / and the lunar months are fifty-three million four hundred and thirty-three thousand three hundred and thirty-six.

1.54.s:
prāgāteḥ sūryamandasya kalpesaptāṣṭavahnayaḥ /
kaujasya vedasvayamā baudhasyāṣṭartuvahnayaḥ //
1.54.d:
प्रागातेः सूर्यमन्दस्य कल्पेसप्ताष्टवह्नयः ।
कौजस्य वेदस्वयमा बौधस्याष्टर्तुवह्नयः ॥
1.54.m: In a kalpa, the revolutions of the slow apogee of the Sun in direct motion are three hundred and eighty-seven; / of Mars, two hundred and four; of Mercury, three hundred and sixty-eight;

1.54.s:
ravaravarandhrāṇi jaivasya śaukrasyārdhaguṇeṣavaḥ /
gognayaḥ śanimandasya pātānāmathavā mataḥ //
1.54.d:
रवरवरन्ध्राणि जैवस्य शौक्रस्यार्धगुणेषवः ।
गोग्नयः शनिमन्दस्य पातानामथवा मतः ॥
1.54.m: of Jupiter, nine hundred; of Venus, five hundred and thirty-five; / of Saturn's slow apogee, thirty-nine; or else, the views regarding the nodes [are as follows]:

1.54.s:
manudasrāstu kaujasya baudhasyāṣṭāṣṭasāgarāḥ /
kṛtādricandrājaivasya ravaikasyāgniravanandakāḥ //
1.54.d:
मनुदस्रास्तु कौजस्य बौधस्याष्टाष्टसागराः ।
कृताद्रिचन्द्राजैवस्य रवैकस्याग्निरवनन्दकाः ॥
1.54.m: Of Mars, two hundred and fourteen; of Mercury, four hundred and eighty-eight; / of Jupiter, one hundred and seventy-four; of Venus, eight hundred and ninety-nine;

1.54.s:
śanipātasya bhagaṇāḥ kalpe yamarasartavaḥ /
vartamānayuge pānāvatsarābhagaṇābhidhāḥ //
1.54.d:
शनिपातस्य भगणाः कल्पे यमरसर्तवः ।
वर्तमानयुगे पानावत्सराभगणाभिधाः ॥
1.54.m: and the revolutions of Saturn's node in a kalpa are six hundred and sixty-two. / In the current yuga, the years called revolutions [are noted];

1.54.s:
māsīkṛtāyutā māsairmadhuśuklādibhirgataiḥ /
pṛthaktthāsidhimāsagrāsūryamāsavibhājitāḥ //
1.54.d:
मासीकृतायुता मासैर्मधुशुक्लादिभिर्गतैः ।
पृथक्त्थासिधिमासग्रासूर्यमासविभाजिताः ॥
1.54.m: turned into months and added to the elapsed months beginning with the bright half of Madhu, / placed in a separate position, they are multiplied by the intercalary months and divided by the solar months.

1.54.s:
athādhimāsakairyuktā dinīkṛtya dinānvitāḥ /
dvisthāstitikṣayābhyastāścāndravāsarabhājitāḥ //
1.54.d:
अथाधिमासकैर्युक्ता दिनीकृत्य दिनान्विताः ।
द्विस्थास्तितिक्षयाभ्यस्ताश्चान्द्रवासरभाजिताः ॥
1.54.m: Then, combined with the intercalary months, converted into days, and increased by the elapsed days, / placed in two positions, multiplied by the omitted lunar days, and divided by the lunar days:

1.54.s:
lathonarātrirahitālaṅkāryāmarddharātrikāḥ /
sāvanodyūgasārarkādirdinamāsābdayāstataḥ //
1.54.d:
लथोनरात्रिरहितालङ्कार्यामर्द्धरात्रिकाः ।
सावनोद्यूगसारर्कादिर्दिनमासाब्दयास्ततः ॥
1.54.m: diminished by the resulting omitted days, they are the civil days at midnight at Laṅkā. / Thence the terrestrial civil days, the lord of the day, month, and year [are found]:

1.54.s:
saptibhiḥ kṣapitaḥ śeṣaḥ mūryādyovāsareśvaraḥ /
māsābdadinasaṃkhyāsaṃdvitrighnaṃ rūpasaṃyutam //
1.54.d:
सप्तिभिः क्षपितः शेषः मूर्याद्योवासरेश्वरः ।
मासाब्ददिनसंख्यासंद्वित्रिघ्नं रूपसंयुतम् ॥
1.54.m: divided by seven, the remainder indicates the lord of the day, beginning with the Sun. / The number of months, years, and days multiplied by two and three, and increased by one,

1.54.s:
saptorddhanāvaśeṣau tau vijñeyau māsavarṣapau /
snehasya bhagaṇābhyasto dinarāśiḥ kuvāsaraiḥ //
1.54.d:
सप्तोर्द्धनावशेषौ तौ विज्ञेयौ मासवर्षपौ ।
स्नेहस्य भगणाभ्यस्तो दिनराशिः कुवासरैः ॥
1.54.m: divided by seven, the remainders are to be known as the lords of the month and of the year. / The sum of days multiplied by the revolutions of a planet and divided by the terrestrial civil days [yields its position].

1.54.s:
vibhājito madhyagatyā bhagaṇādirgraho bhavet /
evaṃ hyaśīghramandāñcaye proktāḥ pūrvapāpinaḥ //
1.54.d:
विभाजितो मध्यगत्या भगणादिर्ग्रहो भवेत् ।
एवं ह्यशीघ्रमन्दाञ्चये प्रोक्ताः पूर्वपापिनः ॥
1.54.m: Divided by the mean motion, the planet is obtained in revolutions and the rest. / Thus indeed are the slow apogees and fast apogees declared for the previous planets.

1.54.s:
vilomagatayaḥ pātāstadvañcakrāṣviśodhitāḥ /
yojanāni śatānyaṣṭau bhūkarṇauṃ dviguṇāḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.54.d:
विलोमगतयः पातास्तद्वञ्चक्राष्विशोधिताः ।
योजनानि शतान्यष्टौ भूकर्णौं द्विगुणाः स्मृतः ॥
1.54.m: The nodes, having retrograde motion, are likewise subtracted from the circle. / The diameter of the earth is known to be eight hundred multiplied by two yojanas.

1.54.s:
tadvargato daśaguṇātpada bhūparidhirbhavet /
laṃbajyāghnasvajīvāptaḥ sphuṭo bhūparidhiḥ svakaḥ //
1.54.d:
तद्वर्गतो दशगुणात्पद भूपरिधिर्भवेत् ।
लंबज्याघ्नस्वजीवाप्तः स्फुटो भूपरिधिः स्वकः ॥
1.54.m: The square root of ten times its square is the circumference of the earth. / Multiplied by the sine of colatitude and divided by the radius, it becomes the true circumference of one's own locality.

1.54.s:
tena deśāntarābhyastā grahabhuktirvibhājitā /
kalāditatphalaṃ prārcyāḥ grahebhyaḥ pariśodhayet //
1.54.d:
तेन देशान्तराभ्यस्ता ग्रहभुक्तिर्विभाजिता ।
कलादितत्फलं प्रार्च्याः ग्रहेभ्यः परिशोधयेत् ॥
1.54.m: The daily motion of the planet multiplied by the terrestrial longitude and divided by that, / yields a result in minutes and the rest; one should subtract that from the planets to the east.

1.54.s:
rekhāpratīcisaṃsthāne prakṣipetsyuḥ svadeśataḥ /
rākṣasātapadevaukaḥ śailayormadhyasūtragāḥ //
1.54.d:
रेखाप्रतीचिसंस्थाने प्रक्षिपेत्स्युः स्वदेशतः ।
राक्षसातपदेवौकः शैलयोर्मध्यसूत्रगाः ॥
1.54.m: One should add it if the locality is situated west of the prime meridian. / Those on the central meridian between the abode of the demons and the mountain of the gods,

1.54.s:
avantikārohatikaṃ tathā sannihitaṃ saraḥ /
vārapravṛttivāgdeśe kṣayārddhebhyadhiko bhavet //
1.54.d:
अवन्तिकारोहतिकं तथा सन्निहितं सरः ।
वारप्रवृत्तिवाग्देशे क्षयार्द्धेभ्यधिको भवेत् ॥
1.54.m: are Avantikā, Rohitaka, and the nearby lake Kurukṣetra. / The start of the weekday in that eastern region would exceed the half-reduction;

1.54.s:
taddeśāntaranāḍībhiḥ paścādūne vinirdiśet /
iṣṭanāḍīguṇā bhuktiḥ ṣaṣṭyā bhaktā kalādikam //
1.54.d:
तद्देशान्तरनाडीभिः पश्चादूने विनिर्दिशेत् ।
इष्टनाडीगुणा भुक्तिः षष्ट्या भक्ता कलादिकम् ॥
1.54.m: by the nāḍīs of that terrestrial longitude, one should declare it to be less in the west. / The daily motion multiplied by the desired nāḍīs and divided by sixty yields minutes and the like.

1.54.s:
gate śoddhyaṃ tathā yojyaṃ gamye tātkāliko grahaḥ /
bhacakraliptāśītyaṃśaḥ paramaṃ dakṣiṇottaram //
1.54.d:
गते शोद्ध्यं तथा योज्यं गम्ये तात्कालिको ग्रहः ।
भचक्रलिप्ताशीत्यंशः परमं दक्षिणोत्तरम् ॥
1.54.m: It is subtracted when past, and likewise added when to come; [thus is] the planet for that immediate time. / One-eightieth part of the minutes of the zodiacal circle is the maximum north-south

1.54.s:
vikṣipyate svapātena svakrāntyantādanuṣṇaguḥ /
tatra vāsaṃ dviguṇitajīvasriguṇitaṃ kujaḥ //
1.54.d:
विक्षिप्यते स्वपातेन स्वक्रान्त्यन्तादनुष्णगुः ।
तत्र वासं द्विगुणितजीवस्रिगुणितं कुजः ॥
1.54.m: deflection from the end of its declination by its node for the sun. / In that matter, Mars is doubled, Jupiter tripled,

1.54.s:
budhaśukrārkajāḥ pātairvikṣipyante caturguṇam /
rāśiliptāṣṭamo bhāgaḥ prathamaṃ jyārddhamucyate //
1.54.d:
बुधशुक्रार्कजाः पातैर्विक्षिप्यन्ते चतुर्गुणम् ।
राशिलिप्ताष्टमो भागः प्रथमं ज्यार्द्धमुच्यते ॥
1.54.m: and Mercury, Venus, and Saturn are deflected fourfold by their nodes. / The eighth part of the minutes of a sign is called the first sine-segment.

1.54.s:
tato dvibhaktalabdhonamiśritaṃ taddvitīyakam /
ādyenaiva kramātpiṇḍānbhaktāllabdhonitairyutān //
1.54.d:
ततो द्विभक्तलब्धोनमिश्रितं तद्द्वितीयकम् ।
आद्येनैव क्रमात्पिण्डान्भक्ताल्लब्धोनितैर्युतान् ॥
1.54.m: That, reduced by the quotient of its division by two, combined, is the second. / By that very first, successively divided by the quotients obtained from dividing the tabular sines,

1.54.s:
khaṇḍakāḥ syuścaturviśā jyārddhapiṇḍāḥ kramādamī /
paramā pakramajyā tu saptarandhraguṇendavaḥ //
1.54.d:
खण्डकाः स्युश्चतुर्विशा ज्यार्द्धपिण्डाः क्रमादमी ।
परमा पक्रमज्या तु सप्तरन्ध्रगुणेन्दवः ॥
1.54.m: the segments would be the twenty-four tabular sines in order. / The maximum sine of declination is one thousand three hundred and ninety-seven.

1.54.s:
tadgumajyā trijivāptā tañcāpaṃ krāntirucyate /
grahaṃ saṃśodhya mandoñcattathā śīghnādviśodhya ca //
1.54.d:
तद्गुमज्या त्रिजिवाप्ता तञ्चापं क्रान्तिरुच्यते ।
ग्रहं संशोध्य मन्दोञ्चत्तथा शीघ्नाद्विशोध्य च ॥
1.54.m: Its sine multiplied and divided by the radius, the arc of that is called the declination. / Subtracting the planet from the slow apogee, and likewise subtracting it from the fast apogee,

1.54.s:
śeṣaṃ kandapadantasmādbhujajyā koṭireva ca /
gatādbhujajyāviṣame gamyātkoṭiḥ pade bhavet //
1.54.d:
शेषं कन्दपदन्तस्माद्भुजज्या कोटिरेव च ।
गताद्भुजज्याविषमे गम्यात्कोटिः पदे भवेत् ॥
1.54.m: the remainder is the anomaly and quadrant; from that arise the base-sine and perpendicular-sine. / In an odd quadrant, the base-sine is from the past [anomaly] and the perpendicular-sine from the anomaly to come.

1.54.s:
sameti gamyādvāhudajyā koṭijyānugatā bhavet /
liptāstattvayamairbhaktā labdhajyāpiṇḍakaṃ gatam //
1.54.d:
समेति गम्याद्वाहुदज्या कोटिज्यानुगता भवेत् ।
लिप्तास्तत्त्वयमैर्भक्ता लब्धज्यापिण्डकं गतम् ॥
1.54.m: In an even quadrant, the base-sine is from the anomaly to come, and the perpendicular-sine is from the past. / The minutes divided by two hundred and twenty-five yield the elapsed tabular sine.

1.54.s:
gatagamyāntarābhyastaṃ vibhajettattvalocanaiḥ /
tadavāptaphalaṃ yojyaṃ jyāpiṇḍe gatasaṃjñake //
1.54.d:
गतगम्यान्तराभ्यस्तं विभजेत्तत्त्वलोचनैः ।
तदवाप्तफलं योज्यं ज्यापिण्डे गतसंज्ञके ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by the difference between the elapsed and to-come, one should divide by two hundred and twenty-five. / The result thus obtained should be added to the tabular sine called the elapsed.

1.54.s:
syātkramajyāvidhiścaivamutkramajyāgatā bhavet /
liptāstattvayamairbhaktā labdhajyā piṇḍakaṃ gatam //
1.54.d:
स्यात्क्रमज्याविधिश्चैवमुत्क्रमज्यागता भवेत् ।
लिप्तास्तत्त्वयमैर्भक्ता लब्धज्या पिण्डकं गतम् ॥
1.54.m: Such is the rule for the right sine; and the versed sine elapsed would be: / the minutes divided by two hundred and twenty-five yield the elapsed tabular sine.

1.54.s:
gatagamyāntarābhyastaṃ vibhajettattvalocanaiḥ /
tadavāptaphalaṃ yojyaṃ jyāpiṇḍe gatasaṃjñake //
1.54.d:
गतगम्यान्तराभ्यस्तं विभजेत्तत्त्वलोचनैः ।
तदवाप्तफलं योज्यं ज्यापिण्डे गतसंज्ञके ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by the difference between the elapsed and to-come, one should divide by two hundred and twenty-five. / The result thus obtained should be added to the tabular sine called the elapsed.

1.54.s:
syātkramajyāvidhiścaivamukramajyāsvapismṛtaḥ /
jyāṃ prohya śeṣaṃ tattvatāśvi hṝntaṃ tadvivaroddhṛm //
1.54.d:
स्यात्क्रमज्याविधिश्चैवमुक्रमज्यास्वपिस्मृतः ।
ज्यां प्रोह्य शेषं तत्त्वताश्वि हॄन्तं तद्विवरोद्धृम् ॥
1.54.m: Such is the rule for the right sine, and it is also remembered for the versed sines. / Subtracting the sine, dividing the remainder by two hundred and twenty-five, divided by the difference,

1.54.s:
saṃkhyātattvāśvisaṃvargyasaṃyojyaṃ dhanurucyate /
ravermandaparidhyaṃśā manavaḥ śītagoradāḥ //
1.54.d:
संख्यातत्त्वाश्विसंवर्ग्यसंयोज्यं धनुरुच्यते ।
रवेर्मन्दपरिध्यंशा मनवः शीतगोरदाः ॥
1.54.m: multiplied by two hundred and twenty-five and added to the count, it is called the arc. / The degrees of the sun's slow epicycle are fourteen; those of the moon are thirty-two.

1.54.s:
yugmānte viṣamānte tunakhaliptonitāstayoḥ /
yugmānterthādrayaḥ khāgnisurāḥ sūryā navārṇavāḥ //
1.54.d:
युग्मान्ते विषमान्ते तुनखलिप्तोनितास्तयोः ।
युग्मान्तेर्थाद्रयः खाग्निसुराः सूर्या नवार्णवाः ॥
1.54.m: At the end of an even quadrant they are diminished by twenty minutes; at the end of an odd quadrant, / for them at the end of an even quadrant: seventy-five, thirty, thirty-three, twelve, and forty-nine;

1.54.s:
ojedvyagā ca suyamāradārudrāgajābdhayaḥ /
kujādīnāmataḥ śaughnyāyugmānterthāgnidasrakāḥ //
1.54.d:
ओजेद्व्यगा च सुयमारदारुद्रागजाब्धयः ।
कुजादीनामतः शौघ्न्यायुग्मान्तेर्थाग्निदस्रकाः ॥
1.54.m: in an odd quadrant: seventy-two, twenty-eight, fourteen, and forty-eight. / Next, for Mars and the others, the fast [epicycles] at the end of an even quadrant: two hundred and thirty-five,

1.54.s:
guṇāgnicandrāḥ khanagādvirasākṣīṇi go 'grayaḥ /
ojānte dvitriyamatādviviśveyamaparvatāḥ //
1.54.d:
गुणाग्निचन्द्राः खनगाद्विरसाक्षीणि गो ऽग्रयः ।
ओजान्ते द्वित्रियमताद्विविश्वेयमपर्वताः ॥
1.54.m: one hundred and thirty-three, seventy, two hundred and sixty-two, and ninety-nine; / at the end of an odd quadrant: two hundred and thirty-two, two hundred and sixty-two, and seventy-two,

1.54.s:
khartudasnāvipadvedāḥ śīghnakarmaṇi kīrtitāḥ /
ojayugmāntaraguṇābhujajyātrijyayoddhṛtāḥ //
1.54.d:
खर्तुदस्नाविपद्वेदाः शीघ्नकर्मणि कीर्तिताः ।
ओजयुग्मान्तरगुणाभुजज्यात्रिज्ययोद्धृताः ॥
1.54.m: two hundred and sixty, and four hundred and twenty-four are proclaimed in the fast operation. / Multiplied by the difference between odd and even, the base-sine is divided by the radius;

1.54.s:
yugmavṛttedhanarṇaśyādojādūne 'dhike sphuṭam /
tadguṇe bhujakoṭijyebhagaṇāṃśavibhājite //
1.54.d:
युग्मवृत्तेधनर्णश्यादोजादूने ऽधिके स्फुटम् ।
तद्गुणे भुजकोटिज्येभगणांशविभाजिते ॥
1.54.m: it should be additive or subtractive to the even epicycle according as it is less or greater than the odd, [giving] the true [epicycle]. / Multiplied by that, the base-sine and perpendicular-sine are divided by the degrees of the circle;

1.54.s:
tadbhujajyāphaladhanurmāndaṃ liptādikaṃ phalam /
śai'yakoṭiphalaṃ kendre makarādau dhanaṃ smṛtam //
1.54.d:
तद्भुजज्याफलधनुर्मान्दं लिप्तादिकं फलम् ।
शैऽयकोटिफलं केन्द्रे मकरादौ धनं स्मृतम् ॥
1.54.m: the arc of that base-sine equation is the slow equation in minutes and the like. / The fast perpendicular-equation, when the anomaly begins with Capricorn, is regarded as additive;

1.54.s:
saṃśodhyaṃ tu trijīvāyāṃ karkādau koṭijaṃ phalam /
tadbāhuphalavargaikyānmūlakarṇaścalābhidhaḥ //
1.54.d:
संशोध्यं तु त्रिजीवायां कर्कादौ कोटिजं फलम् ।
तद्बाहुफलवर्गैक्यान्मूलकर्णश्चलाभिधः ॥
1.54.m: it is to be subtracted from the radius when it begins with Cancer. / From the sum of the squares of that base-equation [and perpendicular], the square root is the hypotenuse named variable.

1.54.s:
trijyābhyastaṃ bhujaphalaṃ makarādau dhanaṃ smṛtam /
saṃśodhyaṃ tu trijīvāyāṃ karkādau koṭijaṃ phalam //
1.54.d:
त्रिज्याभ्यस्तं भुजफलं मकरादौ धनं स्मृतम् ।
संशोध्यं तु त्रिजीवायां कर्कादौ कोटिजं फलम् ॥
1.54.m: The base-equation multiplied by the radius is regarded as additive when beginning with Capricorn; / but the equation produced from the perpendicular is to be subtracted from the radius when beginning with Cancer.

1.54.s:
tadbāhuphalavargaikyānmūlaṃ karṇaścalābhidhaḥ /
trijyābhaghyastaṃ bhujaphalaṃ palakarṇavibhājitam //
1.54.d:
तद्बाहुफलवर्गैक्यान्मूलं कर्णश्चलाभिधः ।
त्रिज्याभघ्यस्तं भुजफलं पलकर्णविभाजितम् ॥
1.54.m: From the sum of the squares of that base-equation, the square root is the hypotenuse named variable. / The base-equation multiplied by the radius and divided by the equinoctial hypotenuse,

1.54.s:
labdhasya cāpaṃ liptādi phalaṃ śaidhryamidaṃ smṛtam /
etadādau kujādīnāṃ caturthe caiva karmaṇi //
1.54.d:
लब्धस्य चापं लिप्तादि फलं शैध्र्यमिदं स्मृतम् ।
एतदादौ कुजादीनां चतुर्थे चैव कर्मणि ॥
1.54.m: the arc of the quotient in minutes and the like is remembered as this fast equation. / This is in the first and indeed the fourth operation for Mars and the others.

1.54.s:
māndyaṃ karmaikamarkendvorbhaundvorbhauṃmādīnāmāthocyate /
śairdhyaṃ mādyaṃ punarmāndyaṃ śairghyaṃ catvāryanukramāt //
1.54.d:
मान्द्यं कर्मैकमर्केन्द्वोर्भौन्द्वोर्भौंमादीनामाथोच्यते ।
शैर्ध्यं माद्यं पुनर्मान्द्यं शैर्घ्यं चत्वार्यनुक्रमात् ॥
1.54.m: For the sun and the moon there is only one slow operation; now it is declared for Mars and the rest: / fast, slow, again slow, and fast—the four operations in order.

1.54.s:
ajā dikendre sarveṣāṃ māndye śairghye ca karmaṇi /
dhanaṃ grahāṇāṃ liptādi tulādāvṛṇameva tat //
1.54.d:
अजा दिकेन्द्रे सर्वेषां मान्द्ये शैर्घ्ये च कर्मणि ।
धनं ग्रहाणां लिप्तादि तुलादावृणमेव तत् ॥
1.54.m: When the anomaly begins with Aries, in both the slow and fast operations for all planets, / the minutes and the like are additive; when beginning with Libra, that is indeed subtractive.

1.54.s:
arkabāhuphalābhyastā grahabhuktivibhājitāḥ /
bhacakrakalikābhistu liptāḥ kāryā graher'kavat //
1.54.d:
अर्कबाहुफलाभ्यस्ता ग्रहभुक्तिविभाजिताः ।
भचक्रकलिकाभिस्तु लिप्ताः कार्या ग्रहेर्ऽकवत् ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by the sun's base-equation and divided by the minutes of the zodiacal circle, / the daily motions of the planets are converted into minutes like the sun.

1.54.s:
grahabhaktaḥ phalaṃ kāryaṃ grahavanmandakarmaṇi /
karkādau taddhanaṃ tatra makarādāvṛṇaṃ smṛtam //
1.54.d:
ग्रहभक्तः फलं कार्यं ग्रहवन्मन्दकर्मणि ।
कर्कादौ तद्धनं तत्र मकरादावृणं स्मृतम् ॥
1.54.m: The equation divided by the planet should be applied like the planet in the slow operation: / there, beginning with Cancer, it is additive, and beginning with Capricorn, it is remembered as subtractive.

1.54.s:
dorjyottaraguṇābhuktistattvanetroddhṛtā punaḥ /
svamandaparidhikṣuṇṇā bhagaṇāṃśoddhṛtāḥkalāḥ //
1.54.d:
दोर्ज्योत्तरगुणाभुक्तिस्तत्त्वनेत्रोद्धृता पुनः ।
स्वमन्दपरिधिक्षुण्णा भगणांशोद्धृताःकलाः ॥
1.54.m: The daily motion multiplied by the base-sine and again divided by two hundred and twenty-five, / multiplied by its slow epicycle and divided by the degrees of the revolution, yields the minutes.

1.54.s:
mandasphuṭakṛtā bhuktiḥ śīghnoccabhuktitaḥ /
taccheṣaṃ vivareṇātha hanyātrijyāṅkakarṇayoḥ //
1.54.d:
मन्दस्फुटकृता भुक्तिः शीघ्नोच्चभुक्तितः ।
तच्छेषं विवरेणाथ हन्यात्रिज्याङ्ककर्णयोः ॥
1.54.m: The daily motion corrected by the slow process [is subtracted] from the motion of the fast apogee; / one should then multiply that remainder by the difference between the radius and the hypotenuse.

1.54.s:
cakrakarṇahṛtaṃ bhuktau karṇe trijyādhike dhanam /
ṛṇamūne 'dhike prohya śeṣaṃ vakragatirbhavet //
1.54.d:
चक्रकर्णहृतं भुक्तौ कर्णे त्रिज्याधिके धनम् ।
ऋणमूने ऽधिके प्रोह्य शेषं वक्रगतिर्भवेत् ॥
1.54.m: Divided by the hypotenuse of the circle, it is additive to the daily motion when the hypotenuse exceeds the radius; / subtractive when less; subtracted when greater, the remainder becomes retrograde motion.

1.54.s:
kṛtartucandrairvedendraiḥ śūnyatryekairguṇāṣṭabhiḥ /
śararudraiścaturyāṃśukendrāṃśerbhūsutādayaḥ //
1.54.d:
कृतर्तुचन्द्रैर्वेदेन्द्रैः शून्यत्र्येकैर्गुणाष्टभिः ।
शररुद्रैश्चतुर्यांशुकेन्द्रांशेर्भूसुतादयः ॥
1.54.m: At one hundred and sixty-four, one hundred and forty-four, one hundred and thirty, eighty-three, / and one hundred and fifteen degrees of the fast anomaly, Mars and the other planets

1.54.s:
vakriṇaścakraśuddhaistairaṃśairujutivakratām /
kramajyā viṣuvadbhāghnī kṣitijyā dvādaśoddhṛtā //
1.54.d:
वक्रिणश्चक्रशुद्धैस्तैरंशैरुजुतिवक्रताम् ।
क्रमज्या विषुवद्भाघ्नी क्षितिज्या द्वादशोद्धृता ॥
1.54.m: become retrograde; and when those degrees are deducted from the circle, they attain direct motion. / The right sine multiplied by the equinoctial shadow and divided by twelve is the earth-sine.

1.54.s:
trijyāguṇā dinavyāsabhaktā cāpaṃ ca śatravaḥ /
tatkārmukamudakrāntau dhanahīno pṛthakkṣate //
1.54.d:
त्रिज्यागुणा दिनव्यासभक्ता चापं च शत्रवः ।
तत्कार्मुकमुदक्रान्तौ धनहीनो पृथक्क्षते ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by the radius and divided by the day-diameter, the arc [is determined]. / That arc is separately calculated as added or subtracted in northern declination;

1.54.s:
svāhorātracaturbhāgedinarātridale smṛte /
yāmyakrāntau viparyaste dviguṇaite dinakṣaye //
1.54.d:
स्वाहोरात्रचतुर्भागेदिनरात्रिदले स्मृते ।
याम्यक्रान्तौ विपर्यस्ते द्विगुणैते दिनक्षये ॥
1.54.m: in the quarter of its day-and-night circle, the halves of day and night are known. / In southern declination, it is reversed; when doubled, in the decrease of the day.

1.54.s:
bhabhogo 'ṣṭaśatīrliptāḥ svāśivaśailostathāttitheḥ /
grahaliptā bhagābhogābhāni bhuktyādinādikam //
1.54.d:
भभोगो ऽष्टशतीर्लिप्ताः स्वाशिवशैलोस्तथात्तिथेः ।
ग्रहलिप्ता भगाभोगाभानि भुक्त्यादिनादिकम् ॥
1.54.m: The span of an asterism is eight hundred minutes; and seven hundred and twenty is that of a lunar day. / The minutes of a planet [divided by] the span of an asterism give the asterisms, daily motion, and the like.

1.54.s:
ravīnduyogaliptāstu yogābhabhogabhājitāḥ /
gatagamyāśca ṣaṣṭighnā bhuktiyogāptanāḍikāḥ //
1.54.d:
रवीन्दुयोगलिप्तास्तु योगाभभोगभाजिताः ।
गतगम्याश्च षष्टिघ्ना भुक्तियोगाप्तनाडिकाः ॥
1.54.m: The sum of the minutes of the sun and moon divided by the span of an asterism yields the yoga. / The elapsed and to-come multiplied by sixty and divided by the sum of daily motions give the nāḍīs.

1.54.s:
arkenacandraliptāstu tithayo bhogabhājitāḥ /
gatagamyāśca ṣaṣṭighnā nātobhuktataroddhṛtāḥ //
1.54.d:
अर्केनचन्द्रलिप्तास्तु तिथयो भोगभाजिताः ।
गतगम्याश्च षष्टिघ्ना नातोभुक्ततरोद्धृताः ॥
1.54.m: The minutes of the moon [separated] from the sun, divided by the span, give the lunar days. / The elapsed and to-come, multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference in daily motion, [give the nāḍīs].

1.54.s:
tithayaḥ śuklapratipado dvighnāḥ saikā na gāhatāḥ /
śeṣaṃ bavo bālavaśca kaulavastaitilo garaḥ //
1.54.d:
तिथयः शुक्लप्रतिपदो द्विघ्नाः सैका न गाहताः ।
शेषं बवो बालवश्च कौलवस्तैतिलो गरः ॥
1.54.m: The lunar days starting with the bright fortnight's first day, multiplied by two, increased by one, and divided by seven: / the remainders are Bava, Bālava, Kaulava, Taitila, Gara,

1.54.s:
vaṇijobhre bhavedviṣṭiḥ kṛṣṇabhūtāparārddhataḥ /
śakunirnāgāśca catuṣpada kiṃstughnameva ca //
1.54.d:
वणिजोभ्रे भवेद्विष्टिः कृष्णभूतापरार्द्धतः ।
शकुनिर्नागाश्च चतुष्पद किंस्तुघ्नमेव च ॥
1.54.m: Vaṇij, and at zero it is Viṣṭi. From the second half of the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, / Śakuni, Catuṣpada, Nāga, and Kiṃstughna occur.

1.54.s:
śilātalevasaṃśuddhe vajralepetivāsame /
tatra śakāṅgulairiṣṭaiḥ samamaṇḍalamālikhet //
1.54.d:
शिलातलेवसंशुद्धे वज्रलेपेतिवासमे ।
तत्र शकाङ्गुलैरिष्टैः सममण्डलमालिखेत् ॥
1.54.m: On a leveled stone surface, coated with plaster and very smooth, / one should draw a regular circle there with desired digits of the gnomon.

1.54.s:
tanmadhye sthāpayecchaṅkuṃ kalpanā ddvādaśāṅgulam /
tacchāyāgraṃ spṛśedyatra dattaṃ pūrvāparāhnayoḥ //
1.54.d:
तन्मध्ये स्थापयेच्छङ्कुं कल्पना द्द्वादशाङ्गुलम् ।
तच्छायाग्रं स्पृशेद्यत्र दत्तं पूर्वापराह्नयोः ॥
1.54.m: In its centre one should set up a gnomon, by convention twelve digits [in height], / where the tip of its shadow touches, marked in the forenoon and afternoon.

1.54.s:
tatra binduṃ vidhāyobhau vṛtte pūrvāparābhidhau /
tanmadhye timinā rekhā kartavyā dakṣiṇottata //
1.54.d:
तत्र बिन्दुं विधायोभौ वृत्ते पूर्वापराभिधौ ।
तन्मध्ये तिमिना रेखा कर्तव्या दक्षिणोत्तत ॥
1.54.m: Having made two points there on the circle, called east and west, / in their middle a north-south line should be drawn by means of a fish-figure.

1.54.s:
yāmyottaradiśormadhye timinā pūrvapaścimā /
digmadhyamatsyaiḥ saṃsādhyā vidiśastadvadeva hi //
1.54.d:
याम्योत्तरदिशोर्मध्ये तिमिना पूर्वपश्चिमा ।
दिग्मध्यमत्स्यैः संसाध्या विदिशस्तद्वदेव हि ॥
1.54.m: Between the southern and northern directions, the east-west [line is drawn] by a fish-figure; / by means of fish-figures between the cardinal points, the intermediate directions are likewise determined.

1.54.s:
caturastaṃ bahiḥ kuryātsūtrairmadhyādviniḥsṛtaiḥ /
bhujasūtrāṅgulaistatra dattairiṣṭaprabhā matā //
1.54.d:
चतुरस्तं बहिः कुर्यात्सूत्रैर्मध्याद्विनिःसृतैः ।
भुजसूत्राङ्गुलैस्तत्र दत्तैरिष्टप्रभा मता ॥
1.54.m: One should make a square outside with cords extending from the centre; / by the digits of the base-cords marked there, the desired shadow is determined.

1.54.s:
prāṅkpaścimāśritā rekhā procyate samamaṇḍalam /
bhamaṇḍalaṃ ca viṣuvanmaṇḍalaṃ parikīrtitam //
1.54.d:
प्राङ्क्पश्चिमाश्रिता रेखा प्रोच्यते सममण्डलम् ।
भमण्डलं च विषुवन्मण्डलं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.54.m: The line lying east and west is called the prime vertical, / and the circle of constellations is proclaimed to be the equinoctial circle.

1.54.s:
rekhā prācyaparā sādhyā viṣuvadbhāgrayā tathā /
iṣṭacchāyāviṣuvatormadhyehyagrābhidhīyate //
1.54.d:
रेखा प्राच्यपरा साध्या विषुवद्भाग्रया तथा ।
इष्टच्छायाविषुवतोर्मध्येह्यग्राभिधीयते ॥
1.54.m: The east-west line should likewise be determined by the tip of the equinoctial shadow; / the distance between the desired shadow and the equinoctial [shadow] is called the agrā.

1.54.s:
śaṅkucchāyākṛtiyutermūlaṃ karṃṇo 'ya vargataḥ /
prohya śaṅkukṛte mūlaṃ chāyā śekuviparyayāt //
1.54.d:
शङ्कुच्छायाकृतियुतेर्मूलं कर्ंणो ऽय वर्गतः ।
प्रोह्य शङ्कुकृते मूलं छाया शेकुविपर्ययात् ॥
1.54.m: The square root of the sum of the squares of the gnomon and the shadow is the hypotenuse; / subtracting the square of the gnomon from the square [of the hypotenuse], the square root is the shadow, and conversely for the gnomon.

1.54.s:
triṃśatkṛtyoyuge bhānāṃ cakraṃ prākparilaṃbate /
tadguṇādbhadinairbhaktyā dyugaṇādyadavāpyate //
1.54.d:
त्रिंशत्कृत्योयुगे भानां चक्रं प्राक्परिलंबते ।
तद्गुणाद्भदिनैर्भक्त्या द्युगणाद्यदवाप्यते ॥
1.54.m: Thirty times in a yuga the circle of asterisms oscillates eastward; / by the quotient of that multiplier times the elapsed days divided by the days of a stellar revolution,

1.54.s:
taddosrivnādaśādhnāṃśā vijñeyā ayatānidhāḥ /
tatsaṃsvakṛtāddhahātkānticchāyāvaradalādikam //
1.54.d:
तद्दोस्रिव्नादशाध्नांशा विज्ञेया अयतानिधाः ।
तत्संस्वकृताद्धहात्कान्तिच्छायावरदलादिकम् ॥
1.54.m: the degrees multiplied by the sine of that and by twelve are known as the ayanāṃśas; / from the planet adjusted by that, the declination, shadow, day-radius, and so forth [are derived].

1.54.s:
śaṅkucchāyāhate trijye viṣuvatkarkabhājite /
laṃbākṣajye tayośchāye laṃbākṣau dakṣimau sadā //
1.54.d:
शङ्कुच्छायाहते त्रिज्ये विषुवत्कर्कभाजिते ।
लंबाक्षज्ये तयोश्छाये लंबाक्षौ दक्षिमौ सदा ॥
1.54.m: The trijyā multiplied by the gnomon and shadow and divided by the equinoctial hypotenuse / yields the sines of colatitude and latitude; their shadows, colatitude and latitude, are always to the south.

1.54.s:
sākṣārkāpakramayutirddiksāmyentaramanyathā /
śeṣahyānāṃśāḥ sūryasya tadvāhujyātha koṭijāḥ //
1.54.d:
साक्षार्कापक्रमयुतिर्द्दिक्साम्येन्तरमन्यथा ।
शेषह्यानांशाः सूर्यस्य तद्वाहुज्याथ कोटिजाः ॥
1.54.m: The sum of latitude and the sun's declination [is taken] when in the same direction, and their difference otherwise; / the remainder is the zenith distance of the sun; its sine is the bāhujyā, and the sine of the complement is the koṭijyā.

1.54.s:
śaṅkumānāṅgulābhyaste bhujatrijye yathāṅkramam /
koṭījyayāvibhajyāpte chāyākarmābahirddale //
1.54.d:
शङ्कुमानाङ्गुलाभ्यस्ते भुजत्रिज्ये यथाङ्क्रमम् ।
कोटीज्ययाविभज्याप्ते छायाकर्माबहिर्द्दले ॥
1.54.m: The sine of the base and the trijyā, multiplied respectively by the measure of the gnomon in digits, / and divided by the sine of the complement, give the shadow and the hypotenuse.

1.54.s:
svākṣārkanatabhāgānāṃ diksāmye 'taramanyathā /
digbhedopakramaḥ śeṣastasya jyā trijyayā hatā //
1.54.d:
स्वाक्षार्कनतभागानां दिक्साम्ये ऽतरमन्यथा ।
दिग्भेदोपक्रमः शेषस्तस्य ज्या त्रिज्यया हता ॥
1.54.m: The difference between one's latitude and the degrees of the sun's zenith distance [is taken] when in the same direction, and otherwise [the sum]; / when there is a difference of direction, the remainder is the declination, whose sine is multiplied by the trijyā.

1.54.s:
paramopakramajyāpta cāpamepādigo raviḥ /
karkādau prohyacakrārddhāttulādau bhārddhasaṃyutātta //
1.54.d:
परमोपक्रमज्याप्त चापमेपादिगो रविः ।
कर्कादौ प्रोह्यचक्रार्द्धात्तुलादौ भार्द्धसंयुतात्त ॥
1.54.m: Divided by the sine of maximum declination, the arc is the sun beginning with Aries; / beginning with Cancer, it is subtracted from half a circle; beginning with Libra, it is added to half the circle;

1.54.s:
mṛgādau prohyacakrāttu madhyāhner'kaḥ sphuṭo bhavet /
tanmandamasakṛddhāmaṃphalaṃ madhyo divākaraḥ //
1.54.d:
मृगादौ प्रोह्यचक्रात्तु मध्याह्नेर्ऽकः स्फुटो भवेत् ।
तन्मन्दमसकृद्धामंफलं मध्यो दिवाकरः ॥
1.54.m: and beginning with Capricorn, it is subtracted from the whole circle; thus the sun at midday becomes true. / From repeated equations of the centre, the true sun is [derived from] the mean sun.

1.54.s:
grahodayāḥ prāṇahatāḥ khakhāṣṭaikoddhatā gatiḥ /
cakrāsavo labdhayutī svrahorātrāsavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.54.d:
ग्रहोदयाः प्राणहताः खखाष्टैकोद्धता गतिः ।
चक्रासवो लब्धयुती स्व्रहोरात्रासवः स्मृताः ॥
1.54.m: The risings of the planets multiplied by prāṇas and divided by one thousand eight hundred is the motion; / the respirations of the revolution, joined to the quotient, are remembered as the respirations of one's own day-and-night.

1.54.s:
tribhadyukarṇārddhaguṇā svāhorātrārddhabhājitāḥ /
kramādekadvitribhaghājyā taccāpāni pṛthak pṛthak //
1.54.d:
त्रिभद्युकर्णार्द्धगुणा स्वाहोरात्रार्द्धभाजिताः ।
क्रमादेकद्वित्रिभघाज्या तच्चापानि पृथक् पृथक् ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by half the equinoctial day-hypotenuse and divided by half one's own diurnal circle, / the sines of one, two, and three signs in succession yield their respective arcs separately.

1.54.s:
svādhodhaḥ praviśodhyātha meṣāllaṅkodayāsavaḥ /
svāgāṣṭayorthagogaikāḥ śaratryekaṃ himāṃśavaḥ //
1.54.d:
स्वाधोधः प्रविशोध्याथ मेषाल्लङ्कोदयासवः ।
स्वागाष्टयोर्थगोगैकाः शरत्र्येकं हिमांशवः ॥
1.54.m: Then, subtracting each from the one beneath it, the rising respirations at Laṅkā from Aries [are]: / one thousand six hundred seventy, one thousand seven hundred ninety-five, and one thousand nine hundred thirty-five.

1.54.s:
svadeśacarakhaṇḍonā bhavantīṣṭodayāsavaḥ /
vyastāvyastairyutāstaistaiḥ karkaṭādyāstatastu yaḥ //
1.54.d:
स्वदेशचरखण्डोना भवन्तीष्टोदयासवः ।
व्यस्ताव्यस्तैर्युतास्तैस्तैः कर्कटाद्यास्ततस्तु यः ॥
1.54.m: Diminished by the local ascensional difference portions, they become the desired rising respirations [for Aries, Taurus, and Gemini]; / increased by those same [portions] in inverse order, [they are the rising respirations] for Cancer and the following signs.

1.54.s:
utkrameṇa ṣaḍevaite bhavantīṣṭāstulādayaḥ /
gatabhogyāsavaḥ kāryāḥ sāyanāḥsveṣṭabhāskarāḥ //
1.54.d:
उत्क्रमेण षडेवैते भवन्तीष्टास्तुलादयः ।
गतभोग्यासवः कार्याः सायनाःस्वेष्टभास्कराः ॥
1.54.m: These six in reverse order are the desired [rising times] for Libra and the rest. / The elapsed and remaining respirations should be calculated, with the ayanāṃśas added to one's desired sun.

1.54.s:
svodayātsuhatā bhaktā bhaktabhogyāḥ svamānataḥ /
abhiṣṭadhaṭikāsubhyo bhogyāsūnpraviśodhayet //
1.54.d:
स्वोदयात्सुहता भक्ता भक्तभोग्याः स्वमानतः ।
अभिष्टधटिकासुभ्यो भोग्यासून्प्रविशोधयेत् ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied well by their own rising [times] and divided by their own measure, the elapsed and to-be-passed [degrees] are obtained; / from the desired respirations of the ghaṭikās, one should subtract the respirations yet to be passed.

1.54.s:
tadvadevaiṣyalagnāsūnevaṃ vyāptāstathā kramāt /
śeṣaṃ triṃśatkramāddhyastamaśuddhena vibhājitam //
1.54.d:
तद्वदेवैष्यलग्नासूनेवं व्याप्तास्तथा क्रमात् ।
शेषं त्रिंशत्क्रमाद्ध्यस्तमशुद्धेन विभाजितम् ॥
1.54.m: Likewise with the respirations of the subsequent rising signs successively traversed in this manner; / the remainder, multiplied by thirty and divided by the unexhausted [rising time],

1.54.s:
bhāgayuktaṃ ca hīnaṃ ca vyayanāṃśaṃ tanuḥ kuje /
prākpaścānnatanāḍībhyastadvallaṅkodayāsubhiḥ //
1.54.d:
भागयुक्तं च हीनं च व्ययनांशं तनुः कुजे ।
प्राक्पश्चान्नतनाडीभ्यस्तद्वल्लङ्कोदयासुभिः ॥
1.54.m: increased or diminished by the degrees, minus the ayanāṃśas, is the ascendant on the horizon. / By the elapsed nāḍīs before and after midday, in the same way, by the rising respirations at Laṅkā,

1.54.s:
bhānau kṣayadhane kṛtvā madhyalagnaṃ tadā bhavet /
bhogyāsūnūnakasyātha bhuktāsūnadhikasya ca //
1.54.d:
भानौ क्षयधने कृत्वा मध्यलग्नं तदा भवेत् ।
भोग्यासूनूनकस्याथ भुक्तासूनधिकस्य च ॥
1.54.m: applied as subtractive or additive to the sun, the meridian-ecliptic point is then obtained. / For the lesser, the respirations to be traversed, and for the greater, the respirations already traversed,

1.54.s:
sapiṇḍyāntaralagnāsūnevaṃ syātkālasādhanam /
virāhvarkabhujāṃśāścedindrālpāḥ syād graho vidhoḥ //
1.54.d:
सपिण्ड्यान्तरलग्नासूनेवं स्यात्कालसाधनम् ।
विराह्वर्कभुजांशाश्चेदिन्द्राल्पाः स्याद् ग्रहो विधोः ॥
1.54.m: together with the respirations of the intervening signs, thus constitutes the computation of time. / If the base degrees of the sun diminished by Rāhu are less than twelve, an eclipse of the moon takes place.

1.54.s:
teṣāṃ śivaghnāḥ śailāptā vyāvarkājaḥ śarāeṅgulaiḥ /
arkaṃ vidhurvidhuṃ bhūbhā chādayatyathā channakam //
1.54.d:
तेषां शिवघ्नाः शैलाप्ता व्यावर्काजः शराएङ्गुलैः ।
अर्कं विधुर्विधुं भूभा छादयत्यथा छन्नकम् ॥
1.54.m: Multiplied by eleven and divided by seven, they are the celestial latitude of the sun and moon in digits. / The moon covers the sun, and the earth's shadow covers the moon; then, the obscured portion [is calculated].

1.54.s:
chādyachādakamānārdhaṃ śaronaṃ grāhyavarjitam /
tatsvacchannaṃ ca mānaikyārddhāṃśaṣaṣṭaṃ daśāhatam //
1.54.d:
छाद्यछादकमानार्धं शरोनं ग्राह्यवर्जितम् ।
तत्स्वच्छन्नं च मानैक्यार्द्धांशषष्टं दशाहतम् ॥
1.54.m: Half the sum of the diameters of the eclipsed and eclipsing bodies, diminished by the latitude, is the obscured part; / that is the eclipsed portion; and one-sixtieth of half the sum of diameters multiplied by ten,

1.54.s:
channaghnamasmānmūlaṃ tu khāṅgonaglauvapurhṛtam /
sthityarddhaṃ ghaṭikādisyādvyaṅgabāhvaṃśasaṃmitaiḥ //
1.54.d:
छन्नघ्नमस्मान्मूलं तु खाङ्गोनग्लौवपुर्हृतम् ।
स्थित्यर्द्धं घटिकादिस्याद्व्यङ्गबाह्वंशसंमितैः ॥
1.54.m: multiplied by the obscured part—the square root of this, divided by the moon's diameter diminished by sixty, / yields the half-duration in ghaṭikās and so on, by degrees corresponding to the arm devoid of limbs.

1.54.s:
iṣṭaiḥ palaistadūnāḍhyaṃ vyagāvūner'kaṣaṅguṇaḥ /
tadanyathādhike tasminnevaṃ spaṣṭe sukhāntyage //
1.54.d:
इष्टैः पलैस्तदूनाढ्यं व्यगावूनेर्ऽकषङ्गुणः ।
तदन्यथाधिके तस्मिन्नेवं स्पष्टे सुखान्त्यगे ॥
1.54.m: Diminished or increased by that according to the desired minutes, if less than seventy, the sun is multiplied by six; / otherwise, when it is greater, the beginning and end [of the eclipse] are thus made clear.

1.54.s:
grāsena svāhate cchādyamānāme syurviśopakāḥ /
pūrṇāntaṃ madhyamatra syāddarśānteñjaṃ tribhonakam //
1.54.d:
ग्रासेन स्वाहते च्छाद्यमानामे स्युर्विशोपकाः ।
पूर्णान्तं मध्यमत्र स्याद्दर्शान्तेञ्जं त्रिभोनकम् ॥
1.54.m: When the obscured part is multiplied by its own [diameter] and divided by the diameter of the eclipsed body, the viśopakas are obtained; / the end of the full moon is the middle here; at the new moon, [one takes] the ecliptic point devoid of three signs.

1.54.s:
pṛthak tatkrāntyakṣabhāgasaṃskṛtau syurnatāṃśakāḥ /
taddighnāṃśakṛtidvyūnārddhārkayutā hariḥ //
1.54.d:
पृथक् तत्क्रान्त्यक्षभागसंस्कृतौ स्युर्नतांशकाः ।
तद्दिघ्नांशकृतिद्व्यूनार्द्धार्कयुता हरिः ॥
1.54.m: Adjusted separately by the degrees of declination and latitude, they become the zenith-distance degrees; / their square multiplied by two, minus two, halved, and joined to twelve, is the divisor.

1.54.s:
tribhānāṅgārkaviśleṣāṃśo ḥṃśonaghnāḥ /
purandarāḥ
harāptālaṃbanaṃ svarṇavitribherkādhikonake //
1.54.d:
त्रिभानाङ्गार्कविश्लेषांशो ःंशोनघ्नाः ।
पुरन्दराः
हराप्तालंबनं स्वर्णवित्रिभेर्काधिकोनके ॥
1.54.m: The degrees of the difference between the sun and the point ninety degrees from the ascendant, multiplied by fourteen / and divided by the divisor, give the parallax in longitude, additive or subtractive when the sun is less or greater than that point.

1.54.s:
viśvaghnalaṃbanakalāḍhyonastu tithivadyaguḥ /
śaronolaṃbanaṣaḍaghne tallavāḍhyonavitribhāt //
1.54.d:
विश्वघ्नलंबनकलाढ्योनस्तु तिथिवद्यगुः ।
शरोनोलंबनषडघ्ने तल्लवाढ्योनवित्रिभात् ॥
1.54.m: The parallax minutes multiplied by thirteen are added or subtracted as for a lunar day; / diminished by the latitude and multiplied by six, increased or diminished by those parts from the nonagesimal,

1.54.s:
natāṃśāstajāṃsāne prādhṛtastadvivarjita /
śabdenduliptaiḥ ṣaḍbhistu bhaktānatirnatirnatāṃśadik //
1.54.d:
नतांशास्तजांसाने प्राधृतस्तद्विवर्जित ।
शब्देन्दुलिप्तैः षड्भिस्तु भक्तानतिर्नतिर्नतांशदिक् ॥
1.54.m: the zenith-distance degrees in the direction of the zenith distance, subtracted from that, / divided by one hundred and six minutes, yield the parallax in latitude in the direction of the zenith distance.

1.54.s:
tayornāṭyohabhinnaikadik śaraḥ sphuṭatāṃ vrajet /
tataśchannasthitidale sādhye sthityarddhaṣaṭtribhiḥ //
1.54.d:
तयोर्नाट्योहभिन्नैकदिक् शरः स्फुटतां व्रजेत् ।
ततश्छन्नस्थितिदले साध्ये स्थित्यर्द्धषट्त्रिभिः ॥
1.54.m: When their directions are different or the same, the true celestial latitude is arrived at; / then the obscured portion and the half-duration are to be calculated by three-sixteenths of the half-duration.

1.54.s:
aṃśastairvintribhandvisthaṃlaṃbanetayoḥ pūrvavat /
saṃskṛtestābhyāṃ sthityarddhe bhavataḥ sphuṭe //
1.54.d:
अंशस्तैर्विन्त्रिभन्द्विस्थंलंबनेतयोः पूर्ववत् ।
संस्कृतेस्ताभ्यां स्थित्यर्द्धे भवतः स्फुटे ॥
1.54.m: With those degrees applied twice to the nonagesimal, parallax is calculated as before; / corrected by these two, the two half-durations become true.

1.54.s:
tābhyāṃ hīnayuto madhyadarśaḥ kālau mukhāntagau /
arkādyūnā viśva īśā navapañcadaśāṃśakāḥ //
1.54.d:
ताभ्यां हीनयुतो मध्यदर्शः कालौ मुखान्तगौ ।
अर्काद्यूना विश्व ईशा नवपञ्चदशांशकाः ॥
1.54.m: Diminished and increased by these two, the middle new-moon day yields the times of contact and separation. / Less by the sun and others, thirteen, eleven, nine, and fifteen degrees

1.54.s:
kālāṃśāstairūnayukte ravau hyastodayau vidhoḥ /
dṛṣṭvā hyādau kheṭabiṃbaṃ dṛgauñcye laṃbamīkṣya ca //
1.54.d:
कालांशास्तैरूनयुक्ते रवौ ह्यस्तोदयौ विधोः ।
दृष्ट्वा ह्यादौ खेटबिंबं दृगौञ्च्ये लंबमीक्ष्य च ॥
1.54.m: are the time-degrees; when the sun is diminished or increased by them, the setting and rising of the moon occur. / Having first observed the disk of the planet and observed its vertical plumb-line at the altitude,

1.54.s:
talluṃbapāpabiṃbāntardṛṇau vyāptaravighnabhāḥ /
aste sāvayavā jñeyā gataiṣyāstithayo budhaiḥ //
1.54.d:
तल्लुंबपापबिंबान्तर्दृणौ व्याप्तरविघ्नभाः ।
अस्ते सावयवा ज्ञेया गतैष्यास्तिथयो बुधैः ॥
1.54.m: the line of sight between that plumb and the disk covers the ray-shadows; / at sunset, the elapsed and future tithis with their fractional parts should be known by the wise.

1.54.s:
vyaste yuktāntibhāgaiśca dvighnatithyāhṛtā sphuṭam /
saṃskāradikalaṃbanamaṅgulādyaṃ prajāyate //
1.54.d:
व्यस्ते युक्तान्तिभागैश्च द्विघ्नतिथ्याहृता स्फुटम् ।
संस्कारदिकलंबनमङ्गुलाद्यं प्रजायते ॥
1.54.m: Taken inversely and combined with the end-portions, clearly divided by twice the tithi, / the deflection, parallax, and so forth in digits and so on are produced from the calculation.

1.54.s:
seṣvaśonāḥ sitaṃ tithyo balannāśonnataṃ vidhoḥ /
śṛṅgamanyatra udvācyaṃ balanāṅgulalekhanāt //
1.54.d:
सेष्वशोनाः सितं तिथ्यो बलन्नाशोन्नतं विधोः ।
शृङ्गमन्यत्र उद्वाच्यं बलनाङ्गुललेखनात् ॥
1.54.m: Diminished by the fifth part, the illuminated portion of the moon is elevated by the force of the deflection; / the cusps are to be described otherwise by drawing the deflection digits.

1.54.s:
pañcatve goṅkaviśikhāḥ śeṣakarṇahatāḥ pṛthak /
vikṛjyakāṅgasiddhāgnibhaktālabdhonasaṃyutāḥ //
1.54.d:
पञ्चत्वे गोङ्कविशिखाः शेषकर्णहताः पृथक् ।
विकृज्यकाङ्गसिद्धाग्निभक्तालब्धोनसंयुताः ॥
1.54.m: In the case of the five [planets], nine, nine, and five, multiplied separately by the remaining hypotenuse / and divided by three hundred sixty-six, the results are subtracted or added.

1.54.s:
trijyādhikone śravaṇe vapūṃṣi syurhṛtāḥ kujāt /
ṛjvoranṛjvorvivaraṃ gatyantaravibhājitam //
1.54.d:
त्रिज्याधिकोने श्रवणे वपूंषि स्युर्हृताः कुजात् ।
ऋज्वोरनृज्वोर्विवरं गत्यन्तरविभाजितम् ॥
1.54.m: When the hypotenuse is greater or less than the trijyā, the sizes [of the planets] from Mars onward are derived. / The difference between two direct or two retrograde [planets], divided by the difference of their daily motions,

1.54.s:
vakrartvorgatiyogāmaṃ gamyetīte dinādikam /
khanatyāsaṃskṛtauvveṣūdaksāmyenyentaraṃ yutiḥ //
1.54.d:
वक्रर्त्वोर्गतियोगामं गम्येतीते दिनादिकम् ।
खनत्यासंस्कृतौव्वेषूदक्साम्येन्येन्तरं युतिः ॥
1.54.m: or [divided by] the sum of the motions of a retrograde and a direct one, gives the days and so forth to come or past [at conjunction]. / Adjusted by the parallax in latitude, the difference is taken if their celestial latitudes are in the same direction, and the sum otherwise.

1.54.s:
yāmyodakkheṭavivaraṃ mānaukyāddholpakaṃ yadā /
yadā bhedolaṃbanādyaṃ sphuṭārthaṃ sūryaparvavat //
1.54.d:
याम्योदक्खेटविवरं मानौक्याद्धोल्पकं यदा ।
यदा भेदोलंबनाद्यं स्फुटार्थं सूर्यपर्ववत् ॥
1.54.m: When the north-south distance of two planets is less than half the sum of their diameters, / then there is an occultation; parallax and so forth are [computed] for true results as in a solar eclipse.

1.54.s:
ekāyanagatau syātāṃ sūryācandramasau yadā /
tayute maṇḍale krāntyau tulyatve vai dhṛtābhidhaḥ //
1.54.d:
एकायनगतौ स्यातां सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ यदा ।
तयुते मण्डले क्रान्त्यौ तुल्यत्वे वै धृताभिधः ॥
1.54.m: When the sun and the moon move in the same solstitial half-cycle, / and their declinations in that combined circle are equal, [the aspect] is called dhṛta (vaidhṛta).

1.54.s:
vipaṭītāyanagatau candrākārai krāntiliptikāḥ /
samāstadā vyatīpāto bhagaṇārddhe tapoyutau //
1.54.d:
विपटीतायनगतौ चन्द्राकारै क्रान्तिलिप्तिकाः ।
समास्तदा व्यतीपातो भगणार्द्धे तपोयुतौ ॥
1.54.m: When the Moon and the Sun are moving in opposite solstices, and their minutes of declination / are equal, then it is vyatīpāta, when the sum of their longitudes is half a revolution [six signs].

1.54.s:
bhāskaredvor bhacakrānta cakrārddhāvadhisaṃsthayoḥ /
dṛkkalpasādhitāṃśādiyuktayoḥ svāvapakramau //
1.54.d:
भास्करेद्वोर् भचक्रान्त चक्रार्द्धावधिसंस्थयोः ।
दृक्कल्पसाधितांशादियुक्तयोः स्वावपक्रमौ ॥
1.54.m: When the Sun and the Moon are situated near the ends of the zodiacal circle or half-circle, / endowed with the degrees and so on calculated through observation, their respective declinations [are obtained].

1.54.s:
athojapadagamyendoḥ krāntirvikṣepasaṃskṛtāḥ /
yadi syādadhikā bhānoḥ krānteḥ pāto gatastadā //
1.54.d:
अथोजपदगम्येन्दोः क्रान्तिर्विक्षेपसंस्कृताः ।
यदि स्यादधिका भानोः क्रान्तेः पातो गतस्तदा ॥
1.54.m: Now, if the Moon's declination, corrected by celestial latitude, in an odd quadrant, / should be greater than the Sun's declination, then the pāta is already past.

1.54.s:
nyūnā cetsyāttadā bhāvī vāmaṃ yugmapadasya ca /
yadānyatvaṃ vidhoḥ krāntiḥ kṣepāccedyadi śuddhyati //
1.54.d:
न्यूना चेत्स्यात्तदा भावी वामं युग्मपदस्य च ।
यदान्यत्वं विधोः क्रान्तिः क्षेपाच्चेद्यदि शुद्ध्यति ॥
1.54.m: If it should be less, then it is yet to occur; and the reverse is true for an even quadrant. / When there is a difference, if the declination of the Moon is subtracted from the latitude,

1.54.s:
krāntyorjetrijyayābhiste paramāyakramoddhate /
taccāpāntarmarddhavāyorjyabhāvinaśītagau //
1.54.d:
क्रान्त्योर्जेत्रिज्ययाभिस्ते परमायक्रमोद्धते ।
तच्चापान्तर्मर्द्धवायोर्ज्यभाविनशीतगौ ॥
1.54.m: multiplied by the sine of the radius, and divided by the maximum declination, / the arc between them [is obtained], and the sine is applied to the Moon that is yet to occur.

1.54.s:
śodhyaṃ candrādgate pāte tatsūyagatitāḍitam /
candrabhuktyā hṛtaṃ bhānau liptādiśaśivatphalam //
1.54.d:
शोध्यं चन्द्राद्गते पाते तत्सूयगतिताडितम् ।
चन्द्रभुक्त्या हृतं भानौ लिप्तादिशशिवत्फलम् ॥
1.54.m: When the pāta is past, it is to be subtracted from the Moon; multiplied by the Sun's motion / and divided by the Moon's daily motion, the result in minutes and so forth is applied to the Sun just like the Moon.

1.54.s:
tadūcchaśāṅkapātasya phalaṃ deyaṃ viparyayāt /
karmaitadasakṛttāvatkrāntī yāvatsametayoḥ //
1.54.d:
तदूच्छशाङ्कपातस्य फलं देयं विपर्ययात् ।
कर्मैतदसकृत्तावत्क्रान्ती यावत्समेतयोः ॥
1.54.m: The result of the Moon's node is to be applied inversely. / This operation is repeated until the declinations of both become equal.

1.54.s:
krāntyoḥ samatve pāto 'tha prakṣiptāṃśonite vidhau /
hīner'dvarātraghikāghato bhāvī tātkālike 'dhikā //
1.54.d:
क्रान्त्योः समत्वे पातो ऽथ प्रक्षिप्तांशोनिते विधौ ।
हीनेर्ऽद्वरात्रघिकाघतो भावी तात्कालिके ऽधिका ॥
1.54.m: When their declinations are equal, the pāta occurs. Now, when the Moon is diminished by the projected degrees, / if less, the pāta occurred before midnight; if greater, it will occur at that current time.

1.54.s:
sthirīkṛtārddharā trārddhau dvayorvivaraliptakāḥ /
ṣaṣṭiścācandrabhuktāptā pātakālasya nāḍikāḥ //
1.54.d:
स्थिरीकृतार्द्धरा त्रार्द्धौ द्वयोर्विवरलिप्तकाः ।
षष्टिश्चाचन्द्रभुक्ताप्ता पातकालस्य नाडिकाः ॥
1.54.m: Taking the fixed half of midnight, the minutes of difference between the two, / multiplied by sixty and divided by the Moon's daily motion, are the nāḍikās of the time of the pāta.

1.54.s:
ravīndvormānayogārddhaṃ ṣaṣṭyā saṃguṇya bhājayet /
tayorbhuktayantareṇāptaṃ sthityamarddhāṃ nāḍikādivat //
1.54.d:
रवीन्द्वोर्मानयोगार्द्धं षष्ट्या संगुण्य भाजयेत् ।
तयोर्भुक्तयन्तरेणाप्तं स्थित्यमर्द्धां नाडिकादिवत् ॥
1.54.m: One should multiply half the sum of the diameters of the Sun and the Moon by sixty and divide / by the difference of their daily motions; the result gives half the duration in nāḍikās and so on.

1.54.s:
pātakālaḥ sphuṭo madhyaḥ so 'pi sthityarddhavarjitaḥ /
tasya saṃbhavakālaḥ syāttatsaṃyogektasaṃjñakaḥ //
1.54.d:
पातकालः स्फुटो मध्यः सो ऽपि स्थित्यर्द्धवर्जितः ।
तस्य संभवकालः स्यात्तत्संयोगेक्तसंज्ञकः ॥
1.54.m: The precise middle time of the pāta, minus half the duration, / is its beginning time, and combined with it, it is known as the end.

1.54.s:
ādyantakālayormadhye kālo jñeyo 'tidāruṇaḥ /
prajvalajjvalanākāraḥ sarvakarmasu garhitaḥ //
1.54.d:
आद्यन्तकालयोर्मध्ये कालो ज्ञेयो ऽतिदारुणः ।
प्रज्वलज्ज्वलनाकारः सर्वकर्मसु गर्हितः ॥
1.54.m: The time between the beginning and the end is to be known as exceedingly dreadful, / having the appearance of a blazing fire, and condemned in all rites.

1.54.s:
ityetadgaṇito kiñcitproktaṃ saṃkṣepato dvija /
jātakaṃ vācmi samayādrāśisaṃjñāpuraḥsaram //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde jyotiṣavarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.54.d:
इत्येतद्गणितो किञ्चित्प्रोक्तं संक्षेपतो द्विज ।
जातकं वाच्मि समयाद्राशिसंज्ञापुरःसरम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे ज्योतिषवर्णनं नाम चतुःपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.54.m:
Thus, O twice-born one, a little of mathematical astronomy has been stated in brief. / I shall now explain horoscopy (jātaka) according to time, beginning with the designations of the zodiacal signs.

Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, named Description of Jyotiṣa, in the second quarter of the Bṛhad-upākhyāna in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
